text:
Why River Cruises Are One of the Easiest and Most Rewarding Ways to Travel
For travelers who want to see multiple destinations without the hassle of constantly packing, unpacking, navigating unfamiliar roads, or changing hotels, river cruising offers a uniquely relaxed and enriching vacation experience. Whether compared with traditional land tours or large ocean cruises, river cruises provide an exceptional combination of comfort, convenience, culture, and personalized service.
Unpack Once and Let the World Come to You
One of the greatest advantages of a river cruise is simplicity. Unlike a land-based vacation where you may change hotels several times, river cruises allow you to unpack once and settle into your stateroom for the entire journey.
Your floating hotel travels with you, carrying you from one fascinating destination to the next. There is no need to haul luggage through airports, train stations, or hotel lobbies. Each morning, you wake up in a new destination while your room, dining venues, and familiar surroundings remain the same.
A More Intimate Experience
River cruise ships are significantly smaller than ocean cruise vessels. Most accommodate fewer than 200 guests, creating a comfortable, boutique atmosphere and allowing access to ports and waterways that larger ships simply cannot reach.
The smaller size offers several advantages:
Less crowded public spaces
Shorter boarding and disembarkation times
Quicker excursion departures
Easier socializing with fellow travelers
A quieter, more relaxed onboard environment
Many guests find they quickly become acquainted with fellow travelers and crew members, creating a warm and welcoming atmosphere that is difficult to replicate on larger ships.
Exceptional Service
Because river cruise ships carry fewer passengers, they typically provide a higher crew-to-guest ratio than many traditional vacation experiences. Crew members often learn guests' preferences within the first day or two, whether it's a favorite beverage, dining preference, or seating location.
This attentive service contributes to a highly personalized vacation where guests feel recognized and valued throughout the journey.
Dock in the Heart of the Action
Perhaps the most unique advantage of river cruising is location.
Unlike many ocean cruise ports that can be miles from city centers, river cruise ships frequently dock directly in the heart of historic cities and towns. Travelers can step off the ship and immediately begin exploring.
Imagine:
Walking into the center of Vienna from your ship
Strolling through medieval towns along the Rhine
Exploring Budapest's historic districts within minutes
Beginning a Paris excursion with views near the Eiffel Tower and other iconic landmarks along the Seine
Rather than spending valuable vacation time on lengthy motorcoach transfers, travelers are immersed in their destination almost immediately.
Destination-Focused Cuisine
Dining is a highlight aboard most river cruises. Menus frequently incorporate regional specialties and local ingredients from the destinations visited along the itinerary.
Guests might enjoy:
French cuisine while sailing the Seine
German specialties along the Rhine
Austrian pastries on the Danube
Portuguese wines on the Douro
Cajun and Creole dishes on American river itineraries
Many cruise lines also feature local wines, cultural presentations, cooking demonstrations, and tasting events that bring the destination's culinary traditions to life.
Learning While You Travel
River cruises are often described as "floating cultural journeys."
Many itineraries include:
Local historians and guest lecturers
Cultural demonstrations
Language lessons
Wine tastings
Cooking presentations
Regional music and entertainment
These enrichment opportunities provide deeper insight into the history, culture, art, and traditions of each destination.
Included Excursions
Most river cruise fares include guided shore excursions at every port.
Common excursion options include:
Walking tours
Castle visits
Museum tours
Wine tastings
Bicycle excursions
Market visits
Architectural tours
Food-focused experiences
Many cruise lines now offer multiple activity levels, allowing guests to choose active, moderate, or leisurely experiences.
Scenic Travel at Its Best
Unlike ocean cruising, where days may pass without seeing land, river cruising offers constantly changing scenery.
Passengers enjoy:
Vineyards cascading down hillsides
Ancient castles
Charming villages
Historic city skylines
Rolling countryside
Riverfront cafés and promenades
The journey itself becomes a central part of the vacation experience.
Comparing River Cruises to Other Vacation Styles
River Cruises vs. Land Tours
River Cruises Offer:
One unpacking
No hotel changes
Fewer bus rides
Easier logistics
Consistent accommodations
Included dining and excursions
River Cruises vs. Ocean Cruises
River Cruises Offer:
Smaller ships
More personalized service
Fewer passengers
City-center docking
More cultural immersion
Greater destination focus
Ocean cruises often emphasize onboard entertainment and resort-style amenities, while river cruises focus on history, culture, cuisine, and destination experiences.
Major International River Cruise Lines
Some of the world's leading river cruise operators include:
Viking River Cruises
AmaWaterways
Avalon Waterways
Tauck River Cruising
These companies operate itineraries on Europe's most famous rivers, including the Rhine, Danube, Seine, Rhône, Douro, and others, as well as selected sailings in Asia, Africa, and South America.
Major River Cruise Lines in the United States
The leading operators in the U.S. market include:
American Cruise Lines
Viking
American Cruise Lines is among the largest dedicated U.S. river cruise companies operating on the Mississippi River, Columbia and Snake Rivers, and numerous coastal waterways.
Typical Amenities Found on River Cruises
Most modern river cruise ships feature:
Elegant staterooms and suites
Fine dining restaurants
Complimentary Wi-Fi
Lounge and observation areas
Fitness centers
Sun decks
Specialty dining experiences
Local wine and beer selections
Educational programs
Included sightseeing excursions
Bicycle fleets on many ships
Airport transfers on select itineraries
Luxury river cruise lines may also include butler service, premium beverages, gratuities, and exclusive shore experiences.
When Should You Book?
Because river ships are small and carry relatively few passengers, popular sailings often sell out well in advance.
A good rule of thumb is:
12 to 18 months ahead for popular European cruises, holiday markets, tulip season, and prime summer departures
9 to 12 months ahead for most itineraries
18 months or more ahead for suites and specialty departures
Early booking also typically provides the best selection of cabins, preferred sailing dates, and promotional pricing.
The Bottom Line
River cruising combines the convenience of an all-inclusive vacation, the comfort of a boutique hotel, and the cultural depth of an immersive land tour. With only one unpacking, attentive service, city-center docking, destination-inspired cuisine, and enriching experiences throughout the journey, it's one of the most relaxing and rewarding ways to explore the world. For travelers seeking a seamless blend of comfort, culture, and convenience, a river cruise may be the perfect voyage.

Yen Breaks 160 | August 31, 2026
(📍Data From https://t.co/rtKhA53pFF Daily Report)

USD/JPY has broken above 160 again, placing Japanese authorities back on intervention watch only one month after their largest-ever operation.

Japan spent ¥15.4T—approximately $96.5B—supporting the yen between July 30 and August 26. The operation, which included rare coordination with the United States and South Korea, initially pushed USD/JPY from nearly 164 toward 155.

More than half that move has already been reversed.

The lesson is uncomfortable:

Intervention can create a violent correction. It cannot permanently erase the interest-rate differential.

Three zones now matter.

160–161: Warning zone

This level attracts political attention, but it may not trigger immediate action. Officials consistently emphasize the speed and disorderliness of currency moves rather than a fixed exchange rate.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recently described the yen’s decline as “pretty well contained,” suggesting Washington does not yet see the conditions required for another coordinated operation.

Above 162: Intervention risk becomes real

A rapid move through 162 would increase the probability of verbal warnings, rate checks and direct yen purchases.

The 162.9–163.3 area deserves particular attention because it overlaps with levels surrounding the previous intervention. However, the authorities deliberately preserved surprise last time, so traders should not treat this range as an official barrier.

Near 164: Credibility test

A return toward July’s 40-year low of 163.99 would imply that a record intervention had failed to change the trend.

At that point, Japan may need more than currency purchases. The pressure would intensify for a Bank of Japan hike, faster tightening guidance or another coordinated operation involving the US.

Markets currently assign approximately an 80% probability to a September BOJ hike, although intraday pricing varies. That creates another problem: much of the tightening support for the yen is already priced in.

For intervention to produce a lasting reversal, at least one fundamental driver must change:

• US yields must fall.
• The Fed must become less hawkish.
• The BOJ must tighten more aggressively than expected.
• Japanese capital must begin returning home.

Without one of those shifts, intervention may simply offer leveraged dollar buyers a lower re-entry level.
Cross-asset implications
A sudden yen intervention could lift Japanese government bonds, pressure export-heavy Japanese equities and force carry-trade deleveraging across global risk assets.
The biggest danger is therefore not a slow move from 160 to 161. It is a rapid intervention-driven reversal that catches crowded yen shorts and leveraged carry positions simultaneously.

Trader’s takeaway: monitor the velocity of USD/JPY, one-week implied volatility, risk reversals and official rate-check headlines—not just the spot level.

Japan has enough reserves to shock the market again.

But unless the rate gap narrows, it is still fighting the tide with increasingly expensive ammunition.

Dear members of the American press!

Steve Jobs once said, "If you can convince the press of your technology, and the press convinces us, we'll pay attention."

That's why I'm reaching out to you.

For years, the development of personal devices has been driven by advances in smartphones, tablets, and virtual reality technologies. However, all of these solutions still require people to adapt to the device. I've developed a concept based on the opposite principle: the device should adapt to the user and interact with them as naturally as possible.

I believe this technology has the potential to be the next major step in the development of consumer electronics. It offers a fundamentally new way to interact with the digital environment and has the potential to replace many existing devices that accompany people in their daily lives today.

If my assessment is correct, this isn't just another gadget, but a platform capable of transforming the market in the same way that the personal computer, iPod, and iPhone once did. Such opportunities arise extremely rarely, and that's why they deserve independent attention and objective assessment.

I believe Apple has the experience, engineering culture, and vision necessary to turn this idea into a world-class product. Moreover, the successful implementation of such technology could strengthen the leadership of the American tech industry at a time when global competition is becoming increasingly fierce.

I'm not asking you to take my word for it. I'm asking only one thing: help draw Apple's attention to this development and give it the opportunity to be considered by those capable of objectively assessing its potential.

If the technology truly represents the value I see in it, ignoring it could be a missed opportunity. If not, that will become clear after a professional evaluation. But in either case, the idea deserves to be heard.

Thank you for your attention.

Sincerely,

Alexander.

text:
Let's talk to the embedded systems engineer who didn't get into this for passion

You got into it for the money

You have the skills now

Here's a more realistic path to actually making that money, without the sugar-coated advice you'll find everywhere else

1. Freelancing is not a quick fix, so treat it as a long game

Upwork specifically is trial and error sometimes.

You'll spend money on Connects, submit proposals, and hear nothing back more times than you'd like

That's the reality, not the exception

Instead, use freelancing as a slow-burn income stream you build alongside something more stable

Not your primary plan from day one

Start small, get your first review, then let each project make the next one easier to land

2. Price around outcomes once you have that first review

Before you have proof, hourly rates protect you

After you have 2-3 completed projects, shift toward fixed pricing tied to deliverables

Don't rush this. Reviews and trust come first.

3. Be realistic about local demand, especially in Nigeria

IoT and embedded contracts are not as available locally as international freelance platforms make it seem

Most consistent paying work here tends to come from companies needing embedded engineers on salary, not freelance IoT gigs

If you're based in Nigeria, prioritize applying to companies directly

Local tech companies, hardware startups, and international companies hiring remote embedded talent

Freelance IoT contracts are the exception, not the reliable plan

4. One strong portfolio project beats ten weak ones

This part holds regardless of freelance or full-time

A single well-documented project closes more opportunities than a scattered collection of half-finished ones

5. Stop competing on price only after you have real proof behind you

Not immediately. Not on your first project.

Build the track record first, then reposition

6. Document your work publicly, consistently

This remains one of the most realistic ways opportunities actually find you, whether that's a full-time offer, a referral, or a freelance client reaching out first

Making money from this skill is realistic

But it takes patience, a mix of income sources...

And honest expectations about what freelancing platforms can and can't guarantee, especially depending on where you're based

I'm rooting for you
You've got this 👑

text:
A 16-year-old girl asked for help in the rain. She was offered a lift. That supposed act of help allegedly turned into a horrific crime.

This is not merely another crime report. It is a shame on every institution entrusted with protecting children and a serious failure of both society and government.

• Strongest condemnation: There can be no excuse, justification or grey area when a child seeking safety becomes vulnerable to predators. Such brutality demands immediate and unequivocal condemnation.

• Society failed first: A schoolgirl stranded in darkness and rain should have found compassion and protection, not exploitation. When society looks away, remains silent or treats such horror as just another headline, it has already failed its daughters.

• Government must answer: Unsafe night travel, inadequate safeguards in public transport and weak last-mile security are not simply unfortunate accidents. They expose serious governance and safety gaps. A State that cannot provide reasonable safety to a child seeking help has failed one of its most basic responsibilities.

• Arrest is not justice: Justice means a swift, fair and transparent trial, protection of the survivor’s dignity and privacy, comprehensive support for her recovery, and meaningful accountability wherever institutional failure is established.

• The delay demands answers: If the incident occurred on 4 August but the public is learning about it only on 31 August, legitimate questions must be asked. Why the delay? Who knew what, and when? Were the required procedures followed? Was the survivor adequately protected?

• The public deserves accountability: These are not political questions. They are questions of governance, institutional responsibility and public safety.

• The fear of ordinary families: If a girl cannot trust public transport when she is alone, lost, frightened and seeking help, then every slogan about women’s safety rings hollow.

• No ideology can wash this away: No political party should exploit such a tragedy. No government should hide behind procedure. And no society should remain silent.

• The real test: A democracy is not judged merely by the values it proclaims, but by how firmly it protects its most vulnerable citizens.

Swift justice. Dignity and complete support for the survivor. Stronger safeguards in public transport. Transparent accountability.

Anything less is not justice. It is another institutional failure.

Deputy Minister of Transport Phattrapong Phattraprasit visited Satun province to assess the feasibility of establishing water takeoff and landing sites for seaplanes. The Minister was accompanied by Satun Deputy Governor Damrongsak Kaewduang, the President of the Satun Provincial Administrative Organization, and local transport officials. The visit is part of an official inspection tour covering Songkhla and Satun provinces from August 31 to September 1, 2026.

During the morning itinerary, the delegation surveyed the Pak Bara Pier area in La-ngu district before moving on to inspect Mu Ko Phetra National Park. The objective of evaluating these sites was to determine their potential to integrate seaplane operations and enhance connections between Satun’s coastal destinations and other marine tourism hubs along the Andaman coast.

The establishment of seaplane landing sites will require thorough evaluations regarding technical suitability, operational safety, and minimal disruption to existing maritime traffic. Authorities emphasized that full compliance with relevant regulations and strict protection of aquatic ecosystems are essential requirements for moving forward.

If deemed viable, seaplane services will offer a new travel alternative, improving convenience for tourists and elevating the overall tourism profile of Satun and the wider Andaman region.

Following the field inspections, the delegation scheduled an afternoon meeting at the Seesea Resort Pak Bara. The discussion aimed to analyze feasibility data, gather feedback from relevant agencies, and establish guidelines for potential next steps to introduce seaplane transportation to the area.

text:
Saint Raymund Nonnatus, Confessor from Lives of the Saints by Father Francis Xavier Weninger, DD, SJ., 1876.
.
Catalonia was the native country of Saint Raymund who, to the astonishment of the Physicians, was born after his mother’s death. As soon as he was old enough to comprehend how early he had become an orphan, he chose the Queen of Heaven as his mother, and to his last day, called her by no other name. When he had studied for some time with great success, his father, fearing the youth would enter a Religious Order, sent him into the country to take care of a farm. Raymund obeyed, and found there also opportunity to serve God. He became very fond of solitude and therefore chose for his occupation the care of the sheep, in order to gain more time for prayer and meditation. At the foot of the mountain to which he generally led his flock, was a small, deserted hermitage, with a chapel, in which an extremely lovely picture of the Blessed Virgin was kept, which was a source of great joy to him. He there spent several hours daily, in devout exercises. Other shepherds, who observed this, and to whom the piety of Raymund was a reproach of their own negligence, reported to his father that he was doing nothing but praying, and thereby neglected his flock. The father came to convince himself of the fact, but although he found his son praying in the chapel, he saw that the flock was meanwhile attended to by a youth of uncommon beauty of form and features. Asking his son who this young shepherd was, and why he had engaged him, Raymund, to whom it was unknown that Providence had worked a miracle in his behalf, fell on his knees before his father, and begging forgiveness, earnestly promised not to commit the fault again. The Divine Mother, of whom he begged the grace of knowing his vocation, appeared to him, saying that she desired him to take the habit of the newly established Order for the redemption of captives. He did so, and was sent to Algiers where he found a great many Christians in slavery, and as the money he had brought for their ransom was not sufficient, he offered himself as a hostage to redeem the others. He was induced to this by the danger in which the prisoners were of losing their faith and with it eternal life. This great and heroic charity gave him occasion to suffer much for the sake of Christ. At first, he was treated very harshly by his masters, but when they began to fear that he would die before the ransom was paid, they allowed him more liberty, which the holy man used only for the salvation of the captive Christians. He strengthened them in their faith, and, at the same time, endeavored to convert the infidels. Accused of this before the Judge, he was condemned to be impaled alive, and nothing but the hope of a large ransom prevented the execution of this barbarous sentence, and caused it to be changed into a cruel bastinado. Raymund, who desired nothing more fervently than to die for Christ’s sake, was not intimidated by what he had undergone, but wherever an opportunity offered itself, he explained to the infidels the word of God. The Judge, informed of it, ordered him to be whipped through all the streets of the city, and then to be brought to the market-place, where the executioner, with a red hot iron, pierced his lips, through which a small chain was drawn and closed with a padlock, in order that the holy man might no more use his tongue to instruct others. Every three days the lock was opened, and he received just enough food to keep him from starvation. Besides this, he was loaded with chains, and cast into a dungeon, where he lay for eight months, until his ransom arrived. Although it was the desire of the Saint to remain among the infidels, as he would there have an opportunity to gain the crown of martyrdom, obedience recalled him to his monastery.
.
When the Pope was informed of all that Raymund had suffered during his captivity, he nominated him Cardinal; but the humble Saint returned to his convent and lived like all the other brothers of the Order, without making the least change in his dress, food, or dwelling, nor accepting any honor due to him as so high a dignitary of the Church. Gregory IX, desired to have so holy a man near him, and called him to Rome. The Saint obeyed and set out on his journey. He had, however, scarcely reached Cardona, six miles from Barcelona, when he was seized with a malignant fever, which soon became fatal. He desired most fervently to receive the holy Sacraments, but as the priest called to administer them to him, delayed to come, God sent an angel, who brought him the divine food. After receiving it, he returned thanks to God for all the graces he had received from Him during his life, and peacefully gave up his soul, in the 37th year of his age. After his death, the inhabitants of Cardona, the clergy of Barcelona and the religious of his order, contended as to where the holy body should be buried. Each party thought they had the greatest claim to possess his tomb. At last they resolved to leave the decision to Providence. They placed the coffin, in which the holy body reposed, upon a blind mule, determined that the treasure should be deposited in the place to which this animal should carry it. The mule, accompanied by a large concourse of people, went on until it had reached the hermitage and chapel where the holy cardinal, as a shepherd boy, had spent so many hours in prayer, and had received so many graces from God. There the Saint was buried, and Saint Peter Nolasco, in the course of time, founded there a Convent, with a Church in which the holy remains are still preserved and greatly honored by the people of Catalonia.
.
Practical Considerations
.
1. Saint Raymund instructed the faithful and the infidels; and to prevent him from this, his enemies most barbarously closed his mouth with a lock. Oh! how much more just it would be, if such a lock were suspended from your mouth, which you open so frequently to lie, to curse, to blaspheme, to quarrel, to calumniate, to make impure speeches, to sing impure songs, and to talk frivolously in Churches. But believe me, if your mouth is not punished in this world, it will most surely suffer in the next, and as the mouth of Saint Raymund, which he used so nobly, and in which he suffered so cruelly, will be specially rewarded in the abode of the angels, so will your wicked mouth be specially punished in the dwelling of the evil spirits. Saint Gregory believes that the rich man suffers special pains in his tongue, because he used it at table for indecent speeches, as is yet today the habit of many. The same punishment awaits your tongue, your sinful mouth; and if you wish to escape it, be careful how you use them. Place the fear of God as a guard over them, that they may not utter a word offensive to the Most High. “Hedge in thine ears with thorns, hear not a wicked tongue, and make doors and bars to thy mouth.” (Eccles. 28)
.
2. Saint Raymund, at the close of his days, gave fervent thanks to the Almighty for all favors bestowed upon him, and thus ended his life full of heavenly comfort. To give thanks to God is a duty which we ought to perform every morning and evening; for, no day, no night passes in which we, do not partake of the bounty of the Lord. You thank men who bestow kindness upon you; why then do you not thank God who has overwhelmed you with favors, and still grants them to you daily. Do not forget your duty, but attend to it every day. Give thanks to Him also at the end of each month, in consideration of so many benefits which you have received from Him and for which you did not even ask. Whom have you to thank that you did not die during the past four weeks; that you have dot been condemned to eternal flames, as so many that have been called away? Whence comes it that you were preserved from the dangers and misfortunes that befell so many others? that time and opportunity are left you to work out your salvation, whilst thousands no longer possess them? Most assuredly, these are all benefits of the Almighty which you deserve much less than a great many others. Is it not just that you should give fervent thanks to God at the end of each month? But is your soul in such a condition that you can end this month or close your life, as peacefully as Saint Raymund? Ah! if you had lived as he did, if you had constantly practiced good works, and had borne adversity with his patience, you might be comforted now, as well as at the end of your days. As, however, this is unhappily not the case, repent of your wickedness and indolence with your whole heart, and pray humbly for grace to make better use of the next month. Endeavor to atone, during the same, for your past negligence, that, one day you may not sigh uselessly: “I have had empty months.” (Job viii “Who will grant me that I might be according to the months past” (Job 29)

text:
Manusmriti, Women’s Freedom & the Constitutional India

The image refers to S.N. Sahu’s recent The Wire article, “In Rahul’s Attack on Manusmriti Resonates the Vision of Mahatma Gandhi and Ambedkar.” The article argues that Rahul Gandhi’s criticism of Manusmriti’s prescriptions concerning women echoes important aspects of both Gandhi’s and Ambedkar’s critiques of traditional social hierarchy. 

The question is not whether a text is ancient.
The question is whether the values it prescribes are compatible with human dignity today.

Rahul Gandhi’s recent criticism of Manusmriti focuses on its prescriptions that women remain dependent on their fathers in childhood, husbands in youth and sons in old age. His argument is that a woman's relationships with her family should never erase her independent identity, agency and freedom. 

That criticism has historical precedent.

In a 1918 speech, Mahatma Gandhi himself criticised prescriptions in the Smritis that subordinated women, arguing for women's equal mental capacity, freedom and independent sphere of activity. He explicitly rejected the idea that religious tradition should be defended merely because it is tradition. 

And B.R. Ambedkar's critique was considerably more radical. His 1950 essay The Rise and Fall of the Hindu Woman examined the historical subordination of women and criticised Manu for turning ideas of female dependence into normative social rules. Ambedkar had also publicly burnt Manusmriti in 1927 as a symbol of the caste and social inequalities against which he was fighting. 

So this debate should not be reduced to:

“Rahul Gandhi versus Hinduism.”

That is historically and intellectually far too simplistic.

The more meaningful question is:

Which values should determine the India of today—hierarchy and inherited status, or equality and individual liberty?

A person can respect Hindu traditions while critically examining texts and practices within that tradition.

A person can be religious and still reject patriarchy.

A person can value cultural heritage while insisting that no scripture, custom or ideology can override the constitutional equality of citizens.

That is precisely where Gandhi and Ambedkar offer an important lesson: tradition is not beyond criticism simply because it is tradition.

And there is an important distinction worth preserving.

Criticising Manusmriti is not the same as insulting Hindus.

Likewise, defending women's equality does not require hatred of religion.

The standard should be universal:

If an idea denies women autonomy → challenge it.
If an idea entrenches caste hierarchy → challenge it.
If an idea denies human dignity → challenge it.
If an idea supports equality and freedom → defend it.

The Constitution gives us that common framework.

India's future cannot be built by asking women to remain subordinate to inherited social identities. It must be built around liberty, equality, dignity, fraternity and equal citizenship.

We don't have to choose between culture and justice.
We have to choose justice when culture is used to justify inequality.

And that is why the conversation around Manusmriti matters—not as an attack on anyone's faith, but as a question about what kind of society we want to build.

Women are not someone's property.
Women are not extensions of fathers, husbands or sons.
They are citizens, individuals and complete human beings.

Constitution before hierarchy.
Equality before inherited privilege.
Human dignity before patriarchy.

text:
Pray for Our Nation: New Jersey
Lord of gardens, rivers, and living liberty, we come before You for New Jersey — a land of farms and pine woods, busy cities and a long bright shore, a people formed at the crossing of many roads. Thank You for civil and religious liberty so long enjoyed, for neighbors who still open their doors, and for churches and quiet ministries that feed the hungry, shelter the weary, and lift the fallen.

Teach this people to hold liberty with clean hands, and to seek a prosperity that does not forget the poor. Provide a home for families pressed by the cost of shelter. Restore those bound by addiction. Guard the shore and all who dwell along it. Give wisdom to those who lead, compassion to those who serve, and courage to those who labor in crowded streets and forgotten towns.

Where faith has grown thin, awaken a living hunger for You. Let true religion and civil liberty remain inseparable. Transmit the blessing of worship freely offered to the children yet unborn. Comfort the brokenhearted. Keep this Garden State under Your holy protection, and let its people walk in justice, mercy, and hope. Amen.

text:
Operation Denver started in 1983. The KGB planted a story in an Indian newspaper claiming the U.S. Army had engineered HIV/AIDS at Fort Detrick. Over the next several years, that story migrated through Soviet-friendly outlets, got picked up by Western fringe press, and eventually required direct diplomatic intervention to counter. It took years. It cost real credibility. And the people who designed it understood something that a lot of counter-disinformation policy still hasn't fully absorbed: you don't need to make people believe your lie. You just need them to be less certain about the truth.

A theoretical framework out of City University London has now mapped that intuition into a formal psychological architecture, and it's worth sitting with because it explains why so much of what we call "disinformation response" keeps swinging at the wrong target.

The researchers identify three distinct campaign types, each exploiting a different cognitive vulnerability. They're not interchangeable. They don't respond to the same countermeasures. Treating them as a single phenomenon called "disinformation" is roughly equivalent to treating pneumonia, a broken leg, and arsenic poisoning as "feeling bad."

The first type is identity-grievance operations. This is the one that got the most attention after 2016, and for good reason. The Internet Research Agency's work targeting American audiences, documented exhaustively by the Senate Intelligence Committee and confirmed through State Department reporting, represents the modern template. Black Lives Matter content, Blue Lives Matter content, evangelical Christian content, pro-gun content, all running simultaneously from the same St. Petersburg troll farm. The operational logic wasn't to invent racial or partisan tension in the United States. The tension was already there. The operation just found the fractures and hammered them.

The psychological mechanism here is in-group/out-group processing, which is not some exotic vulnerability. It's load-bearing architecture in how human cognition works. We are wired to sort, and we are wired to weight information differently depending on whether it comes from someone we perceive as "us" or "them." State actors running identity-grievance operations are essentially exploiting the same neural shortcuts that made tribal survival possible for 200,000 years. The sophistication isn't in the technology. It's in the targeting.

RAND's analysis of Russian disinformation documented this systematically, and the finding that keeps getting underplayed is the scale issue. The operations didn't create polarization. They amplified existing polarization. That distinction matters enormously for policy, because it means you cannot correct your way out of an identity-grievance campaign. The underlying grievances are real. The people receiving the amplified content aren't being tricked into caring about things they didn't already care about. They're being nudged toward more extreme expressions of things they genuinely feel.

The second campaign type, false attribution and false flag operations, is structurally different. Operation Denver is the historical archetype, but the contemporary versions are faster, cheaper, and far harder to attribute. The mechanism is misattribution: a real event, or a fabricated event, gets assigned to a convenient actor. CIA did this. The Ukrainian government did that. NATO is responsible for X. The psychological target is causal reasoning. Once you've successfully planted a false cause-effect chain, correcting it is genuinely difficult, partly because corrections require people to hold two versions of events in mind simultaneously and perform a comparison, which is cognitively expensive.

The good news, relatively speaking, is that false attribution campaigns are the most vulnerable to factual counter-pressure. Prebunking works here. Inoculation theory works here. If you can get ahead of the false attribution before it embeds, or if you can quickly produce credible authoritative counter-attribution, you can meaningfully blunt the operation. This is the terrain where the "disinformation response" playbook was largely developed, and it's where that playbook actually functions as designed.

The third type is where things get genuinely uncomfortable for standard counter-disinformation methodology.

Strategic ambiguity campaigns don't try to make you believe a specific false thing. They try to make you uncertain about whether true things are actually true. Russia's deployment of multiple simultaneous contradictory narratives around the MH17 shootdown is probably the clearest documented case. The plane was hit by a Ukrainian Buk. The plane was hit by a Ukrainian fighter jet. The plane wasn't hit from the ground at all. The photos of the Buk are fabricated. The investigation is NATO-controlled and therefore corrupt. None of these narratives needed to be believed. They just needed to exist, loudly, in enough information spaces that someone who wasn't already paying close attention would come away thinking "well, there are a lot of theories and it's complicated."

The RAND analysis describes this as collapsing epistemic foundations rather than substituting false beliefs for true ones. The target isn't your conclusion. It's your confidence in your ability to reach conclusions.

And here is where standard counter-disinformation response can actively make things worse. When authoritative sources respond to strategic ambiguity campaigns by carefully enumerating the competing narratives and then debunking them one by one, they are, by the act of enumeration, lending those narratives a kind of ontological legitimacy. You've now told your audience there are six competing theories, and you've explained each one. The audience that was already skeptical of authoritative sources doesn't walk away thinking "good, the authorities sorted it out." They walk away thinking "even the official response acknowledges there are six theories."

This is not a hypothetical failure mode. It has played out repeatedly in exactly this way, and the City University framework at least gives us a vocabulary for explaining why.

The platform exploitation mechanisms documented in the framework are by now fairly well catalogued: algorithmic amplification of high-engagement divisive content, coordinated inauthentic behavior networks manufacturing artificial consensus, bot networks inflating narrative velocity to create the impression of organic momentum, and cross-platform laundering where something starts on a fringe forum, gets picked up by a mid-tier partisan site, and eventually shows up in mainstream coverage as "a claim circulating online." The laundering pathway is the one that still gets too little attention in platform governance discussions, partly because it implicates mainstream media practices as much as fringe platform behavior.

The policy implication that falls out of the three-campaign architecture is fairly stark: there is no single intervention that addresses all three campaign types, and some interventions that work for one type are counterproductive for another. Factual correction is valuable against false attribution and relatively neutral against identity-grievance, but can amplify strategic ambiguity campaigns. Platform-level structural interventions reducing algorithmic promotion of divisive high-engagement content address the identity-grievance mechanism more effectively than the other two, but create their own legitimacy and censorship problems. Prebunking and inoculation address false attribution well but have limited purchase against strategic ambiguity, because you can't really prebunk "things might be uncertain."

Counter-disinformation as a field has, with some exceptions, operated as though all three campaign types are the same problem. The academic framework from City University doesn't offer a complete solution, and the researchers aren't claiming it does. What it offers is a diagnostic tool that might prevent us from repeatedly applying the wrong treatment to the wrong condition.

The KGB understood in 1983 that different operations serve different strategic purposes and require different operational designs. That's not a particularly advanced insight. It's been true about information warfare since before it was called that. The fact that it still needs to be restated in 2024 as a theoretical framework contribution says something about how slowly the defensive side of this has moved.

text:
SoftBank's SB Energy just offered OpenAI a $5.5 billion perk to lock it in as a data-center tenant. Here's what you need to know.

SB Energy is SoftBank's little-known data-center subsidiary, and it's now preparing to go public, targeting $5B to $7B in IPO proceeds as soon as this week.

To secure OpenAI as its anchor tenant, SB Energy issued OpenAI warrants that were worth $3.6 billion when granted in January 2026 and had risen to an estimated $5.5 billion by the end of June 2026. OpenAI is expected to hold a single-digit percentage stake in SB Energy after listing.

OpenAI also put $500 million into SB Energy, and SB Energy pledged at least $50 million toward OpenAI software through 2028. OpenAI signed a 20-year lease for a data center campus in Ohio, initially planned at up to 10 gigawatts, starting at 800 megawatts and scaling toward 8 gigawatts, coming online by 2028.

SB Energy's data-center unit doesn't generate revenue yet and has no operating data centers, but it claims a contracted backlog exceeding $400 billion, with tenants including SoftBank, OpenAI, and Nvidia.

Key numbers:
- $5.5 billion: estimated value of OpenAI's SB Energy warrants as of end of June 2026
- $3.6 billion: value of those warrants when issued in January 2026
- $400 billion: SB Energy's contracted backlog
- $5B to $7B: target IPO proceeds for SB Energy
- $500 million: OpenAI's investment in SB Energy
- $50 million: SB Energy's minimum pledge for OpenAI software through 2028
- 10 gigawatts: scale of OpenAI's 20-year Ohio data-center lease, coming online in 2028

The deal was first reported by the Wall Street Journal's Anissa Gardizy, based on draft IPO documents.

5Applications are open for the AI Safety Policy Entrepreneurship Fellowship, The fellowship supports individuals with practical ideas for addressing frontier AI safety, security and governance challenges.

The programme is designed to help fellows move a policy idea from concept towards real-world implementation by engaging decision-makers, building coalitions and developing practical pathways for policy adoption.

What the Fellowship Offers
Selected fellows will receive:

$5,000 stipend
An additional $1,000 merit award for the fellow with the most specific and actionable policy memo and advocacy plan
Travel support for selected expenses related to the programme
Policy entrepreneurship training
Professional editing support for written work
Monthly one-on-one check-ins with an FAS staff mentor
Support in connecting with relevant experts and stakeholders
Invitations to FAS programmes and policy-focused sessions.
What Will Fellows Do?
Fellows will work on a specific frontier AI safety challenge and develop a policy memo containing a practical solution and a strategy for getting the idea adopted.

Participants will also:

Take part in training sessions and reading groups
Learn how to identify policy opportunities
Build coalitions and engage decision-makers
Explore pathways for implementation through legislation, regulation, standards, procurement or other governance mechanisms
Attend a retreat in California
Participate in a capstone event in Washington, DC.
Areas of Focus
Applicants are encouraged to develop proposals relating to:

Technical AI safety
AI governance and policy
AI risk assessment and mitigation
Transparency and accountability in AI
Cybersecurity
AI capability thresholds
Risk taxonomies
Critical infrastructure
Compute governance
AI model proliferation
Governance of catastrophic AI risks.
Who Can Apply?
The fellowship welcomes applicants from different backgrounds and is particularly suited to early- and mid-career professionals with limited direct experience in public policy who want to turn their technical or subject-matter expertise into practical policy impact.

Relevant backgrounds may include:

AI research
Academia
Think tanks
Civil society
Industry
Law
Cybersecurity
National security
Other related fields.

📷 Fellowship Period: September 30, 2026 – February 28, 2027

📷 Format: Part-time and hybrid
Participants will also take part in twice-monthly group check-ins and other mandatory programme activities.
Important Dates

📷 California Retreat: Tentatively November 4–7, 2026
📷 Washington, DC Capstone: Tentatively during the week of February 22, 2027
📷 Application Deadline: September 7, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET.

Why You Should Apply
This fellowship may be a strong opportunity for professionals who already understand an important AI-related challenge and have an idea for how governments, institutions or other decision-makers could address it.
Unlike a traditional research fellowship, the programme focuses strongly on implementation, helping fellows develop ideas that could potentially influence real-world policy and governance.

Is War Coming Now?

Iran’s media machine has kicked into gear, spinning the strike on Larak Island along classic lines. State outlets will shift focus from destroyed launchers to “military and civilian casualties” legitimizing a future military response for domestic audiences

Such a military pretext could be just what Tehran’s leadership needs right now. The U.S. naval blockade and “sanctions noose” are choking Iran’s economy, slashing oil exports by nearly 70% and sharply cutting trade revenues

To derail the “slow economic strangulation” strategy, Iran needs to raise the stakes militarily. A strike on its territory offers a convenient excuse for controlled escalation and triggering a sharp spike in energy prices

However, aware of all this, Washington is unlikely to go for a major military exchange or a new round of war just yet. The U.S. has bet on financial strangulation and, apparently, will continue limiting itself to targeted “preemptive” strikes and intercepts in the Strait of Hormuz

text:
Wind as friend and enemy for airships:

An airship flies with the air mass. Early low-power engines could not usefully fight headwinds. Later ships were faster but still slow by airplane standards. Captains waited for favourable weather and often chose routes that exploited prevailing winds (for example the South Atlantic service of the Graf Zeppelin).

Many losses—among them the U.S. Navy’s Akron and Macon—were weather-related. The large surface area made airships vulnerable to gusts, shear and storms.

The golden age and the decline
World War I saw German Zeppelins used for reconnaissance and bombing; they caused alarm and forced defensive resources to be diverted, but accuracy was poor and losses to weather, accidents and improving fighters were high. 

The interwar years were the commercial peak. Graf Zeppelin flew more than a million miles, circumnavigated the globe, and ran a regular Germany–South America service with remarkable safety.

Hindenburg offered luxury transatlantic travel.

Large passenger airships were then largely abandoned. Airplanes became faster, more reliable and cheaper to operate for most routes. Airships needed enormous hangars and were fragile in wind. Hydrogen burned; the Hindenburg disaster of 6 May 1937 at Lakehurst, New Jersey—captured on newsreel and radio—shattered public confidence even though most aboard survived.

Helium was safer but scarcer; the United States controlled most production and restricted exports to Nazi Germany. As World War II approached, Germany dismantled its remaining rigid airships for aircraft production. Post-war jets made the speed gap decisive. Balloons and small helium blimps survived in niches: sport, advertising, science and occasional surveillance. Hybrid and cargo concepts continue to be proposed, but none have yet returned to mainstream transport.

text:
POPULAR UNITY
 (with AI DeepSeek and ChatGTP collaboration)
"...we must ask: when is a popular unity truly unbeatable? Political theory and history offer some conditions:  
Institutionalized pluralism: unity is not fusion, but respectful coordination of differences. Chantal Mouffe defends a "left-wing populism" that articulates diverse demands without eliminating conflict.
Unbeatability comes from the ability to add, not to refine.  
Dual power: build alternative power structures (neighborhood councils, community health systems, solidarity economy) that can replace the State in case of collapse, not just put pressure on it.
The Zapatistas and the Landless Rural Workers Movement (MST) learned this in Brazil: unity becomes unbeatable when it has territory and self-management.  
International alliances: no popular unit survives alone in a globalized world.
Samir Amin and dependency theory show that reactionary power has external allies (multinationals, foreign governments, financial organizations). Unbeatability requires a solidarity network that counteracts this support. 
 Permanent pedagogy: lucidity is not a state, but a process.
Paulo Freire insisted that critical consciousness is built through dialogue and praxis, it is not possessed all at once. An unbeatable popular unit is one that educates its members and rectifies their errors, avoiding dogmatism."

text:
The Congress government completes 1,000 days in Telangana, and the numbers offer a magnificent picture of the direction the CM Revanth Reddy government has taken!

Telangana’s per capita income has reached ₹4,18,931 in 2025–26, marking a significant rise over the previous year and taking the state further ahead of the national average. At the same time, the government has tried to push growth and welfare together rather than treating them as competing priorities.

The farm economy has been a major part of that approach - over ₹36,000 crore provided under Rythu Bharosa, farm loans waived up to ₹2 lakh for more than 25 lakh families, and Telangana surpassing Punjab in paddy cultivation and production.

For households, the impact is visible in less headline-heavy numbers: free electricity up to 200 units for more than 53 lakh families, ₹500 LPG cylinders reaching around 43 lakh families, and over 15 lakh new ration cards. These are the kinds of interventions that rarely make for dramatic political messaging, but matter considerably in the monthly household budget.

Then there is the other side of the equation - investment and jobs. ₹1.29 lakh crore secured through TG-iPASS, ₹5.75 lakh crore worth of agreements at the Telangana Rising Global Summit, and more than 72,000 government appointments point towards an effort to make Telangana’s next phase of growth broader than Hyderabad’s traditional economic story.

What stands out about these 1,000 days is therefore not one particular announcement. It is the attempt to connect welfare, agriculture, employment, investment and long-term infrastructure into one larger economic direction.

Revanth Reddy’s Telangana is increasingly being presented not simply as a state seeking growth, but as one trying to decide what that growth should look like, who should benefit from it, and what kind of state it wants to become by 2047.

#RevanthReddy

text:
WHY DOES EVERY TIME AMERICAN LEADERS LECTURE OTHER COUNTRIES LOOK A SIGN OF FAILURE OF THE US?

The research assistant paused the live video feed on her tablet as the spokesman finished his speech. "Every time Washington issues one of these moral warnings to another government, it seems to make America look weaker instead of stronger. Why does that happen?"

The veteran diplomat laid down his pen and looked at the recorded screen. "Because public rhetoric is usually what you use when quiet leverage has already run out. When a state possesses strong economic or strategic leverage, it changes behaviour behind closed doors. You don't need a podium when your sanctions, trade terms, or military posture are already doing the work."

The strategy consultant turned from the window where rain washed down the glass. "It's a clear sign of systemic substitution. The lecture isn't designed to alter the foreign government's actions. It's designed to satisfy domestic voters, political donors, or parliamentarians who demand that their leaders say something. The primary audience for an American diplomatic sermon is almost always inside America, not abroad."

The assistant frowned, watching the target foreign minister on the screen offer a sharp dismissal during his own press conference. "So the target state knows the lecture is meant for home consumption?"

"Of course they know," the diplomat said, tapping his fingers on the wooden table. "And that knowledge changes the calculation completely. The target government realises the US lacks either the willingness or the material capability to enforce compliance privately. So the target government publicly rejects the lecture, which raises their own domestic standing by showing they can stand up to Washington."

The consultant stepped closer to the table. "Look at the shift in global power structure over the past two decades. During a unipolar moment, a public lecture carried an implicit threat of isolation because there were no alternative trading partners or security patrons. In a multipolar world, when America lectures a middle power, that middle power simply pivots to alternative markets, alternative lenders, or alternative regional alliances. The lecture exposes the limit of American power rather than extending it."

The assistant pointed at a graph on her tablet displaying regional trade flows. "So by issuing the warning, the US forces the other country to demonstrate its independence, which accelerates the breakdown of the very influence Washington wanted to preserve?"

"Yes," the diplomat replied, taking a sip of tea. "It creates a self defeating loop. Furthermore, moral lectures require moral authority to function as soft power. When domestic dysfunction, civil unrest, or economic inequality in the US are visible across global media, lecturing others on governance triggers an immediate charge of hypocrisy. The lecture shifts the global conversation away from the target nation's faults and onto America's inconsistencies."

The consultant picked up a printed briefing paper. "When statecraft relies on public scolding, it reveals that the underlying instruments of influence, such as domestic consensus, economic dominance, and irresistible diplomatic coalition building, are decaying. The volume of the sermon increases as the strength of the pulpit declines."

The assistant looked back at the frozen image of the American official at the podium. "So the lecture isn't an exercise of power at all. It's the visible surface of a failed mechanism."

"It's the sound of a gear slipping," the diplomat said, closing his notebook. "Real power alters reality without needing to explain why it had the right to do so."

@usbank

U.S. Bank publicly presents itself as one of the world’s most ethical companies. Yet the environment I experienced there was the most ethically troubling workplace environment of my career.

A state employment record now says that I was discharged for “work performance or neglect of duties.” I dispute that characterization and am requesting the complete documentation U.S. Bank relied upon when providing this information.

Here is my side of the record.

In October 2024, I was assigned to perform quality assurance work on dashboards used by Corporate Audit Services. During that review, I identified numerous errors and reported them to management.

I was told that my communication was the problem and that I should describe the errors as “future enhancements.” I agreed that minor improvements could be presented that way. However, I explained that dashboards containing significant inaccuracies should be temporarily removed, corrected, validated, and then republished.

After that review, my working environment changed substantially. My manager told me that I should leave his team immediately and stated that the Audit group had a tradition of retaining only employees who followed instructions.

My manager assigned me a materially different job title and told me that whatever he entered into the system would become my job. For approximately one year and a half, I received negative feedback on a weekly basis. On every project, I was told that someone within Corporate Audit Services had a problem with my “relationships” or communication. EVERY ONE of them.

Because I had previously worked in Wells Fargo’s Conduct Management organization, this pattern raised concerns for me about possible retaliation. I reported those concerns through the Ethics Line and involved Human Resources.

After HR completed its investigation, my manager immediately changed his explanation for the job-description change. I was then told that the entirely different position had been entered manually and incorrectly by an HR contractor. HR concluded that there had been no retaliation and advised me to look for another position. I subsequently applied for several internal roles but did not receive a single interview. 
Since my discharge, I have applied for more than 1,000 positions, including many within the banking industry, without receiving a single job offer. This experience has raised a serious concern for me: whether anyone in U.S. Bank management communicated information about me to other financial institutions or prospective employers. I am not presenting this as a confirmed fact, but I am requesting disclosure of any external communications, employment references, or other information shared about me following my separation.

While I was working in U.S. Bank Corporate Audit Services, my manager instructed me to add a chart to an existing dashboard. However, I found that the underlying data was inaccurate by hundreds, and in some areas, thousands, of records. To correct the problem, I rewrote the SQL and rebuilt the dashboard.
Despite completing this corrective work, I received a formal written warning for allegedly failing to follow instructions. Approximately one month later, my manager gave a different explanation, stating that I had received the warning because I had refused to fix the dashboard. I dispute that characterization because I had, in fact, rewritten the SQL and rebuilt the dashboard specifically to correct its underlying problems. I was the person to request to fix the dashboard from errors. 

Despite completing this corrective work, I received a formal written warning for allegedly failing to follow instructions. Approximately one month later, my manager gave a different explanation, stating that I had received the warning because I had refused to fix the dashboard. I dispute that characterization because I had, in fact, rewritten the SQL and rebuilt the dashboard specifically to correct its underlying problems.ard to fix all the underlying problems. I was then formally warned for allegedly failing to follow instructions in email. Approximately one month later, I was told by my manager that I had refused to fix the dashboard, so, I received the warning. 

In subsequent projects, I identified potential OCC and SOX related control issues. The proposed testing was declined, and findings I had submitted were removed from the records. After raising these concerns to HR, I was placed on a 20-day Performance Improvement Plan and then terminated.

At separation, I received a document stating that my discharge was involuntary. I completed the work assigned to me, and the employee records subsequently provided to me contained no clear documentation explaining the stated basis for my termination.

The available records also raise questions about where responsibility for neglected duties actually belonged:

• The team folder contained a documented procedure requiring quarterly QA reviews, yet management said the former project manager had placed it there on her own initiative.

• Management also referred to having complete records from the prior year’s QA work, but that work did not appear to have been formally documented or compiled as manager claimed. 

• My personnel file response did not include the supporting termination records that would explain the statement submitted to the state.

I am therefore formally requesting that U.S. Bank provide:

The exact information it submitted to the state concerning my separation.
Every document, communication, performance record, and approval relied upon to characterize my discharge as related to performance or neglect of duties.
The names or job functions of those who prepared, reviewed, approved, or transmitted that characterization.
The documentation supporting my 20-day PIP and termination.
The audit trail for the findings, testing decisions, and deleted or altered submissions associated with the OCC- and SOX-related issues I raised.
Any records omitted from the employee file previously provided to me.

This is not simply a disagreement about management style. It concerns the accuracy of dashboards used by an audit organization, the treatment of employees who raise control concerns, and the accuracy of information reported to a state agency.

If U.S. Bank believes its characterization is accurate, it should provide the complete contemporaneous evidence supporting it. If it cannot, the record should be corrected.

An organization’s commitment to ethics is tested not by its public recognition, but by how it responds when an employee identifies errors, questions controls, and asks for the documented truth.

U.S. Bank Corporate Audit Services serves as the Third Line of Defense and is responsible for providing independent assurance to the Board. If, as my manager stated, the group has a tradition of retaining only employees who follow instructions, that raises a serious governance question: How can the Board and shareholders be confident that they are receiving complete, independent, and unfiltered information, especially when audit findings may conflict with management’s preferred narrative?

text:
The scientifically usable claim is amplification and allocation of attention, not remote collapse of other minds.

8. The legal anatomy of human–AI co-creation

8.1 Copyright: human authorship remains the gate

The Copyright Office’s Part 2 report (29 January 2025) states the governing principles with unusual clarity: existing law is adequate; AI assistance does not bar protection; purely AI-generated material, or material over which a human lacks sufficient control of expressive elements, is not protected; prompts, however elaborate, do not presently supply that control; selection, coordination, arrangement, and creative modification can. The D.C. Circuit in Thaler v. Perlmutter has affirmed that the 1976 Act requires a human author.

Applied to this manuscript: the human author’s research programme, iterative constraints, rejection of non-fitting material, and demanded structure are the candidates for protectable expression. Fluent paragraphs emitted by the model, unedited, are the candidates for the unprotected residue. The Office requires case-by-case analysis and, for registration, disclosure of AI-generated material.

8.2 Contract: ownership retained, license granted

xAI’s consumer Terms (page last updated / effective 24 August 2026) do not claim that the company owns user outputs. The operative sentences are:

“To the extent permitted by applicable law, and as between you and SpaceXAI, you retain your ownership rights to the User Content.”

and, separately, a grant of

“an irrevocable, perpetual, transferable, sublicensable, royalty-free, and worldwide right” to use, copy, store, modify, process, adapt, transmit, distribute, reproduce, publish, display, make derivative works of, and aggregate User Content “for any purpose,” including maintaining the service and improving products.

Logged-in users may elect whether User Content is used to train models. Private Chat and deletion requests are queued, with a stated window of up to thirty days, subject to legal holds. Unauthenticated use, where offered, is described as granting full rights for product development and training. Enterprise terms are stricter still: no training on customer content by default.

Exhibit G (contractual, primary). The legally accurate description is retained ownership + extremely broad license + training opt-out for authenticated consumer use, not “the company owns the paper.” The political-economy complaint that survives this correction is still substantial: an irrevocable, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to aggregate and make derivative works is, for many practical purposes, the economic equivalent of appropriation even when title remains with the user.

8.3 Why the Takings Clause does not do the work assigned to it

The Fifth Amendment’s Takings Clause constrains governmental taking of private property for public use. Intellectual property can be property in that sense. A private terms-of-service bargain is not a taking unless the firm is a state actor under the state-action doctrine—a showing that “close integration with public infrastructure and national AI strategy” does not, without more, make. Courts have been reluctant even to treat government patent-office procedures as takings.

Exhibit H (constitutional, negative). The Takings argument, as previously drafted, is not viable on present doctrine. The live legal questions are contract unconscionability, copyright preemption of overreaching licences, the Office’s human-authorship test, and forthcoming training-data litigation under Part 3 of the Office’s AI report—not eminent domain.

8.4 The extraction-pipeline claim, restated without mythology

There is no public evidence that a single conversation is distilled into model weights “within seconds to minutes.” Training is batched, expensive, and periodic. What is immediate is logging: inputs and outputs are stored, may be reviewed under the licence, and—unless the user has opted out or used Private

text:
Finality in 3 to 5 seconds is what makes both micropayments and larger transfers possible.

People often mix up TPS, confirmation speed, and fees. For someone paying, the question that matters is usually not a claim of a million TPS. It is whether the other side can treat the payment as settled a few seconds after send. Pi’s figure is about 3 to 5 seconds to finality. At a coffee counter, that beats a chain that advertises huge throughput but still makes you wait for settlement.
On throughput, the early white paper scale was about one block every 5 seconds and about 1,000 transactions per block, or roughly 200 TPS, with room to raise block capacity if needed. That is far above Bitcoin. It is not exchange-grade high-frequency throughput. Raise the node requirements high enough that only data centers can participate, and TPS can climb. The cost is dropping ordinary nodes around the world. A payments chain is for people paying, not for bots flooding the book.
Micropayments are the test. Card networks and wires have a cost floor. A $2 cross-border tip can cost more in fees than the tip itself. If confirmation takes a few seconds and the on-chain fee is close to negligible, tipping, gig payouts, and small splits start to make economic sense. That is the same direction as the G20 goal of letting more people use electronic cross-border payments.
Larger cross-border transfers can sit on the same ledger. Settlement is a state change, not a process that gets slower as the amount grows, and there is no stack of correspondent markups. Once the amount gets large, the bottleneck stops being “is the chain fast?” and becomes whether the other side accepts Pi, how much slippage fiat conversion adds, whether compliance clears, and whether the ledger can connect to banks and instant-payment systems.
The clean claim is this. Pi offers a low-energy payments ledger with second-level finality and near-zero on-chain fees. In principle it can cover both micropayments and larger transfers. The G20 offers the policy direction. Those two can line up. Lining up is not the same as G20 designating Pi as a global settlement layer, and it is not the same as the user’s all-in cost already being zero. On-ramps, FX, and compliance still sit off-chain.

text:
Never let your spouse question their place in your life...✍🏽
Not even quietly. Not even once. Because the moment doubt enters, love no longer feels like shelter—it starts to feel like something they have to earn or defend. And no one should have to compete for space in the heart of the person who promised to choose them.

Respect is not proven by words alone. Anyone can say “I love you.” Respect shows up in actions, in daily choices, in how carefully you handle the heart that has been placed in your hands. It shows in who you prioritize, who you protect, and who you make feel secure. When your partner starts to feel like they are competing for your attention, your honesty, or your loyalty, the foundation of your relationship begins to crack—slowly, quietly, but steadily.

Love cannot survive in uncertainty.
When you leave room for suspicion, unanswered questions, or emotional distance, you force your partner into a state of constant alert. They start watching instead of trusting. Wondering instead of resting. Loving you begins to hurt instead of heal. And every time you dismiss their discomfort or minimize their concerns, you push them a little further away.

Trust is fragile. It isn’t destroyed all at once—it erodes. Every unexplained action, every hidden detail, every “it’s not a big deal” moment chips away at the safety you once had. If something you’re doing would hurt your spouse or make them feel uneasy, then that action is already too costly. And if you can’t explain what you’re doing with honesty and clarity, then it isn’t worth doing at all.

Love does not grow in secrecy.
Marriage is meant to be a shared life, not a divided one. When you begin hiding parts of yourself—your phone, your conversations, your decisions—you’re not just protecting privacy, you’re creating distance. You’re building walls where there should be openness. And walls don’t protect love; they suffocate it.

Your spouse should never feel locked out of your world. Your friendships, your choices, your plans—none of these should exist in shadows. The moment you start separating what they can know from what you choose to hide is the moment intimacy begins to fade. Be where you said you’d be. Do what you said you’d do. Let your word mean something. Consistency is love in action.

Making your partner your priority doesn’t mean perfection. It means intention. It means choosing them even when it’s inconvenient. It means caring about their peace as much as your own. It means asking yourself, Does this strengthen us—or weaken us? And being honest about the answer.

Transparency is not control. It is safety.
It is the foundation of trust, security, and a love that can endure storms without falling apart. Without it, affection becomes fragile and commitment feels hollow. If you are not willing to offer openness, then you must ask yourself whether you are truly ready for the responsibility of partnership.

Let your spouse all the way in.
Not halfway. Not selectively. Completely.
Because only when two people feel chosen, protected, and fully seen can they build a love that doesn’t just survive—but lasts.

text:
He beat the state of Missouri at the Supreme Court of the United States and won the right to attend law school. Three months later, Lloyd Gaines was never seen again. Not once. Ever.

He was a valedictorian denied a legal education because Missouri had no law school that would admit a Black man — the state offered instead to pay his tuition to leave. He refused, and sued.

In 1938 the Supreme Court ruled for him: a state that provides a law school must provide one for its Black citizens. A landmark on the road to Brown.

He got hate mail by the sack. He was, by his own letters, exhausted and alone.

Then, in March 1939, he vanished.

Missouri's response to his disappearance was to move to dismiss his case — for failure to appear.

Let these young kids serve in the Military and do their best with the logistics, planning, administration, and so on…. Like DR, she is running rings around what I am aware of in the government space. That can be used in the military. Look at DOGE when it started. Outdated computer programs from the 1990’s and older. DOGE came in, money was given to them, and they were able to upgrade the systems (I’m speaking in generality here as I only have access to public info). However, they developed programs to determine how many Social Security recipients there were, ages, etc. they identified and since this has been cleared. Other programs too.

The retiring process and records retention of government employees. Paperwork only. boxes and boxes retained in an underground location, little to no computer systems. It took months for people to retire since the system was paper and processes still from, I believe I read, the 1960’s (?) correct me if I’m wrong. However, the DOGE kids (yes kids) came in, broke down the fear barriers of the records folks, they worked together to install computers, the kids wrote programs to process documents and then started getting scanned. The Retirement paperwork went on line and as of a news report I saw, the retirement process is now in 2-4 weeks or so. (Again, I could have the dates wrong)

Something I just saw on a news report was FAA is recruiting “gamers” as ATC Tower controllers. The screams I saw on social media were luscious to see. FAA, @SecDuffy and staff thought outside the box. This is some good stuff. I’ve seen the screams on here for them cutting the training programs from 2 years (on the old copper wire, paper, worn out radar,) to 3-4 months (correct me if I’m wrong.) Find them, train them, utilize their skills, and maybe let them update/refine the new ATC computers.

20+ years ago I saw an Army recruiting trailer at a local farmer’s market. Walked through and they offered me to shoot the guns…. I submit, that back when DR was interested in joining the military, she should have been allowed to, but in the field that best suited her- not an infantry, shoot’em up position, but the behind the scenes work that needs get done too. Lots of unused talent and brain activity not being recruited. With seeing what she does now, what could she have done back then? Could she could have helped many programs for the MIL get developed then and quickly that would put the USA ahead of our adversaries. I am off my soapbox. Thank you and good night.

text:
India's army has signed a Letter of Offer and Acceptance for the American Javelin anti-tank guided missile through the US Foreign Military Sales route, which means this is a government to government deal rather than a straight commercial purchase. The numbers and the value have not been disclosed. It comes roughly sixteen years after a similar attempt in 2010 fell apart.

That earlier effort collapsed because India wanted technology transfer and the United States would not part with the core seeker technology. India then looked to Israel's Spike, planned a large order of around 8,000 missiles in the hope of local production, cancelled the broad deal in 2017 over negotiations and performance concerns, and eventually made an emergency Spike purchase in 2019.

The Javelin itself is a man portable, fire and forget, third generation missile built by the Lockheed Martin and Raytheon joint venture, in American service since 1996. It uses an imaging infrared seeker and attacks from above, where tank armour is thinnest. The joint venture has signed a memorandum of understanding with Bharat Dynamics Limited, and talks now cover assembly and later production in India.

What makes this different is that the relationship has moved beyond a simple buyer and seller arrangement, and the lessons of Operation Sindoor have sharpened the need. The approach is multi track, with the Javelin filling the immediate gap while DRDO's MPATGM continues testing and a fuller domestic missile ecosystem is built over time.
