text:
Crossing the strait into Italy, Belisarios came against Naples, where its walls and steep ground broke every direct attempt to enter, until an abandoned aqueduct was discovered passing beneath the defenses. 

Belisarios had the narrow channel widened in secret and sent chosen soldiers through it under darkness; emerging within the city, the Romans forced their way through the streets, opened the gates to the army outside, and took from within what repeated assault had failed to break from without. Theodahad, king of the Goths, was soon overthrown by his own warriors, and Vitiges, raised in his place, withdrew north to gather the Gothic army around Ravenna. 

Before the new king could return in strength, Belisarios marched upon Rome and entered through the Asinarian Gate while the Gothic garrison withdrew through the Flaminian; with the city in his hands and the Gothic army gathering beyond it, he turned immediately to the immense circuit of the walls, repairing what neglect had weakened and preparing a few thousand soldiers to receive the strength of the kingdom moving south against them.

Vitiges returned in the spring with the Gothic army and surrounded Rome, cutting the aqueducts, closing the roads, and driving his assaults against walls whose enormous circuit Belisarios scarcely possessed enough men to defend. Belisarios answered this lack of numbers with superior movement, shifting reserves along the walls as each attack gathered, throwing cavalry through the gates whenever the Gothic formations opened upon the plain, then wheeling the horsemen back before the greater enemy force could close around them. 

Assault followed assault until the army which had descended upon Rome expecting to recover it had spent more than a year beneath walls it could neither break nor abandon without defeat. When Vitiges finally withdrew north, Belisarios followed, pressing the Goths back toward Ravenna, stripping away the fortified positions guarding its approaches, and taking Auximum after hunger exhausted the garrison. 

He then closed upon Ravenna itself, severing the roads and waterways by which provisions entered the capital and tightening the pressure until hunger began to wreck the people within its walls. 

The Gothic nobles, seeing the kingdom contract around Ravenna while Vitiges remained unable to reverse the war, offered Belisarios the sovereignty of the West if he would abandon Ioustinianos and accept their crown. 

Belisarios allowed them to believe he would take it and entered Ravenna while they awaited his accession; once the Roman army held the city, he declared himself still the emperor’s general, taking in the same stroke the Gothic capital, its treasury, and Vitiges himself, and returning east with the king who had once marched upon Rome expecting to carry Belisarios away in chains.

In scarcely seven years, Belisarios had crossed from Constantinople into Africa, broken the Vandal armies at Ad Decimum and Tricamarum, entered Carthage, extinguished a kingdom that had ruled there for nearly a century, returned east in triumph, crossed again into Sicily, taken the island, forced his passage into Naples, seized Rome before the Goths could recover it, defended the city for more than a year against the gathered strength of their kingdom, and then carried the war north until Ravenna itself opened before him. 

He had begun in 533 with an army sent against one lost province; by 540 he had taken two kingdoms, recovered Africa and the greater part of Italy, took control of Carthage, Rome, and Ravenna, brought Gelimer and Vitiges beneath Roman power, and stood at the end of his victories with the crown of the Italy itself offered to him by the very men he had conquered.

text:
Sailing for Africa in 533, Belisarios crossed the Mediterranean before Gelimer, king of the Vandals, had drawn the full strength of his kingdom together; with the Vandal forces still scattered, he landed at Caput Vada without opposition and drove north along the coast toward Carthage.

Gelimer followed behind him with the main Vandal army, while Ammatas, the king’s brother, came south from Carthage and Gibamund, his nephew, swept across the country from the west, the three forces intending to meet at Ad Decimum and crush the Roman column between them.

Ammatas reached the ground before the others, bringing only those nearest him while the remainder still followed from Carthage in scattered companies; Iōannēs the Armenian, commanding three hundred Roman horsemen at the head of the march, struck this first force, killed Ammatas in the fighting, and drove the survivors almost to the gates of the city.

Gibamund meanwhile moved against Belisarios’s inland flank and came upon the Hunnic cavalry posted there; the Huns fell upon his two thousand Vandals, shattered them, and killed Gibamund before he could unite with Gelimer.

The Vandal king arrived last with the main army, after the two forces meant to close upon the Roman march had already been destroyed; taking the high ground above Decimum, his horsemen drove the Roman federates from it and then broke eight hundred of Belisarios’s guards advancing to their support. Federates and guards alike fell back toward the main army, leaving Gelimer in possession of the heights with the Roman cavalry already retreating before him.

Descending onto the field, Gelimer found Ammatas among the dead and halted over his brother while the advantage still lay entirely in his hands. Belisarios met the retreating horsemen as they reached him, stopped their flight, rebuilt their formation, and immediately commanded them back toward Decimum; before Gelimer had restored the order lost in the pursuit, Belisarios fell upon the Vandals, swept them from the ground they had just won, and drove the king westward into Numidia, leaving the road to Carthage open behind him.

Gelimer gathered what remained of his strength once more at Tricamarum, placing Tzazon, his brother, at the center of the Vandal line. Belisarios sent his cavalry across the stream against him, drawing them back and returning to the charge until Tzazon fell; with their commander dead beneath them, the Vandal center broke, and the Roman cavalry drove through the opening. The infantry came up behind them with the Vandal camp exposed ahead, and Gelimer abandoned the field for the mountains, bringing within a single campaign the collapse of a kingdom which had ruled Roman Africa for nearly a century.

From Africa Belisarios crossed into Sicily in 535, landing at Catana and receiving Syracuse with most of the island by surrender, until Panormus alone remained behind walls too strong to be easily approached from the land. 

Belisarios brought the fleet into the harbor beneath the fortifications and found the mastheads rising above the battlements; filling the small boats carried aboard his ships with bowmen, he had them hauled by ropes up the masts until the archers themselves stood above the level of the walls. 

From there the Romans poured arrows down upon defenders who had prepared themselves against every assault from below, driving them from the battlements and compelling Panormus to surrender, leaving all Sicily in the grasp of Roman hands.

🔸 Former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov is seeking U.S. investment for a new defense-tech fund that would both finance and create Ukrainian weapons companies, the Financial Times reports.

🔸 Fedorov said the fund would initially focus on battlefield robots, cheap high-speed interceptor drones and low-cost AI-enabled missiles, saying Ukraine needs faster weapons development if the war continues for several more years.

🔸 He also offered to help the U.S. “build an army of drones” in exchange for American Patriot missile interceptors, which Kyiv is increasingly short of as Russian missile and drone attacks intensify amid the shortfall caused by the Middle East war.

Fedorov, fired by President Zelenskyy last month, said Ukraine is currently “gradually, slowly losing” the war and suggested: “If we don’t respond to these issues, they will smash us.”

text:
Fedorov offers drone technology to US in exchange for Patriots, seeks funding for defense tech fund

Former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov is seeking U.S. investment for a new defense technology fund and offering to help Washington develop drone capabilities in exchange for Patriot missile interceptors for Ukraine, he told the Financial Times in an interview published Aug. 30.
The proposal comes as Fedorov has begun an international trip that has included Italy and the United States after being dismissed by President Volodymyr Zelensky as defense minister.

Fedorov told the FT in Washington that he is seeking backing from venture capitalists, private investors, and U.S. technology companies for a fund that would invest in Ukrainian defense startups and create new companies focused on battlefield technologies.
"This is not exactly a classic venture fund," Fedorov said in an interview. "We're writing a new history of the war."

Fedorov said the fund would initially focus on battlefield robotics, high-speed interceptor drones capable of countering Russia's newer jet-powered attack drones, and low-cost missiles equipped with artificial intelligence.
He also proposed a direct exchange with the United States, saying he would be willing to help Washington "build an army of drones" in return for Patriot interceptors to help Ukraine withstand Russian attacks this winter.
"I'm ready to make that trade," Fedorov told the FT.
Ukraine has faced a critical shortage of Patriot interceptors as Russia has intensified missile and drone attacks against Ukrainian cities and infrastructure. The U.S.-made systems are among the few weapons capable of intercepting Russia's ballistic missiles

Fedorov said Ukraine had already tested high-speed drones designed to bring down Russia's jet-powered attack drones and argued that they could be produced at scale with additional investment.
"We need more jet drones, we need cheap missiles, we need missiles with artificial intelligence," he said. "You can't conduct any kind of dialogue with Putinany other way. He understands only force."
Fedorov served as defense minister from January to July before Zelensky dismissed him in a Cabinet reshuffle. His firing triggered weeks of protestsacross Ukraine and elevated Fedorov's profile as a potential political rival to Zelensky.
After Zelensky declined to reinstate him as defense minister earlier this month, Fedorov called for wartime elections, a move that divided public opinion.

In an interview with the FT, Fedorov defended his call for elections, saying it was not aimed at replacing Zelensky but at updating the country's governing system.
"This is not against Zelensky, it's not against some specific person," Fedorov said. "It's about the fact that we need to … update the state's operating system."
Fedorov's trip to the U.S. follows a visit to Italy, where he agreed to serve as an unpaid adviser to Italian Defense Minister Guido Crosetto on modern warfare technologies, his press service told the Kyiv Independent on Aug. 28.
Fedorov's press service said his primary focus would remain on projects in Ukraine and efforts to attract international resources for the country's defense technology sector. During his meeting with Crosetto, the two discussed drones, autonomous systems, air defense, and the development of Ukraine's defense technology ecosystem.

The FT reported that Fedorov was also considering similar advisory roles with other partner countries, potentially including France and the United States. He declined to say whether he planned to meet with officials from the Trump administration during his Washington visit.
Fedorov also said he remained in close contact with U.S. billionaire and SpaceX CEO Musk, but declined to comment on whether he planned to meet him in the U.S. Ukraine has relied heavily on Musk's Starlink satellite communications system throughout the war.

Source Kyiv independent

text:
❯ Shared storage: The NFS Under Your Cloud Bill
Amazon charges 0.30 dollars per gigabyte-month for EFS. The same platform sells block storage at 0.08. The protocol doing the actual work turned up in 1984 and weighs 1.73 megabytes.

Sun Microsystems had a problem in 1984 that was mostly about furniture. They sold workstations, the workstations stood in rooms full of engineers, and engineers do not stay at one desk. You finished a shift at the machine by the window, came in next morning, sat at whichever one was free, and your files were still by the window.

■ WHAT IT ACTUALLY SOLVED

The worst of the obvious answers meant teaching every program on the system to fetch files over a network, and once applications know about the network they have to cope with it: connection failures, retries, partial reads and authentication, in every program separately and slightly differently each time.

Sun slid the network one layer below the file system instead, where no application would ever have to look at it. A directory on another machine gets attached to the local tree, and from that moment the kernel answers requests for it by talking across the wire. cat opens a file and reads bytes, exactly as it would on a local disk.

The early versions were deliberately stateless, because Sun assumed servers would crash and in 1984 they did. Locking is state by definition, so it arrived bolted on the side through a separate daemon, and NFSv4 eventually took the state back in with sessions and delegations. We have argued about stateless services ever since, forty years after a file protocol settled it.

■ WHAT IT STILL DOES WELL

On the FreeBSD box in front of me the whole thing weighs 1.73 megabytes, across four kernel modules and six userland programs. pkg which /sbin/mount_nfs reports nothing, because the file arrived with the system, along with seven manual pages. Exporting a dataset is a property: zfs set sharenfs=on tank/work, and the pool tells the daemon what to publish.

What that buys is POSIX semantics across machines. Two hosts can hold the same file open, a process can write into the middle of a file without reading the rest, rename is atomic, and locks exist where other machines respect them. Unremarkable until you build the same thing on an object store, where a write is a whole-object upload, a rename is a copy followed by a delete, and locking is something you invent with a database table and a lease.

■ WHERE IT ASKS FOR TROUBLE

AUTH_SYS does not authenticate. The client states which user it is acting for and the server takes it on trust, so keeping numeric identifiers aligned across every host that mounts the share is the sort of faff nobody enjoys. Kerberos through RPCSEC_GSS settles it properly and is deployed far less than it should be, because standing up a realm is a project rather than an afternoon.

A hard mount hangs when the server stops answering, and it hangs in a state that resists interruption, so one unreachable file server can freeze a room full of machines that were only listing a directory. Latency is arithmetic on top of that: every operation costs a round trip, and Amazon advertised a forty per cent cut in write latency for files under 64 kilobytes in 2022, which tells you where the pain was.

■ THE BILL

These days you rent it by the hour, mostly without being told what you are renting.

Amazon EFS is NFS. Google Cloud Filestore is NFS and nothing else. Azure NetApp Files offers v3 and v4.1. And when a Kubernetes user asks for a volume with ReadWriteMany, the access mode you need whenever more than one pod writes to the same files, the driver underneath is almost always an NFS driver.

The managed service buys real things: replication across availability zones, capacity that grows without anybody resizing anything, and an operations team awake at three in the morning. Some organisations should absolutely pay for that. What four times the price cannot buy is a different protocol, and the one you are renting has been in your base system all along.

Somewhere in your estate is a directory that three machines need to write to, and someone is either paying rent on it or has spent a fortnight rebuilding it out of an object store and a lease table.

#FreeBSD #UnixTools #CloudCosts #SysAdmin #Storage

text:
It is deeply provoking to watch nations that gained independence long after us sprint miles ahead, leaving Nigeria so far behind that we can barely see their dust.

While we remain trapped in mediocrity, other countries have built functional systems. Singapore gained independence in 1965 and transformed from a developing port into one of the world's wealthiest, safest, and most technologically advanced financial hubs. Seychelles became independent in 1976 and now boasts the highest Human Development Index ranking in Africa, achieving high-income status through strong social infrastructure. Mauritius took its freedom in 1968 and consistently leads the continent in governance, safety, and economic diversification. Botswana achieved independence in 1966 and turned its diamond wealth into robust public infrastructure, high literacy, and stable democracy. Even newer nations like Rwanda, Cape Verde, and Namibia—which only gained independence in 1990—are setting global benchmarks in ease of doing business, press freedom, and institutional efficiency.

Meanwhile, what are our political figures serving us in 2026?

On one end, Minister of Works David Umahi is actively lecturing the South-East, demanding that citizens express public gratitude and surrender their votes to President Bola Tinubu and the APC just because basic asphalt is being laid on federal roads. As if federal infrastructure is paid for out of his private bank account instead of taxpayer funds and national revenue. On the other end, people are busy defending @davido uncle Governor Ademola Adeleke for prancing around, dancing, and prostrating at every public event, as if political entertainment and cultural theatrics equal actual development.

When did the bare minimum become a personal favor? When did political performance replace constitutional duty?

Every nation that works enforces fierce political accountability. Until Nigerians wake up, reject these cheap distractions, and demand strict accountability from anyone who holds public office—by any legal and civic means necessary—we will remain a country that celebrates bare-minimum roads while the rest of the world builds the future.

We must be ready to demand accountability from these politicians, or will we keep defending the very leaders holding us back. 

This is 2026. If you have nothing to offer sit back in your home and let people like Alex otti and Peter Obi take your position.

We're very honoured to offer this spectacular century-old hand-made Nepalese Kukri knife as a Wild Hornets raffle prize

Heartfelt thanks to Ukrainian-Canadian author Victor Malarek for donating it

The Kukri is Nepal's national weapon—associated with the legendary Gurkha warriors

A Guru gifted this carbon-steel blade—with a water buffalo horn handle and leather-wrapped scabbard—to Victor 40 years ago for his work as a journalist on human rights issues

The Guru was himself gifted it as a young Indian Army officer stationed in Nepal in the early 1950s

🐝
"This gift means a lot to me, as does the incredible work of the Wild Hornets," Victor says

The 10-inch curved blade features traditional floral, dragon and geometric scrollwork and the iconic "cho"

The cho is the distinct semi-circular notch near the handle that serves practical and symbolic functions, such as stopping blood from reaching the handle and representing sacred footprints

🐝
The set includes the main blade—used for combat and heavy-duty tasks like chopping—and two small knives tucked beneath its sheeth, all essential parts of a true traditional Kukri

The smaller of the little blades, the Karda, is a compact utility knife used for tasks like skinning animals, cleaning fish, preparing vegetables and carving wood

The other small blade, the Chakmak, has a blunt polished edge and is used to hone and maintain the Kukri and to start fires; it creates sparks when striking flint

The large blade symbolizes bravery and honour, while the smaller knives represent discipline and self-reliance—defining traits of the Gurkhas

🐝
Custom-made traditional Kukris are considered works of art and collector's items

They're often carried by high-ranking military members and presented during military retirements, promotions, weddings and generational handovers to signify high status and deep appreciation

🐝

text:
What lessons and inspiration can the Polish Solidarity movement offer today, at a time of growing polarisation?

It vindicates Arendt’s insight that freedom arises when people come together and act in concert. Its ethos points to the value of an inclusive agora. Liberals, conservatives, leftists, believers and atheists worked side by side. Under Solidarity’s umbrella, and later in its underground structures, there emerged a lively alternative public sphere of independent periodicals such as Tygodnik Mazowsze, clandestine publishing houses, educational initiatives and discussion circles. The Catholic Church also played an important part, providing meeting places, protection and channels of communication.

Today marks the 46th anniversary of the signing of the Gdańsk Agreement.

Nor was the movement merely a project of the intelligentsia. Staniszkis, who served on Solidarity’s council of experts, later stressed the indispensable role of the workers. They not only risked their jobs and livelihoods; they also combined ideals and visions with immediate practical experience. In her view, some of the movement’s intellectuals and advisers were so confined by their theoretical models that they tended towards excessive caution. It was the workers themselves who insisted on implementing the first of the 21 demands the recognition of free and independent trade unions despite tactical advice to moderate their ambitions.

Some have described the movement’s emergence as a three-stage process. In 1970 the workers protested without the intellectuals. In 1976, with the establishment of the Workers’ Defence Committee, or KOR, intellectuals organised to support persecuted workers. In 1980 the two sides finally came together.

Solidarity’s resonance extended far beyond Poland. As early as August 1980 the International Confederation of Free Trade Unions declared its support; trade unions and other organisations in France, Italy, America and many other countries soon followed. Aid parcels from Germany and other countries, printing presses were sent to the underground; demonstrations and hunger strikes were organised; and humanitarian assistance, often channelled through the Church, poured in. Elsewhere in the Soviet bloc, courageous people openly declared their solidarity with the Poles despite the threat of repression. Ronald Reagan’s Christmas address in December 1981, in which he called on the world to stand with the Polish people, attracted global attention.

Angela Merkel neatly captured Solidarity’s European significance: “Your desire for freedom set stones in motion that ultimately brought down the Berlin Wall and the Iron Curtain.”

There is a reason the United States government does not treat heroin trafficking as a paperwork offence. Heroin is not contraband. It is a death sentence sold by the gram.

Consider what this drug has done to America alone. Drug overdoses have killed over 1.25 million people in the United States since 1999, and over 105,000 Americans died from drug-involved overdose in 2023 alone. Heroin sits at the black heart of that catastrophe. Heroin-involved overdose deaths rose from 3,036 in 2010 to a peak of 15,469 in 2016 — a more than fivefold increase in six years. Even the recent decline in heroin deaths is no mercy: heroin deaths dropped largely because fentanyl displaced heroin in the supply, and fentanyl is far more potent and unpredictable. The heroin pipelines built in the 1980s and 1990s laid the rails on which fentanyl now travels.

Now consider Chicago, and the years that matter. According to US court documents, a white heroin trafficking network operated in Chicago and parts of Indiana, led by Adegboyega Mueez Akande, between 1988 and 1993. The network was actively trafficking white heroin into Illinois, and US court documents and affidavits from the IRS and FBI detailed how funds in bank accounts controlled by Bola Tinubu were tied to narcotics proceeds. The 1993 Illinois court judgment saw Tinubu forfeit 460,000 dollars from two bank accounts, after an investigation linked over 2 million dollars across several of his accounts to proceeds from the heroin trafficking of Akande and Abiodun Agbele. According to the affidavit, Akande controlled the operation of white heroin from Nigeria in conjunction with other individuals, and one individual identified as working with Akande was Bola Tinubu — and the Chicago address Tinubu gave on his account application was the same address used as the drop-off point for packages from Nigeria containing the white heroin. He was never criminally charged. But no innocent explanation has ever been offered for why the American government kept his money.

What was flooding into Chicago in those exact years? Between the 1980s and 1990s, the purity of heroin brought into the United States increased significantly, and Chicago stood among the largest, most lucrative white powder heroin markets in America. US intelligence was explicit about who moved it: Nigerian criminal groups transported Southeast and Southwest Asian heroin to Chicago by couriers aboard commercial aircraft, buses, and trains, and via package delivery services. The bodies followed. There were 803 drug-related deaths in Chicago in 1998, a 32 percent increase over 1995, and in 2000 heroin was a factor in more deaths in the Chicago area than any other illicit drug — 499 heroin-related deaths across the six-county metropolitan area in that single year.

And who died? Not the traffickers. Fierce competition pushed drug sales outdoors into areas with few legal jobs, including public housing complexes and distressed neighbourhoods on Chicago's West Side. Heroin became increasingly plentiful in low-income Black communities through what health experts call predatory marketing — and Black men born between 1951 and 1970 have always had the greatest risk of dying of overdoses, in their 20s, 30s and 40s, in Chicago, Baltimore, Washington and beyond. That is precisely the generation that was young and vulnerable when the Akande network operated. Decades later the wound has not closed: opioid-related death rates in Chicago remain highest for African Americans, and the majority of victims are on Chicago's West Side — Austin, East Garfield Park and West Garfield Park.

This is why the Greenspan v. FBI and DEA litigation before Judge Beryl Howell matters. This is why the release of the full investigative files matters. Nigeria is not being asked to relitigate 1993. Nigeria is being asked to look at what white heroin did to Black families in Chicago —

MESSAGE FROM ST. MICHAEL THE ARCHANGEL, AUGUST 30, 2026

GO AND EVANGELIZE

"Dear brothers in Christ, King of the Universe and Our Lord, today I want to speak to you about evangelization in the modern world in which you live.

As in the time of the first apostles of Christ, you are living in an era in which sin and all its dire consequences are pervading every situation you experience. I know it causes you pain and suffering. I answer you: "The soldier of Our Lord Jesus who does not accept suffering is not worthy of Him and, consequently, of being part of my army."

Whoever is called to battle is tested and sanctified in the purifying fire of suffering. Have you been or are you suffering? Well, you are on the right path to being chosen among my ranks, my army! You only have to accept it arm in arm with the Divine Mother, offer it to God the Father, and bless it as a great grace of the Most Holy Trinity for your glory and eternal salvation. of our brothers still in spiritual blindness.

Suffering produces perseverance, experience, and hope.
"We also glory in tribulations, knowing that tribulation produces perseverance, and perseverance, experience, and experience, hope." Romans 5:3-5

Suffering sanctifies, transforms from imperfect to perfect. Trials perfect, purify, and elect us as soldiers of Christ the King and Queen Mary, worthy of entering the Kingdom of Heaven.
"Consider it pure joy, my brothers, when you encounter various trials, knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance. And let endurance have its perfect work in you." 2 James 1:2-4

The testing of faith leads to spiritual maturity. Faith tested by fire.
"In this you rejoice, even if now for a little while you may have been grieved by various trials, so that the genuineness of your faith, more precious than gold, which though perishable is tested by fire, may be found to bring praise and glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ." 3. 1 Peter 1:6-7

Once you accept, as an integral part of your existence in Christ, the desire to suffer to be like Him, each of you can call yourself a true soldier in the glorious army of God the Father Almighty and the Most Holy Heavenly Mother, for whom I am responsible.

May the example of Saint Pio, Saint Francis, and Saint Clare, of Saint Joan of Arc, Saint Catherine of Siena, and all the Saints, accompany you.

Brothers and sisters, I, Saint Michael, he who, eternally defeating the Satanic rebellion, proclaimed "Who is like God?", therefore call you to unsheath the mystical weapons at your disposal.

[ ] Incessant prayer in communion with the Will of God is the first weapon at your disposal. The great prayerful ones who, together with the Heavenly Mother, our Queen, restrain the hand of the Father and His Son from immediately punishing this ungrateful world and whose intercession saves the multitudes of souls from the darkness and flames of hell.

[ ] The second weapon is evangelization. Every time you bear witness to Christ and the Will of the Father, you are evangelizing. Do so in any situation with holy courage and calculated prudence, using every means and channel of communication at your disposal (e.g., social media). And if it isn't available to you, create it immediately without delay; be creatures in the image and likeness of the Eternal Creator, who prides himself on having children who imitate him in a holy way.

[ ] The third weapon is charity. Be good and kind to everyone, love your neighbor more than yourself, and at the same time, fight the evil one with determination in the situations you encounter. Give the Truth and show the Way to obtain the reward of true Life, Eternal Life. And choose to give rather than receive, while not drawing upon the unwanted goodness that the Good Lord sends you through your brothers and sisters.

text:
August 31 Saint Raymond Nonnatus, Confessor: From the Liturgical Year of Dom Prosper Louis Pascal Guéranger, O.S.B., 1903.
.
White Double
.
August closes as it began, with a feast of deliverance; as though that were the divine seal set by Eternal Wisdom upon this month—the month when holy Church makes the works and ways of Divine Wisdom the special object of her contemplation.
.
Upon the fall of our first parents and their expulsion from Paradise, the Word and Wisdom of God, that is, the Second Person of the Blessed Trinity, began the great work of our deliverance—that magnificent work of human Redemption which, by an all-gracious, eternal degree of the three Divine Persons, was to be wrought out by the Son of God in our flesh. And as that blessed Savior, in his infinite wisdom, made spontaneous choice of sorrows, of sufferings, and of death on a cross as the best means of our redemption, so has he always allotted to his best loved friends the kind of life which he had deliberately chosen for himself, that is, the way of the Cross. And the nearest and dearest to him were those who were predestined, like his Blessed Mother, the Mater Dolorosa, to have the honor of being most like himself—the Man of Sorrows. Hence the toils and trials of the greatest Saints; hence the great deliverances wrought by them, and their heroic victories over the world and over the spirits of wickedness in the high places.
.
On the feasts of St. Raymund of Pegnafort and St. Peter Nolasco, we saw something of the origin of the illustrious Order, of which Raymund Nonnatus added such glory. Soon the august foundress herself, Our Lady of Mercy, will come in person to receive the expression of the world’s gratitude for so many benefits. The following Legend recounts the peculiar merits of our Saint of today.
.
Raymundus, Nonnatus cognomento dictus, quia præter communem naturæ legem e mortuæ matris dissecto latere in lucem eductus fuit, Portelli in Catalaunia piis et nobilibus parentibus ortus, ab ipsa infantia futuræ sanctitatis indicia dedit. Nam puerilia oblectamenta, mundique illecebras respuens, ita pietati operam dabat, ut omnes in puero adultam virtutem admirarentur. Crescente vero ætate, litterarum studiis incubuit: sed mox jubente patre vitam ruri agens, sacellum sancti Nicolai in Portelli finibus situm crebro adibat, ut sacram Deiparæ imaginem, quæ is eo summa fidelium veneratione etiam nunc colitur, visitaret. Thi effusus in preces, ipsam Dei parentem, ut se in filium adoptare viamque salutis ac scientiam sanctorum edocere dignaretur, enixe deprecabatur.
.
Raymund, surnamed Nonnatus, on account of his having been brought into the world in an unusual manner after the death of his mother, was of a pious and noble family of Portelli in Catalonia. From his very infancy he showed signs of his future holiness; for, despising childish amusements and the attractions of the world, he applied himself to the practice of piety so that all wondered at his virtues, which far surpassed his age. As he grew older he began his studies; but after a short time he returned at his father’s command to live in the country. He frequently visited the chapel of St. Nicholas, built near Portelli, in order to venerate in it a holy image of the Mother of God, which is still more honored by the faithful. There he would pour out his prayers, begging God’s holy Mother to adopt him for her son and to deign to teach him the way of salvation and the science of the saints.
.
Nec defuit votis ejus benignissima Virgo. Ab ipsa enim intellexit gratissimum sibi fore, si religionem sub titulo de Mercede, seu de Misericordia redemptionis captivorum, ea suggerente nuper fundatam, ingrederetur. Qua monitione percepta, Barcinomen statim profectus, illus tam præcellentis erga proximum caritatis institutum amplexus est. Regulari igitur militiæ adscriptus, virginitatem, quam pridem beatæ Virgini consecraverat, perpetuo coluit, ceterique virtutibus enituit, caritate præsertim erga christianos, qui sub potestate paganorum miseram in captivitate vitam degebant. Hos ut redimeret, in Africam missus, cum jam multos a servitute liberasset, ne, consumpta pecunia, aliis item in proximo abnegandæ fidei discrimine constitutis deesset, se ipsum pignori dedit; sed cum ardentissimo salutis animarum desiderio succensus, plures mahometanos suis concionibus ad Christum converteret, in arctam custodiam a barbaris conjectus, variisque suppliciis cruciatus, mox labiis perforatis et sera ferrea clausis, crudele martyrium diu sustinuit.
.
The most benign Virgin heard his prayer, and gave him to understand that it would greatly please her if he entered the Religious Order lately founded by her inspiration, under the name of the Order of “Ransom, or of Mercy for the redemption of captives.” Upon this Raymund at once set out for Barcelona, there to embrace that institute so full of brotherly charity. Thus enrolled in the army of holy religion, he persevered in perpetual virginity, which he had already consecrated to the Blessed Virgin. He excelled also in every other virtue most especially in charity towards those Christians who were living in misery, as slaves of the pagans. He was sent to Africa to redeem them, and freed many from slavery. But when he had exhausted his money, rather than abandon others who were in danger of losing their faith, he gave himself up to the barbarians as a pledge for their ransom. Burning with a most ardent desire for the salvation of souls, he converted several Mahometans to Christ by his preaching. On this account he was thrown into a close prison and after many tortures his lips were pierced through and fastened together with an iron padlock, which cruel martyrdom he endured for a long time.
.
Ob hæc et alia fortiter gesta, sanctitatis ejus fama longe lateque diffusa est. Qua permotus Gregorius Nonus, in amplissimum sanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ cardinalium collegium Raymundum adscripsit: sed vir Dei in ea dignitate ab omni pompa abborrens, religiosæ humilitatis tanacissimus semper fuit. Roman vero pergens, statim ac Cardonam pervenit, extremo morbo confectus, ecclesiasticis sacramentis muniri summis precibus postulavit. Cumque morbus ingravesceret, et sacerdos diutius tardaret, Angelorum ministerio, sub specie religiosorum sui Ordinis apparentium, salutari viatico refectus fuit. Quo sumpto, et gratiis Deo peractis, migravit ad Dominum Dominica ultima Augusti, anno millesimo ducentesimo quadragesimo. Mortui corpus, cum circa locum sepulturæ conetntio orta esset, arcæ inclusum, et mulæ cæcæ impositum, ad sacellum sancti Nicolai Dei nutu delatum fuit, ut ibi tumularetur, ubi prima jecerat sanctioris vitæ fundamenta. Illic constructo sui Ordinis cœnobio, a confluentibus voti causa ex universa Catalaunia fidelibus populis honoratur, variis miraculis et signis gloriosus.
.
This and his other noble deeds spread the fame of his sanctity far and near, so that Gregory IX determined to enroll him in the august college of the cardinals of the Holy Roman Church. When raised to that dignity the man of God shrank from all pomp and clung always to religious humility. On his way to Rome, as soon as he reached Cardona, he was attacked by his last illness, and earnestly begged to be strengthened by the Sacraments of the Church. As his illness grew worse and the priest delayed to come, Angels appeared, clothed in the religious habit of his Order, and refreshed him with the saving Viaticum. Having received It he gave thanks to God, and passed to our Lord on the last Sunday of August in the year 1240. Contentions arose concerning the place where he should be buried; his coffin was therefore placed upon a blind mule and by the will of God it was taken to the chapel of St. Nicholas, that it might be buried in that place where he had first begun a more perfect life. A convent of his Order was built in the spot, and there famous for many signs and miracles he is honored by the concourse of all the faithful of Catalonia, who come there to fulfill their vows.
.
To what a length, O illustrious Saint, didst thou follow the counsel of the Wise man! The bands of Wisdom, says he, are a healthful binding. And, not satisfied with putting thy feet into her fetters and thy neck into her chains, in the joy of thy love thou didst offer thy lips to the dreadful padlock, not mentioned by the son of Sirach. But what a reward is thine, now that this Wisdom of the Father, whose twofold precept of charity thou didst so fully carry out, inebriates thee with the torrent of eternal delights, adorning thy brow with the glory and grace which radiate from her own beauty! We would fain be forever with thee near that throne of light; teach us, then, how to walk in this world by the beautiful ways and peaceable paths of Wisdom. Deliver our souls, if they be still captive in sin; break the chains of our self-love, and give us instead those blessed bands of Wisdom which are humility, abnegation, self-forgetfulness, love of our brethren for God’s sake, love of God for his own sake.

text:
I had blown this misleading bite from Prashant Kishor to smithereens at the time of Operation Sindoor. Here it is again, and it will continue till the time the propaganda continues:

A. Fact checks

1. OS did not end in a day. Due to Pakistan’s attempt to get even with India, it lasted 4 days: 7-10 May 2025. The ceasefire was declared—with the caveat that it was only being suspended—on the 10th.

2. The “government” does not comprise EAM @DrSJaishankar alone. Our primary source of information was the press conferences by the Indian defence forces. They said there was actionable intelligence on nine—out of many—terrorist camps only. To make sure India is not accused of recklessness, targets that India was not sure harboured terrorists were spared. The EAM said this too; PK’s memory is selective.

3. The government is not answerable to media speculations. PK needs to decide whether he must base his theories on the media commentary or India’s official stand; he claims it’s the latter but veers again and again towards claims made by zealous TV anchors, like (a) reclaiming PoK and (b) freeing Balochistan.

4. Amit Shah never said 3 (a) and 3 (b) in the context of OS, either in Parliament or elsewhere. They may be India’s ultimate goals, but they were never the objectives of OS.

5. India did not yield to nuclear blackmail. If it had, OS would not have happened at all. It went on for 4 days, as already mentioned.

B. My assessment of OS and anticipation of future Indian military action

There are sound arguments against prolonging OS (much as I did not like it winding up in 4 days).

1. India did not announce officially that OS was “war” (Pakistan did say the nine attacks on the first day of OS were India’s declaration of war on Pakistan). An official declaration of war has costs. The country that does it must brace for several restrictions on trade and investment. This is not the same as POTUS @realDonaldTrump claiming his offer of trade dissuaded India and Pakistan. Even without sanctions on the country, businesses worldwide hesitate to invest in a warring country. Stretching the war would have reversed the @narendramodi government’s economic success story of the past 11 years. To be honest, we couldn’t have afforded it.

2. After India declared it had hit 9 targets in Pakistan and PoK, OS was supposed to be over. It continued for three more days only to thwart Pakistan’s bid to settle scores with India. In other words, 7 May was an act of offence (using SCALP and HAMMER missiles and bombs) while 8, 9 and 10 May were acts of defence (where India’s Akash, AkashTeer and S-400 Triumf were blocking incoming Pakistani missiles and drones). Considered from this angle, the cessation of OS was overdue after the first day, notwithstanding our emotions and India’s official statement that it has only been put on hold.

3. OS successfully threatened Pakistan with higher costs for nurturing terrorists, with the Pakistani army now having to pay for its misadventures. It’s no longer about a bunch of expendable terrorists getting killed in India’s retaliation.

4. OS had an unannounced and unanticipated success. It was a bonus: Proving that the Chinese offensive and defensive equipment that Pakistan employs are duds, and it’s perhaps time for the US to realise its F-16s are now obsolete technology. After their inability to penetrate India in 2019, this was the second time that the American fighter planes in the Pakistani inventory proved useless.

5. If the surgical strike of 2016, the airstrike of 2019 and the missile strikes of 2025 show a pattern, the Modi government is constantly raising the bar. As Pakistan cannot abandon Zulfikar Ali Bhutto’s strategy of “bleeding India with a thousand cuts”, India’s next retaliation against Pakistani terrorism is on the cards, and it will be a real war, not a mere skirmish. Our unsatiated souls will then be content.

text:
Who Should New Mobile Bridge Be Named For? VOTE

The planned I-10 Mobile River Bridge is set to become an architectural landmark, featuring the second-highest deck of any bridge over a navigable waterway in the United States, behind only the Golden Gate Bridge. However, as planning moves forward, a passionate debate has emerged over a seemingly simple question: what should it be named?

VOTE HERE: https://t.co/31xp4XIlJz

With proposals sparking arguments across social media and political circles, three prominent figures have surfaced as the top choices: Donald Trump, Jimmy Buffett, and Hank Aaron.

The Case for Donald J. Trump

The push to name the new crossing after the former president began when some Alabama Republicans suggested honoring Donald Trump.

Proponents of this choice point to similar moves in other states, such as Tennessee’s recent legislative decision to rename a portion of an I-40 bridge after Trump. For supporters, naming a massive piece of Southern infrastructure after Trump is a fitting tribute to his political movement and impact.

Critics argue that public infrastructure should not serve as a monument to highly polarizing, active political figures. Opponents also note that Trump is not an Alabama native and has no direct ties to the Mobile area.

The Case for Jimmy Buffett

Looking for a less polarizing alternative, State Senator Chris Elliott, who represents much of Baldwin County, suggested honoring Gulf Coast music icon Jimmy Buffett instead.

Buffett, who grew up in Mobile and went to school in the area, represents the laid-back, coastal lifestyle synonymous with the region. Senator Chris Elliott and other supporters view Buffett as a unifying, non-political figure whose music brought joy to people of all political stripes. While Pascagoula, Mississippi, already has a small bridge named after Buffett, fans argue that Alabama's massive new gateway is a much more appropriate tribute to his global legacy.

Some skeptics argue that a major state-funded transportation corridor should not be named after a commercial brand or entertainer, though the idea remains highly popular among locals.

The Case for Henry "Hank" Aaron

U.S. Representative Shomari Figures offered a third path, arguing that while he loves Jimmy Buffett, the bridge should be named after Mobile's ultimate homegrown hero: baseball legend Henry "Hank" Aaron.

Born in Mobile's Toulminville neighborhood, Aaron is widely regarded as one of the most famous and impactful figures the city and state have ever produced. Beyond breaking Major League Baseball's all-time home run record in the face of blatant racism and death threats, Aaron was a global icon, athlete, and dedicated philanthropist. Proponents believe naming the bridge after Aaron would honor a true native son who represents resilience and triumph.

Opponents point out that Aaron already has the downtown loop in Mobile named after him. However, supporters counter that a landmark of this scale is a far more fitting tribute to his historic achievements.

Alternative and Compromise Paths

As the debate between MAGA, Margaritaville, and the Home Run King continues, several alternative paths have emerged.

Some locals have suggested a compromise: naming it the Aaron-Buffett Bridge to honor the area's two most celebrated former residents together.

A survey of nearly 1,000 local residents conducted by Downtown Mobile Today revealed that the most popular choice was actually to name it after no person at all. Instead, most respondents preferred simply calling it the Mobile River Bridge. Proponents of this view argue that because the bridge is funded by public tax dollars and represents the entire community, it should be named after the city and the river itself, rather than any individual.

The chart in that post is drawn from a March 2025 survey of 1,005 Jewish Israelis. It was commissioned by Penn State historian Tamir Sorek, fielded by the Israeli firm Geocartography Knowledge Group, and first reported in Haaretz.

The questions measured support for:
Forced expulsion (“transfer”) of Gaza residents
Forced expulsion of Arab citizens of Israel
The idea that the IDF, when taking an enemy city, should act as the Israelites did at Jericho under Joshua — i.e., kill all inhabitants

Overall results reported in the articles:
82% supported expulsion of Gaza residents
56% supported expulsion of Israeli Arabs
47% agreed with the Jericho/killing-all-inhabitants framing

The religious-observance breakdowns on the graphic match the figures circulated from that survey:
Gaza expulsion: Secular 70%, Traditional 91%, Orthodox 90%, Haredi 97%
Israeli Arabs: Secular 38%, Traditional 65%, Orthodox 68%, Haredi 91%
Kill all residents of a conquered city: Secular 31%, Traditional 60%, Orthodox 59%, Haredi 63%

Sorek later published a fuller academic write-up of the same survey (Ethnic and Racial Studies, Dec 2025). Other Israeli polls from the same period found high but not identical support for “evacuation” or “transfer” of Gazans (often in the 60–75% range among Jews, depending on wording and whether “don’t know” was offered). Some analysts argued the Sorek/Geocartography wording and response options produced higher “support” numbers than other instruments.

Jewish teaching and learning have been essential components of Jewish tradition since earliest times. The command to “teach your children” first appeared in Devarim (Deuteronomy) in what later became the Shema — the most central Jewish prayer. Rabbinic literature is filled with references to schools and education, as well as to teaching and learning at every level and for every age, from the youngest children through adulthood. The New York Times has written that the United States has learned nothing from its defeat in Afghanistan, and that its conflict with Iran is now turning into another prolonged war.

The war in Afghanistan ended five years ago. But after the U.S. withdrawal, many of the key fears that had prevented three successive American presidents from leaving proved largely unfounded. Afghanistan did not become the hub for terrorist attacks against the United States that Washington had feared.

The New York Times asks; If the United States is now trying to avoid another prolonged war in Iran, why was it so difficult to leave Afghanistan, and what lessons does the Afghan experience offer for Iran?

According to the newspaper, the United States had a major opportunity to withdraw from Afghanistan in 2011, but chose to continue the war. Eventually, Washington was no longer trying to completely defeat the Taliban. Instead, it focused on reducing American casualties and financial costs while keeping the Afghan government in power, that strategy ultimately failed as well.

The New York Times says the Taliban understood that they did not need to defeat the United States directly. They only needed to sustain a prolonged resistance against U.S. forces and a war-weary American public. Over time, political support for continuing the war weakened in the United States, and Washington eventually lost the conflict.

The article says Iran's current situation has similarities to Afghanistan, but there is one important difference, the stakes and costs for the United States in Iran are much lower than they were in Afghanistan. As a result, the cost of withdrawing from the conflict should also be relatively low.

According to The New York Times, U.S. War Secretary Pete Hegseth had insisted that the war with Iran would not resemble the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan. He described it as fast, limited, lethal and decisive.

However, Iran responded to U.S. attacks by moving to close the Strait of Hormuz. Senior U.S. military officials later acknowledged that airstrikes alone might not be enough to defeat Iran and might not even be sufficient to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Ina Garten was 30, working in a federal budget office in Washington, writing policy papers on nuclear energy.

One April morning in 1978 she was reading the New York Times at her desk and saw an advertisement. A 400 square foot specialty food shop in Westhampton Beach. Twenty-five thousand dollars.

She had no experience in food. She had taught herself to cook at night from Julia Child's books and thrown dinner parties at weekends. That was the whole of her qualification.

She offered 20,000. The owner accepted the same day.

Her line about the Washington job was that it was intellectually exciting and stimulating, and not her at all. The shop was tiny and the work was brutal. She ran it for twenty years, expanded it, and eventually sold it to two employees.

Then she was in her fifties with an office above the shop and nothing particular to do in it. So she wrote a cookbook, mostly to record what the place had been.

The Barefoot Contessa Cookbook came out in 1999. She was 51. It sold in numbers nobody expected and made her a household name in a country she had not been famous in at any point in the previous five decades.

The television show came at 54. She has published more than a dozen books since.

Her advice on changing direction is that people stand at the side of the pond working out what the water will be like. She says to get in.

text:
🚨 IT’S AMAZING THAT ONE WORD CAN SAY THIS MUCH: “BUY.” SONY IS DEFENDING DIGITAL

Sony is currently facing a proposed California class action over the way the PlayStation Store uses words like “Buy Now” and “Confirm Purchase” when what the customer actually receives is a license.

Forget the lawyers for a minute.
Imagine you're 12 years old.

You open the PlayStation Store, find a game you've been wanting, get permission to spend the money and hit a button that says BUY.

What do you think happened?
You bought a game.

The next morning you go to school and tell your friends, “I bought that new game last night.” BRAGGING RIGHTS.

You don't say, “I acquired a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable and potentially revocable license to access software through Sony's ecosystem.”

You're twelve.

But honestly, how many adults talk that way either?

That's what fascinates me about this lawsuit. This isn't about believing that buying a game gives you the copyright, the source code or the right to reproduce it and start selling copies.

Of course it doesn't.

It's about the reasonable expectation that when a company takes your money after putting the word BUY in front of you, something became yours for your personal collection.

And there actually are better ways to handle digital games.

GOG sells DRM-free games with offline installers you can download, back up and keep. You don't need GOG Galaxy running just to prove you're allowed to play them. https://t.co/XYuRYXshF1 doesn't impose platform DRM either, and most releases offer downloadable DRM-free builds.

You still don't own the developer's intellectual property. You can't reproduce the game and sell it.

But you can possess your copy without the storefront having to stand between you and the game every time you want to use it.

That's a HUGE difference.

California law even recognizes that distinction. Its digital-goods law specifically treats permanent offline downloads that the seller cannot later revoke differently from ordinary revocable digital licenses. Are you listening @Sony ?

So maybe the question isn't whether digital ownership is possible.

Maybe the question is how much control companies are willing to give the people handing them the money.

 So,  if “BUY” doesn't mean you're buying something, we probably need to have a much bigger conversation about what that word means in the digital age.

text:
The biggest lesson from BONK GUY @theunipcs is not that he turned $16K into $20M+ on $BONK.

It is the decision making framework behind the trade.

Markets do not reward constant activity.

They reward recognizing asymmetric 
opportunities, developing conviction,

managing risk, and staying rational when everyone else is emotional.

That matters even more in a weak market.

When prices fall and sentiment collapses, people wait for certainty.

They want better macro conditions, a trend reversal, confirmations that the bottom is in.

But markets rarely offer certainty before an opportunity reprices.

By the time the market feels safe, the opportunity may already be gone.

So what would BONK GUY do?

Not blindly buy or blindly sell or blindly wait.

He would look for conviction. How?

1. Build a Thesis first. 

Emotion is one of the most expensive inputs in trading.

Fear creates premature exits.

Greed creates oversized positions.

FOMO creates entries without a thesis.

Panic turns volatility into bad decisions.

The solution:

Have a reason to enter. 
A reason to stay. 
And a reason to leave.

Know why you believe the asset is mispriced, what could make the thesis play out, what would invalidate it, and how much risk you can realistically tolerate.

A red candle is not automatically thesis invalidation.

Neither is FUD.

Price movement is information, not necessarily an argument against your thesis.

2. Conviction beats constant reaction: 

Strong traders do not react to every candle.

They react to meaningful changes in information.

If your thesis depends on price going up immediately, you do not have conviction.

You have hope.

Real conviction allows you to distinguish between:

“The market is temporarily against me.”

and

“My thesis is objectively wrong.”

One requires patience.

The other requires action.

Knowing the difference is an edge.

3. Do not confuse conviction with leverage! 

The lesson from BONK GUY is not to use more leverage.

It is almost the opposite.

Leverage can make being directionally correct irrelevant by forcing you out before your thesis has time to play out.

Copy the framework, not the position size.

You do not need maximum exposure. 

You need enough exposure to matter without taking so much risk that one bad move removes you from the game.

Survival comes before upside.

4. What would the Bonk Guy be doing rn in today’s market? 

He would likely focus on situations where market perception and underlying potential have meaningfully diverged.

Look for:

•Excessive pessimism.
•Strong or improving fundamentals.
•A compelling catalyst or narrative.
•Significant upside relative to downside.
•Manageable risk.
•A thesis strong enough to survive volatility.

The goal is not to predict the exact bottom.

It is to identify asymmetric opportunities before consensus returns.

Because once consensus returns, the asymmetry usually disappears.

The Bigger lesson is this, there are two dangerous extremes:

- Blind aggression: buying everything because prices are down.

- Complete paralysis: refusing to act because conditions are uncertain.

The better approach is simple:

Be selective, patient, then be decisive.

You do not need to know exactly when the market will turn.

You need to know what you believe, why you believe it, what would prove you wrong, and whether the current price justifies the risk.

That is the real BONK GUY lesson.

Not buy the dip, or hold forever, or use leverage.

Is the BONK GUY sitting on his hands in this market?

No, he’s not! but he’s also not blindly pressing every button either.

He waits for his setup, builds conviction then makes decisions quickly!

☑️ Big‑game experience

He also knows:
❌ No more off‑field dramas.

✊ Carrick’s style:

💘 The affection is still there:

  ▶️ The goals, the big nights  
- They also remember:
  ⏺️ The fallout with Amorim  
  ⏺️ The loans and public doubts

Retired chemical engineer, he began his quest to find and preserve lost apple varieties around more than 25 years ago. 

The man who owns an apple orchard called Heritage Apples in Clemmons, North Carolina, USA has re-discovered over 1000 rare varieties of apples.

His Heritage Apples showcase at least 600 of them. He has been working so that the heirloom apples of Appalachia in the Eastern United States do not disappear with time.

Popularly known as the Apple-Hunter, Tom grows around 60 varieties of apples each year on his farm and sells around 1000 trees. text:
In 1988 Dolly Parton pulled every 7th and 8th grader in Sevier County into a room and told them to pick a buddy. 

She made them sign a contract.. if BOTH graduate, she hands you both $500. One fails, nobody gets paid.

The county dropout rate went from 35% to 6%.

She handed out the checks herself.

In 1989 she offered $500 to every kid in the county who wanted to go to the local college. 

When Gatlinburg burned in 2016, she sent 900 families $1,000 a month for six months.

You've probably heard that part. 

Here's the part you haven't: 

The fund raised more than expected, so she showed up in May and handed every one of those families another $5,000 on top. 

Then she quietly put $3 million into the recovery group that handles the years after the news trucks leave.

She built her county an entire hospital. 

She played a benefit concert in 2007, Dollywood and the Stampede matched it, and LeConte Medical Center opened in 2010 with a birthing unit and a women's center in it.

In 2022 she started covering 100% of tuition, books, and fees for Dollywood employees. 

Full-time, part-time, AND seasonal. 

In 1991 she paid for a bald eagle sanctuary because the birds couldn't be released back into the wild, no press release.

And when Hurricane Helene came through here in Western North Carolina, she wrote a personal check for $1 million and her companies matched it. 

She didn't owe North Carolina anything, but she helped us anyway.

She started the Imagination Library because her daddy couldn't read or write. Before he passed, he told her it was the most important thing she ever did.

Rest in Peace, Dolly 🇺🇸

text:
He said the fifth thing most members never do is call the property directly and ask the question that changes everything: "What rooms do you have available tonight?"

He said this works at Marriott more reliably than at most chains — because the Marriott system auto-assigns the lowest-category room that matches your reservation, and the front desk agent can override it.

"When you check in, the system gives you the standard room the algorithm selected. Standard king. Low floor. Parking lot side. That's the default for every guest — including elite members, unless the property's system automatically processes an upgrade. But the system doesn't always auto-upgrade. It depends on the property, the night, and the occupancy."

He said calling the property 24 hours before arrival is more effective than any status tier.

"Call the hotel's direct phone number — not the Marriott 800 line. The 800 number connects you to a call center. The property line connects you to someone standing in the building who can see real-time inventory. Say: 'Hi, I have a reservation for tomorrow under [name]. I'm a Bonvoy [tier] member. I was wondering if there are any complimentary upgrades or premium rooms available for my stay. I'm flexible and grateful for anything you can offer.'"

He said tone matters more than tier.

Exactly optimized doesn't just mean getting high frame rates...

It means reaching your gameplay and visual goals running at the best target resolutions and frame rates that can still achieve it.

A game can be only 30 FPS and still be optimized based on the truly "next generation" experience it delivers and another could be running at a perfect 60 FPS and still be considered severely unoptimized based on how little their game is actually achieving.

The word optimized gets thrown around way too much without taking into account that it's all about a balance between the performance of your game versus the complexity and overall experience it offers for it.

text:
1. Most extreme and unrealistic elements

24-hour removal for all new arrivals.

The paper wants anyone arriving illegally processed and deported within 24 hours, with no individualised assessment. This is simply operationally impossible for the great majority of nationalities, since obtaining travel documents, verifying identity and country of origin, and securing a receiving state's agreement routinely takes weeks or months, and the document's own Section on returns agreements admits Britain has formal arrangements with only 7 countries and informal ones with 17 more, while 75% of illegal entrants in 2024 came from countries with no agreement at all. The 24-hour figure isn't a policy, it's a slogan.

Retrospective revocation of already-granted asylum.

All 56,605 people who received asylum or protection status after Channel crossings since 2018 would have that status stripped and be deported, no individual reassessment, no distinction for people who arrived as children a decade ago and have since built lives, families, or careers here. Revoking lawfully acquired status en masse, retroactively, is one of the more legally and ethically extreme proposals in the document.

Detention capacity to increase nearly sevenfold (2,200 to 15,000 beds).

They calim this would be achieved by using decommissioned RAF bases as physical sites, several closed for 30 years with no assessment of the state of their infrastructure, security perimeters, water, sewage, or healthcare provision, alongside the odd move of costing this against the 2020 London ExCeL Nightingale hospital conversion, a temporary medical facility with none of the security, legal-visit, or long-term custody requirements a detention estate needs, before the document itself concedes "such a gainful capacity-to-cost ratio is unlikely to be obtainable in the construction of detention facilities." The disclaimer arrives after the headline number has already done its work.

"Deportation NATO."

A proposed coalition of the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and multiple EU states subordinating their own bilateral relationships with India, Nigeria, Pakistan and others to a British-led sanctions ladder, with zero discussion of what Britain offers these partners in return, why they'd accept the reputational and diplomatic cost of joining, or what happens when their own migration priorities conflict with Britain's. Borrowing NATO's name lends the appearance of an existing, credible alliance structure to what is, at this stage, a wish-list.

2. Ethically alarming elements

A cash-reward whistleblowing scheme (£500 to £2,500 per successful tip) to encourage the public to report neighbours, colleagues, and tenants, on top of the existing hostile-environment architecture (NHS, banking, housing, employment).

Financially incentivising surveillance of your own community is a significant escalation, and creates an obvious incentive for malicious or racially-motivated false reporting, since a reward is paid on "verified intelligence," but the initial report, not the outcome, is what drives the behaviour being encouraged.

Children's welfare barely appears. The Immigration and Asylum Act repeal list explicitly targets legislation forcing the Home Office to consider "the best interests of the dependants of immigrants," dismissed as "a sentimental statute." Combined with the hostile-environment measures on healthcare, housing and homelessness, which carve out no exceptions for minors, this is a policy programme that would apply eviction and destitution pressure to families with children as a matter of design.

The Home Office's own 2018 data-sharing plan to extract non-medical information from NHS and GP records was abandoned after public and clinical opposition (GPs warned it would deter people from seeking care for communicable diseases). The report calls for its revival "in phases," beginning with areas with the highest suspected populations, without engaging with why it was dropped in the first place.

A 25% remittance tax and a dividend tax aimed at putting economic pressure on individuals and foreign governments alike, justified partly by pointing out that Nigeria derives close to 6% of GDP from remittances, is presented as leverage over a government, but its immediate effect falls on migrant workers and their families abroad, often among the poorest people affected by any part of this plan.

3. Likely ineffective and under-costed

The plan's own cost-benefit arithmetic barely breaks even. Total direct costs are given as £49-57.6bn over five years, roughly £10-11.5bn a year. Total claimed savings are "at least £12.5bn a year." That's a wafer-thin margin for a programme this disruptive, and it is achieved by treating enforcement, detention and diplomatic coalition costs as a "one-off," while the savings side draws on a static per-migrant cost figure lifted from a 2023 impact assessment built for a different bill, applied uncritically to a rounded, conveniently-total 1.5 million adults and 300,000 children, numbers that sum precisely to the document's own preferred 1.8 million headline estimate. That precision from admittedly uncertain population data should at least raise an eyebrow.

Rwanda is used as a template despite its own numbers undermining the case. By the document's own account, the scheme cost £715m and, when scaled up, was projected to reach nearly £4bn, all without a single deportee ultimately removed under it. The paper doesn't mention that the scheme was found unlawful by the UK Supreme Court over Rwanda's safety as a destination, a legal and factual finding, not merely a matter of insufficiently aggressive human-rights law that a future Parliament could simply override.

The remittance tax likely undermines itself. Elsewhere the document acknowledges that enforcement against the "black economy" is limited because "there are alternatives to traditional banking spanning from cash-in-hand to informal networks," yet proposes a 25% remittance tax as a serious £3bn/year revenue and leverage tool without addressing that a tax this size gives people a strong incentive to move to exactly those informal channels the paper has just flagged as unstoppable.

The deportation flight calculations assumes commercial partners' full cooperation. Chartering 600 flights a year (up from 60) and doubling the average deportees per flight assumes airlines will accept reputational risk and logistical strain at scale, and that origin countries will keep accepting these flights even as diplomatic and remittance pressure escalates against them, two assumptions in some tension with each other.

4. Rhetorical tricks and misleading framing

Motivated statistical sourcing.

The claim that "one in 13" Londoners is an illegal immigrant comes from a debunked Thames Water market analysis intended to model water demand, not a demographic study, based on 2017 data the report itself calls outdated, then used as a springboard to assert the true figure is "no doubt a great deal higher," turning an acknowledged weakness in the source into license for an upward guess rather than a reason for caution.

Precision theatre.

Detailed statistics (£1.75 per RtW check, £600,931.46 per fine, 87.4% compliance rates) are deployed throughout to create an impression of rigorous costing, while the two largest single cost items in the entire plan, the £30bn Immigration Enforcement budget and the £1.5bn/year Rwanda-style third-country provision, are given as round, top-line figures with no comparable itemisation.

"Deportation NATO" as branding.

Naming a proposed coalition after an existing, binding, mutual-defence treaty organisation implies a level of pre-existing alignment and institutional machinery that doesn't exist, priming the reader to think of this as extending something real rather than inventing something from nothing.

The population estimate dispute is resolved by assertion.

The highly respected and professional Migration Observatory's revised, lower estimate (700,000-900,000) is dismissed in a single sentence as based on a "faulty understanding," with no methodological rebuttal offered, before the paper adopts its own higher figure (1.8-2 million) as the basis for every subsequent calculation in the document.

The "nothing can be done" framing in the conclusion pre-empts practical objections by casting them as bad-faith fatalism ("a brazen political power-play posing as an anti-political assessment") rather than engaging with the specific operational objections raised throughout by the sources the paper itself cites, including its own admissions about detention-cost comparisons being unrealistic and the black economy being resistant to banking enforcement.

Framing repeal of the Equality Act and mass rights-stripping as restoration rather than removal. 

Throughout, withdrawing hard-won democratic legal protections is described as "clearing obstacles," "restoring sovereignty," or "reasserting" a status quo ante, language that frames the removal of existing legal safeguards which protect millions of ordinary lawful British and foreign citizens as a 'return to normalcy' rather than as the elimination of protections that currently exist.

Lowe is a twenty-first century Oswald Mosley, with the key difference being that Mosley wasn't supported and amplified by the richest man in the world.

text:
LADY'S DREAM iPHONE TURNS NIGHTMARE AFTER "TOO GOOD TO BE TRUE" ONLINE DEAL

Vipi, Mondayly? 

Najua Mkwanja iliingia last week. Mmelipwa? 😊 Pia msupport biz za Mbogi wenye hawako kwa monthly pension.

 Sio? 

Weekend ilikuwa aje?

 I hope ManU hawakuchoma tena. Kama kawa niko hapa kuwachanua kabla you make ile kitu ya fake phone...

Kuna huyu Ndranya, 24 years, kaumbwa kaumbika, complete with black synthetic wig. She had just secured her first job and ready to cop the iPhone of her dreams. Ogopa mayuts with dreams!! When the long awaited pay finally landed, aliwaste no time. Nobody can stop Emma! She contacted a smooth talking online seller, Voke wa Madeals, who promised a "clean, almost new" iPhone at a price too good to ignore. No receipt. No original box papers. Just a quick meet up behind a petrol station and a handshake.

Ni deal si deal?

Plot 10 itajua aje kuna new member of the iPhone gang? Ringtone iko design ya nganya style volume that could wake the dead. Kidogo kidogo, Bunge la Plot ndiyo hiyo! "Ati huyu msichana anafikiria sisi hatuwezi afford simu?" furious Mama Otis asked while holding mahindi boiro. Wa Kefini complained the phone was shouting louder than makanga wa Railways. Naliaka mama fua, hii sauti is louder than Wafula wa Jeevanjee, while Jecinta wa Mothers Union wondered if the high voltage volume this early in the morning was calling the angels or summoning demons.

The disturbance became the talk of the plot. Mutina and Bosco barked in protest. Even Atasa's sound effects were being overshadowed.

Unknown to Emma, the shiny iPhone she was proudly flaunting had a dark past. Our boys from the Serious Crimes Unit had been trailing the device after it was reported stolen from a murder victim whose body had been discovered weeks earlier along the Eastern Bypass.

And so, our boys arrived kwa scene "Emma's (Gatangi-one bedroom)" na automobile which can pack up to 300 hp and sprint from 0 to 100Km/h in as little as 7.2 seconds in its most legendary forms! but our boys are humble to brag on earthly materials while their happiness ni-kuserve raia.

Hodi! Hodi!

The neighbours fell silent.

Emma stepped out dressed ile style ya Ngoma ya Matata na Sauti. A few words exchanged. All she could offer were WhatsApp chats and a vague: "I bought it online from a guy called Voke wa Madeals." One neighbour, who had been convinced the officers had finally come to deal with the high voltage noise, slowly realised the noise was not the problem. The phone was. Naliaka was overheard saying, "At least the high voltage noise has gone to jail. Sasa ni time yetu for some high voltage horizontal engineering noise."

As we speak, Emma is enjoying an all expenses paid stay at one of our gated communities as investigations into the murder continue.

Mondaylys, we love a good deal but sometimes deals ni mingi. When buying second-hand gadgets, rushing to grab a bargain without checking properly can land you in real trouble. Ukifanyiwa deal, pia kagua. Buy from authorised sellers. 

Verify before you pay.

🇧🇩🇨🇳 Bangladesh Moves Forward with J-10CE Fighter Acquisition

Bangladesh’s initiative to acquire Chinese J-10CE multirole fighter aircraft is emerging as a significant step in the modernisation of the Bangladesh Air Force.

The acquisition process for the Chengdu J-10CE, the export variant of China’s J-10 fighter, is reportedly progressing. The aircraft is a 4th-generation multirole platform capable of conducting both air-to-air and air-to-ground missions.

Reports indicate that Bangladesh is considering the acquisition of up to 20 J-10CEs, with a potential programme value of around US$2.3 billion. However, the final number of aircraft, contract value and delivery schedule have not yet been officially confirmed and remain subject to negotiations.

The modernisation effort reportedly extends beyond fighter aircraft, with Bangladesh also pursuing attack helicopters, VIP transport helicopters and UAV systems. If implemented, these acquisitions could strengthen the country’s capabilities in air defence, aerial surveillance, reconnaissance and military operations.

With the Bangladesh Air Force already operating a substantial fleet of Chinese-origin combat aircraft, including F-7 variants and MiG-29s, the introduction of the J-10CE could offer some advantages in terms of existing Chinese defence-industrial familiarity, training and logistics. Nevertheless, integrating a modern fighter fleet would require significant investment in pilot training, weapons, maintenance infrastructure, ground support systems and long-term sustainment.

The J-10CE acquisition, if finalised, would represent one of the most significant upgrades to Bangladesh’s combat aviation capability in recent years.

Sources: Daily Sabah, Anadolu Agency & Reuters
