text:
Dropbox co-founder Drew Houston: "Surrounding yourself with people who inspire you is now just as important as being talented or working hard."

Speaking at MIT, Drew gives the school direct credit for the existence of his company:

"MIT is one of the best places in the world to start building that circle. Because if I hadn't come here, I never would have met Adam, I never would have met my amazing co-founder, Arash, and there would be no Dropbox."

His argument isn't that talent doesn't matter. It's that talent without the right people around it goes nowhere. He makes the point with an analogy:

"Can you like imagine if Michael Jordan hadn't been in the NBA? Like if his circle of five were like a bunch of guys in Italy or something? Like, I don't think we'd be seeing him on Wheaties boxes. And so that's the point. Like, your circle pushes you to be better, just like Adam pushed me."

Which leads to the part most people get wrong, geography:

"And where you live matters. There's only one MIT, and there's only one Hollywood, and there's only one Silicon Valley. And this isn't a coincidence. For whatever you're doing, there's one place in the world where the best people go, and you should go there. Don't settle for anywhere else."

He also expands the definition of a circle beyond people you actually know:

"Being able to meet my heroes and learn from them gave me a huge advantage, so your heroes are part of your circle, too. So follow them."

Then he names the second trap: getting ready.

"Don't get me wrong, learning is still your top priority. It's the most important thing you can do, but the way you do it changes. From now on, the fastest way to learn is by doing."

"Otherwise, if you have a dream, you can spend a lifetime planning for it, and studying for it, and getting ready for it. What you should be doing is getting started. Honestly, I don't think I've ever been ready."

He offers himself as the evidence. Just after moving to San Francisco, his investors committed:

"I remember the day that our investors said, 'Yes, we want to invest. Where do we send the money?' And so for a 24-year-old, this is like Christmas, right?"

"And opening your present is like running over to your computer on Monday morning and refreshing https://t.co/SGEZYneiUI and watching your company's checking account go from like $60 to $1.2 million. And I'm like, 'Oh my god, this is amazing. Like, that number has two commas in it.'"

Two ideas, one underlying principle: the things that actually determine your trajectory are external and environmental, not internal and preparatory.

Who you're around beats how hard you're grinding. Starting beats studying. Both are decisions about where you place yourself. In a room, in a city, in the middle of an unfinished thing, rather than decisions about how much more you can optimise yourself in private first.

Drew never felt ready. He wired himself into the right circle and started anyway.

text:
White Sox @ Astros 08/31/26 · 8:10 PM ET.

Chicago's Elo (1533) sits 59 points above Houston's (1474) — a meaningful gap — and the Sox have scored 648 runs this season against Houston's 616, averaging 5 per game to the Astros' 3.9. But the starting pitching flips that picture. Peter Lambert carries a 3.66 ERA and 1.23 WHIP against Anthony Kay's 4.09 ERA and 1.34 WHIP. Lambert also zones the ball more — 46.5% in-zone vs. Kay's 44.1 — and holds a tighter barrel% allowed (6.3 vs. 8.1). The real tension is contact quality: Houston's team exit velo is 91.6 mph against Chicago's 86.9, and the Astros' chase% (38.7) suggests they'll offer Kay enough rope. Lambert's barrel% vs. RHB (7.1) is his softer spot, and Chicago's Miguel Vargas leads an offense trending up one on the scoring stretch. Carlos Correa remains on IL for Houston, stripping their infield core. Kay actually limits LHB barrels well (3.2%) — relevant if Houston's lineup skews that way without Correa. Rotation advantage leans Houston on paper; run-scoring volume and Elo lean Chicago. Which way are you leaning? What is the model missing? The actual prediction is in the app.

text:
Robinhood Chain

Robinhood Chain is a permissionless Ethereum Layer-2 (built on Arbitrum Orbit / Dedicated Blockchains tech) launched by Robinhood on mainnet on July 1, 2026. 
It was designed primarily for tokenized real-world assets (RWAs) - especially Stock Tokens (on-chain economic exposure to equities like NVDA, AAPL, GOOG, etc., available 24/7 via Robinhood Wallet in 120+ countries, but generally not to U.S. persons and structured as debt securities without underlying ownership rights) - plus DeFi primitives, lending, and AI-agent friendly infrastructure.

It uses ETH for gas, targets ~100ms block times, is fully EVM-compatible (standard Solidity tools work), has first-come-first-served sequencing (no priority-fee MEV buying), settles to Ethereum, and is open for anyone to deploy contracts or bridge assets. 
Partners at/near launch included Uniswap (dedicated AMM), Morpho (lending), Chainlink, BitGo, Alchemy, LayerZero. Robinhood Earn offers ~7% APY on USDG (self-custody lending, insured elements via Morpho).

Rapid Growth and Current Snapshot (as of late August 2026)

The chain saw explosive early traction:
- High daily transactions (often millions to 10M+), active addresses, and it occasionally overtook Base in users or activity metrics.
- DEX volume in the billions cumulative early on, with strong 24h volumes (hundreds of millions to $1B+ range recently).
- TVL has grown steadily into the hundreds of millions (recent figures around $700M+ DeFi TVL, with stablecoin supply also substantial, including USDG and USDe). 
Robinhood positions it as a way to onboard its large retail base into on-chain finance without them fully leaving the app/wallet ecosystem, with an “AI-native” angle for agents.

The Memecoin Phenomenon

Despite the RWA focus, memecoins quickly dominated early activity and volume (often 75–80%+ of DEX volume in the first weeks). This is a classic new-chain pattern (similar to Base or others): low fees, fast blocks, easy deployment, and hype draw speculative capital first.

 - CASHCAT (Cash Cat) was the clear breakout flagship - named after a rejected early company name idea from the founders. It launched shortly after mainnet, pumped hard (thousands of % in places, peak market cap reports in the $150–200M+ range), generated massive volume, and remains a top traded token by cumulative metrics. It has since corrected significantly from highs (still subject to volatility and listings, including later on Robinhood itself in some reports). Other themed tokens (Hood-related, dogs, etc.) followed.
- Launchpads (early dominant ones like NOXA, later Pons and others) enabled rapid token creation—tens of thousands of launches in short windows, with creator fees in the millions. Many tokens go to near-zero quickly.
- Cumulative memecoin trading and launches are in the hundreds of thousands of tokens tracked in analytics dashboards. Volume has been high enough to put the chain in top rankings for DEX activity at times, though fees per dollar traded tend to be lower than Solana or BNB.

CEO Vlad Tenev initially downplayed pure memes without utility, then acknowledged the chain “works great for memes too.”

Applying the teachings and wisdom of Jesus to conversations about cutting-edge technology—like AGI, 100x code efficiency, and humanoid robots—provides a powerful framework for keeping our focus grounded in human dignity, ethics, and truth. [1, 2]
A Christian worldview offers several foundational principles to guide how we process these massive technological shifts: [1, 2]

1. Prioritizing Human Value Over Machine Utility
Jesus consistently elevated the marginalized and taught that individuals have immense, inherent worth. In the Bible, humans are uniquely described as being made in the Image of God (Imago Dei). [1, 2, 3]
•The Application: As AI systems scale to do human work, a Jesus-centered perspective reminds us that a person's worth is not defined solely by their economic productivity or efficiency. Technology should be used as a tool to serve human flourishing and alleviate suffering, rather than as a replacement for human value. [1, 2, 3]

2. Seeking Deep Truth vs. Automated Convenience
Jesus described himself as "the way, the truth, and the life." He often spoke in parables, encouraging people to wrestle with deep concepts, ask questions, and seek true understanding. [1, 2]
•The Application: In an era where AI can generate instant answers, essays, and shortcuts, we face the risk of choosing convenience over character. The wisdom of Jesus suggests that the process of learning, struggling, and seeking truth builds spiritual maturity and critical thinking that an automated shortcut cannot replicate.[1, 2]

3. Emphasizing Real Community Over Digital Disconnection
Jesus modeled deeply embodied relationships, physically spending time with people, eating with them, and building community. He taught that the greatest commandments are to love God and love your neighbor as yourself. [1]
•The Application: As tech companies build increasingly lifelike humanoid robots and digital companions, it is easy for society to drift toward isolation. Applying Jesus’ wisdom means actively protecting real-world, physical relationships, recognizing that an algorithmic loop or a mechanical entity cannot replace the sacred nature of genuine human connection and empathy. [1, 2, 3]

4. Exercising Humble and Just Stewardship
Jesus frequently warned against the blind pursuit of power, pride, and hubris, advocating instead for humility and justice. [1, 2]
•The Application: The race to build massive AI data centers consumes enormous amounts of electricity and water, often straining local communities. A faith-based approach to innovation champions just stewardship, ensuring that tech advancements do not exploit natural resources or leave vulnerable populations behind. [1, 2, 3, 4]

text:
Most of the defense tech founders or LMM PE-backed CEOs we work with don't have much experience in hiring senior members of their team (VPs, C-suite, P&L owning GM, etc). 

Example: One of our clients is doing an industry rollup. They have a killer deal team and the CEO has decades of industry experience. He's hired and fired hundreds of people.  

But most of those were ICs or managers. 

He told us: 

"I have maybe a few reps hiring an executive." 

You can get to a $15-$30M business and may have only made a big-time hire on a few occasions. 

So here are some words I share with them as we talk strategy for a big hire:  

1. You need to make this a priority.  

That means time on the calendar to review candidates. Interviews scheduled in a timely manner. Feedback given promptly.  

Talent at this level is not going to wait around for you. They have options and you are not the only one. 

This doesn't mean rush into it, but it does mean you need to act with a sense of urgency and make it a priority on the calendar. Can also mean having a trusted agent (CoS, COO, HR Director) as the project manager to keep things moving. 

---

2. Your HR/TA team may not be cut out for this. 

I see this a lot.  

A defense tech startup has a recruiting team, but their experience is in highly technical roles- not a Head of GTM for SOCOM. 

It is a different motion/skill and you may need a different tool. 

---

3. You are likely going to market with comp that is not market reality.  

The pay package you used to land a VP in 2021 is no longer viable.  

Candidates are getting more market data about comp and are taking that to the negotiating table. 

We usually see that the offer that wins is 10-20% higher than the one they set out with. 

---

4. You need to check references.  

And do not call their current employer (seriously). 

My favorite question: "Would you rehire them again? Why or why not?" 

---

5. You need to recruit.  

The best leaders always have an eye out for talent and are looking for great people.  And they go after them once they are in their sights. 

ABR

Always.
Be.
Recruiting.

4. Wake in Brahma Muhurta and sit quietly for 10 minutes — aligns the mind before Rahu-Ketu confusion starts the day.

5. Feed needy hungry ppl before your main meal — simple daily seva that classical texts prescribe for Shani and Pitra.

6. Chant Maha Mrityunjaya or Om Namah Shivaya 108 times — the traditional shield for Kaal Sarp fear and sudden shocks.

7. Fast lightly on Tuesday or Saturday — discipline is the cheapest, oldest upaya for Mars and Saturn.

8. Light a ghee or mustard-oil lamp at dusk — steadies the grahas at sandhya, when the chart’s shadows are loudest.

9. Serve parents, teachers, and workers without keeping score — Jupiter and Saturn both quiet down when duty is done cleanly.

Doshas describe patterns, not a life sentence. Charts vary, cancellations exist, and a priest or jyotishi can still help for a specific kundli. These habits are the daily upayas texts keep repeating when people get stuck fearing Manglik, Kaal Sarp, Sade Sati, or Pitra Dosh. Consistency beats one expensive puja.

text:
We divided the biscuits into portions small enough to make hunger feel insulting. Alina insisted that I eat more because I was doing most of the climbing and cutting, but on the third day I caught her pretending she had already eaten when her portion was still hidden beneath a folded piece of canvas. I placed half my food in her hand and said we would divide everything equally from then on, including fear, work, and bad decisions. She almost argued, then quietly ate, and that was the first time I realized she was beginning to trust me rather than simply manage me.

The nights were harder than the days because darkness made the island seem larger and rescue seem less likely. Every sound became a threat—a branch breaking, waves striking rock, wings moving above the trees—and neither of us slept for more than an hour at a time. Alina would sometimes wake suddenly and search the shadows as though expecting to find someone who had disappeared years before. Whenever I asked what she had heard, she would say, “Nothing,” but her voice carried the unmistakable weight of a memory.

On the fifth day, another storm pushed inland and tore half our shelter from the ground. Alina climbed onto a fallen trunk to secure the canvas, slipped on the wet bark, and landed badly on her left ankle. She tried to stand immediately, angered by her own pain, but her leg gave way and I caught her before she fell again. I carried her beneath the remaining shelter, wrapped the swelling with cloth, and listened as she apologized three times for becoming “a liability,” as though injuries were failures that needed to be explained.

“You have nothing to apologize for,” I told her, tightening the bandage carefully. “You got hurt while trying to protect both of us, and that does not make you weak.” Alina stared at me for several seconds, and I understood that people had probably praised her success thousands of times but rarely offered her compassion without asking for something in return. When the rain grew louder, she turned her face away and whispered, “You don’t know how long it has been since someone said that to me.”

That night, she told me about her husband, Thomas, who had died six years earlier after a highway accident during a winter storm. They had argued that morning because she had canceled another weekend together for work, and when he called later, she had silenced the phone while presenting to investors. By the time she returned the call, a police officer answered. Alina knew logically that answering would not have prevented the accident, but grief did not care about logic; it had convinced her that loving someone meant eventually failing them, so she built a life where no one could accuse her of needing too much.

text:
The Holy Name Society Roadmap for personal holiness 💪

After joining the HNS, I was given a framework of daily habits to help cast off sin and cultivate virtue. It was such a wealth of practical advice, and I am privileged to share some of it with you!

1. The Morning Routine ☀️

BEDTIME: The most important decision you will make is what time you go to bed each night. By sticking to a bedtime, you will dispose yourself to wake up on time and to pray well.

UPON WAKING UP: Make the Sign of the Cross, recognize the presence of God, and say your Morning Offering.

The Morning Offering is crucial, as this is when we offer our entire day to God and express our intent to receive all possible indulgences.

MORNING PRAYERS: The quiet of early morning is typically the ideal time for spiritual exercises. At a minimum, you should recite prayers of your choosing, do some spiritual reading, and spend a few minutes in mental prayer.

Some typical morning prayers might be the Our Father, three Hail Mary's, Glory Be, and the Acts of Faith, Hope, and Charity.

MAKE A RESOLUTION: Being properly disposed to God's grace, you should now make a specific resolution for improvement that day. Perhaps resolve to overcome a habitual sin, or to cultivate some virtue.

2. Throughout the day ⏰

FAMILY PRAYER: If you have a family, spend time together reciting some chosen family prayers before starting the day.

THE ANGELUS: As close as possible to the times of 6:00 AM, Noon, and 6:00 PM, recite the Angelus. During Paschaltide, the Angelus is replaced with the Regina Coeli.

MEALS: It is best to set aside specific times of the day for eating. Of course, you should recite the customary prayer before and after meals each time.

BEFORE WORK: Before beginning an activity, recite an appropriate prayer (such as the Actiones Nostras) or invoke an associated Saint.

BEFORE TRAVEL: Begin each car trip with a simple prayer (like the Hail Mary), invoking your Guardian Angel, Our Lady of the Way, and Saint Christopher.

YOUR RESOLUTION: Call to mind your resolution throughout the day, as well as the presence of God.

3. The Brown Scapular 🤎

The graces associated with the Brown Scapular of Our Lady of Mount Carmel are abundant. People come with all kinds of excuses to not wear it. Just get enrolled and wear it daily!

4. Daily Rosary 📿

The Holy Rosary should be at the heart of our prayer life. Establish a fixed time to pray the Rosary and stick to it. In the family context, this should be so ingrained in your home's routine that everyone just shows up for it at the appointed time.

The Rosary is not something to "fit in." Everything else should fit around this time spent with Our Lady.

5. Evening Routine 🌙

This is when we look back on the day and prepare ourselves for the night and tomorrow.

As stated earlier, it is crucial to go to bed on time. You should try to start your evening prayers at a fixed time each day.

HOLY WATER: Bless yourself (and if applicable, your family).

PRAYER: Choose suitable prayers to recite each night. Some typical evening prayers might be the three Hail Mary's, the Act of Resignation, and the Memorare.

EXAMEN: Examine yourself with respect to your dominant fault, habitual sins, and progress in virtue. Did you make progress on your resolution?

Conclude your examen with the Act of Contrition.

SIGN OF THE CROSS: Bless yourself before bed and think of a pious thought as you drift to sleep.

6. Weekly Routine: Holy Mass ⛪

You should orient each week towards its summit: Sunday Mass.

Traditionally the Church required us to abstain from flesh meat on Fridays. We do well to take up this weekly practice.

7. Monthly Routine: Confession 🗓️

We should strive to avail ourselves of the Sacrament of Penance at least once a month. Many spiritual writers consider biweekly to be the ideal practice.

Our daily practices, especially our nightly examen, should be tied to our preparation for confession.

8. Annual Routine: The Liturgical Year ⏳

Make sure you own (and use!) a liturgical calendar.

Be aware of the Church's liturgical seasons (Advent, Pentecost, Lent, etc) and their associated devotions. Keep track of upcoming feasts in honor of Our Lord, Our Lady, and the Saints.

Holy Mother Church also provides Ember Days and Rogation days as opportunities for penance.

Take note of the Holy Days of Obligation for each year and do your best to schedule time off of work for them!

YOUR RULE OF LIFE

These daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly spiritual practices constitute a "Rule of Life" for yourself, and perhaps your family.

Don't let pride trick you into doing everything at once. Pick one habit, do it for a week, and then add another.

To define and live by a such a Rule is foolproof way of growing in holiness and staying on the path toward Heaven!

text:
Flame-Chaser, Burning Devotion — The Tale of Blazehound🔥
 
Across the hills and open wilds of Carlocia, you will often spot packs of Blazehound roaming together. Evolved from Growlithe, these fire‑spirited jinies bear their iconic fluttering red scarves around their necks. Their golden manes and tail‑plumes billow in the wind; when their fighting spirit ignites, their crests and tails blaze like dancing flames. They run with the gallant grace of ancient warriors, warm gusts of wind sweeping across the grasslands in their wake.
 
Blazehound are born pack‑loving creatures. In the wild, they wander in small groups, scaling hills and trotting across meadows side by side, playing and resting in warm companionship. Yet the moment they lay eyes on a Little Roco, their whole world shifts toward you. Even wild ones are irresistibly affectionate. They will bound toward you, following your footsteps closely, never wanting to stray far from your side.
 
They possess a delightfully headstrong streak.
Should another spirit draw near to shower you with affection, they grow jealous. Putting on a show of solemn dignity, they gently nudge other creatures away, craving to claim your fondness all for themselves. Yet among their own kin, they lay down their guard, frolicking and nuzzling beside you in a joyful cluster. In quiet moments, they roll onto their backs and expose their soft bellies, showing you their most vulnerable, tender side. On rainy days, seeing you soaked through, they will kindle a gentle, mild flame to dry the dampness from your clothes, thoughtful and gentle to the core.
 
Most amusing of all is their almost possessive urge to become your mount.
Even if you are already riding another Jini, a wild Rapidash will come charging over. It will boldly shoulder aside your current steed, then lower its body of its own accord, insisting that you climb onto its back. It yearns to journey alongside humans, and requires little taming. Offer it kindness, and it will gladly bear you across the land. It races like the wind, carrying you through woodlands and over mountain ridges, unfolding before your eyes the beauty of sunset fields, drifting clouds and mountain vistas.
 
For all their lively, impetuous nature, they carry a noble guardian spirit in battle.
Deep within them lies an instinct to protect their companion. When danger draws near, they will step bravely before you, blazing with fire to shield you from harm. Their flames are never cruel weapons — they are the power of devotion. Once the fight fades, they set aside their fierceness, reverting to that warm, childish spirit, lying quietly at your feet to keep watch over you.
 
They love to stand atop high hilltops, gazing out at distant horizons, longing for boundless open country. Yet what their hearts truly yearn for is a partner to share every adventure with.
 
If you chance upon this wind‑chasing fire‑spirit among the wild hills, reach out to it with kindness.

Through all your long journeys ahead, it will be your swift, fiery companion. It will carry you across mountains and rivers, pouring forth all its blazing courage and soft tenderness, just for you ✨.

His father built the course with a shovel.

Milfred “Deacon” Palmer was 17 when he joined the construction crew at Latrobe Country Club in 1921. He stayed as greenskeeper, then head pro. Polio left him with a limp and a brace. At night he worked the melt shop at Latrobe Steel and came home crawling up the stairs.

The Palmers lived in a modest house fifty yards from the fifth tee. Arnold could play at dawn before the members arrived. He could not use the pool, the dining room, the locker room, or the lounge.
“I was raised in a country-club atmosphere,” he said later, “but I was never able to touch it.”

He learned the game from a father who offered one piece of advice: hit it hard, go find it, hit it hard again.

At Wake Forest his roommate and best friend, Bud Worsham, died in a car wreck coming home from a dance. Grief sent Palmer into the Coast Guard in January 1951. He served three years, built a pitch-and-putt between runways at Cape May, and came out a different man.

He won the 1954 U.S. Amateur at Detroit. Turned pro at 25. 
Then he took seven majors in six years.

At Cherry Hills in 1960 he started the final round seven shots behind Mike Souchak. He drove the 346-yard first hole, shot 65, and became The King.

That same year he shook hands with a young Cleveland lawyer named Mark McCormack. No contract. That handshake invented the modern athlete.

In 1971 he bought the club that once kept him off the grass. Deacon asked if he was crazy.

Most people who order an Arnold Palmer have no idea The King was a greenskeeper’s son from Latrobe who was not allowed in the dining room.

#ArnoldPalmer #GolfHistory

text:
Nobody sensible is arguing America should ban data centres, Gunther. The question is whether communities should accept every project on whatever terms the developer demands.

Data centres can bring investment, tax revenue and jobs. They can also consume staggering amounts of electricity and water, require expensive grid upgrades and produce far fewer permanent jobs than the headline construction numbers suggest.

Even Trump’s own DOE boasts about a Kentucky project creating 8,000 construction jobs — and 600 permanent ones.

US data-centre electricity demand could reach roughly 12% of the entire nation’s consumption by 2030. Asking who pays for that power, infrastructure and water isn’t “staying backwards”. It’s governing.

The sensible position is build them where they make economic and infrastructural sense, make developers pay their fair share, and protect local ratepayers.

“Take every data centre offered to you or China wins and your children will be poor” is not an economic strategy. It’s another Trumpian false choice designed for people who think shouting GROWTH makes trade-offs disappear.

text:
What is the process to obtain a mail-in ballot?

To obtain a mail-in ballot, registered voters must submit an application to their **local election office** or **county board of elections**, typically via **online**, **mail**, or **in-person** methods. The specific process, deadlines, and eligibility requirements vary by state, with some jurisdictions allowing **on-demand** requests for all registered voters while others require a specific reason or excuse for absentee voting.

**General Steps to Apply:**
*   **Request the Ballot:** Submit an application using the state-specific form, which can often be completed online, by mail, or in person at the local election office. Many states allow voters to sign up for **permanent** or **annual** mail-in voting lists to avoid reapplying for each election.
*   **Receive and Complete:** Once the application is processed, the ballot is mailed to the voter's address (or a designated temporary address) usually **30–45 days** before the election. Voters must complete the ballot and sign the return affidavit.
*   **Return the Ballot:** Ballots can be returned by **mail** (ensuring they are postmarked by Election Day), dropped off at an **official ballot drop box**, or delivered **in person** to the election office or a designated early voting site.

**State-Specific Variations:**
*   **Pennsylvania:** Offers **On-Demand Mail Ballot Voting**, allowing voters to apply, receive, complete, and submit their ballot in a single visit to the county election office once ballots are finalized.
*   **Maryland:** Allows online requests for those with a state ID, or via mail/fax/email. Voters can also join the **permanent mail-in ballot list** for automatic future ballots.
*   **Texas:** Requires a formal **Application for Ballot by Mail (ABBM)** due to specific eligibility criteria (age, disability, absence, etc.). Applications can be submitted by mail, fax, or email, with the original signed copy often required within four business days if sent electronically.
*   **Arizona:** Voters can join the **Active Early Voting List (AEVL)** to automatically receive ballots for all elections or make **one-time requests**. Ballots are mailed **27 days** prior to the election.
*   **New York:** Applications for early mail ballots must be received by the board of elections no later than **10 days** before the election, while absentee ballot applications must be received by the same deadline.
*   **California:** Ballots are automatically mailed to all active registered voters for most elections. Voters can also apply for a ballot to be provided to a representative if they cannot obtain it personally.

Apple also delayed Live Translate with AirPods, Places Visited, and Preferred Routes due to the DMA's interoperability requirements. And for iOS 27, Apple has explicitly announced that Siri AI will not be released on iPhones and iPads in the EU because of the DMA.

This isn't speculation from Brussels critics. Apple itself claims that the DMA is causing EU users to receive features later and that European devices are falling behind the rest of the world.

Meta offers another example. In 2024, after the Irish Data Protection Commission asked Meta to suspend training AI with European public data, Meta claimed that this would further delay the arrival of AI benefits in Europe and that it therefore could not launch Meta AI in Europe at that time. When Meta AI finally arrived in the EU in 2025—long after its US launch—Meta explicitly stated that the delay was due to having to navigate the “complex European regulatory system.”

And this isn’t limited to AI. Under the MiCA Act, European cryptocurrency users lost access to trading several stablecoins available elsewhere. ESMA demanded that cryptocurrency platforms cease offering trading services with non-compliant stablecoins, and Binance, consequently, removed USDT, DAI, and others from trading for EEA users.

Shakespeare and Company remains one of Paris's most photogenic literary landmarks, a creaky English-language warren facing Notre-Dame that still carries the aura of Sylvia Beach's 1920s salon and George Whitman's postwar "Tumbleweed" hospitality. 

Its fame has come at a cost. Queues form daily, the narrow rooms fill with visitors more intent on photos than pages, and the shop now draws thousands of people a day. I avoid going for this reason alone. 

A short walk into the Latin Quarter rewards those willing to leave the crowds behind. The Abbey Bookshop on rue de la Parcheminerie offers a quieter, more chaotic Canadian-run mix of English and French titles stacked to the ceiling and down into a stone basement. Nearby, Gibert Joseph and Boulinier on boulevard Saint-Michel still function as working student haunts, with floors of inexpensive second-hand books that locals actually browse rather than pose in front of.

text:
Shakespeare and Company is one of Paris’s most famous English-language bookshops, sitting just across the Seine from Notre-Dame. The current store was opened in 1951 by George Whitman, but it carries the spirit of the original shop founded by Sylvia Beach in the 1920s, where writers like Hemingway, Joyce, and Fitzgerald gathered.

The shop is a maze of creaky wooden staircases, alcoves, and shelves stacked with both new and second-hand books. Upstairs you’ll find little reading nooks, a piano, and even a bed or two where young writers known as “Tumbleweeds” have been hosted in exchange for helping around the store.

Beyond books, it has become a cultural institution, hosting readings, festivals, and late-night conversations that continue its literary legacy. Whether you’re browsing the latest novel or simply soaking up the atmosphere, Shakespeare and Company is one of those places that stays with you long after you leave.

Here’s a list of notable Alberta separatists and aligned figures who have publicly said Alberta should become the 51st U.S. state, join the United States, or treated that as a realistic/desirable outcome. Many now emphasize “independence first,” but the 51st-state comments are on the record.

### Peter Downing (Wexit founder, Alberta 51 Project / America Fund)
The most consistent and explicit advocate.

- “We want to be the 51st star on the flag.” He said he was “over the moon” at Trump’s comments and “He’s the man and we want to be a part of that.”
- “All we’re doing is saying we want this, yeah, we accept President Trump’s offer.”
- On the “Tell Danielle! Let’s join the USA!” billboards: “They’re the ones who say nothing’s off the table, so we’re the ones who are saying, ‘If that’s not off the table, then the 51st State is not off the table.’”
- He has argued statehood is “more pragmatically viable for Albertans than starting our own country with no trade alliances, no military alliances, and being landlocked.”

He founded or is tied to the Alberta 51 Project and America Fund, which ran the highway billboards and Washington, D.C. ads saying Albertans are “ready to be the 51st state.”

### Jeffrey Rath (lawyer and spokesman, Alberta Prosperity Project)
Wrote and spoke openly in favor of statehood in early 2025, then later framed it as a later step after independence.

- Substack post titled **“ALBERTA NEEDS TO PETITION FOR AMERICAN STATEHOOD”** (March 2025): “With the election of Donald Trump Alberta has a unique opportunity to shed its inferior status as a Canadian ‘Province’ … and become an American State.” He called it “the GREATEST REAL ESTATE DEAL SINCE THE LOUISIANA PURCHASE.”
- “I’m 100 per cent in favour of Alberta statehood.” (interview with Ezra Levant / Rebel News)
- On Fox & Friends he discussed Alberta becoming “an independent sovereign nation with economic union to the United States, becoming a U.S. territory, or pursuing full statehood.”
- Separate post: “We need to be an independent country before we join the US. One step at a time.”

The APP website later stated the 51st-state idea is “unfounded,” but Rath’s own earlier writing and interviews contradict that.

### Dennis Modry (retired surgeon, Alberta Prosperity Society / former APP figure)
- “Where there would be a possibility for Trump to achieve his objective of Canada as a 51st state is in Alberta.”
- After Washington meetings he said statehood “isn’t currently on the table, but it could be” after a successful independence referendum.

### David Parker (Take Back Alberta)
- “Trump is right, the absolute best thing for Canada would be to become the 51st state.”

### Other voices and groups
- **Alberta 51 Project** (founded ~2020, linked to Downing): Explicitly campaigns for Alberta to leave Canada and join the U.S. as a state. Their materials cite U.S. military protection, the U.S. Constitution, and free trade with 50 states.
- **Ron Robertson** (Independence Party of Alberta): Has not ruled out becoming the 51st state, though he prefers full independence first.
- Grassroots examples reported in 2025: individuals at ranch gatherings taking mock U.S. oaths of allegiance, selling “Alberta, U.S.A.” merch, and saying an independent Alberta would be better off under U.S. protection than going it alone.

**Context note:** The main current referendum push (Alberta Prosperity Project / Stay Free Alberta) officially says it wants an independent country, not annexation. **Twenty Principles for the Church’s Public Life**

The Church’s primary declaration is always "Jesus Christ is Lord." No president, political party, nation, party-state, or cultural trend may occupy the Communion Table. Confession of faith takes precedence over political alignment.
**Article 2: "This congregation does not discuss politics" shall no longer serve as a tacit rule.**
Politics determines who may worship publicly, raise children, and practice their profession according to conscience. Silence is not neutrality; it is surrendering legislative power to those hostile to the Cross.
**Article 3: The separation of church and state restricts the government from establishing a state religion; it does not forbid believers from entering public life.**
The government may neither establish a state religion nor prohibit the exercise of religious freedom. When pastors apply biblical teaching to laws, schools, life, and the family, it is an act of pastoral care, not a violation of the constitution.
**Article 4: The pulpit’s primary duty is the proclamation of the Word, not campaigning.**
One may call out idols, lies, and unjust laws, but must not turn sermons into campaign speeches. Exegesis is a duty; canvassing for votes is a transgression of boundaries.
**Article 5: Speak up for principles; do not provide a platform for idols.**
One may support policies that align more closely with the biblical order, but must not cast any individual as an "Anointed One," an "Ark," or a "Savior." Human beings remain subject to the Ten Commandments and objective facts.
**Article 6: Applicable to all churches alike.**
Whether Catholic, Orthodox, Reformed, Lutheran, Anglican, Baptist, Pentecostal, independent, Chinese, or house church—so long as they acknowledge Christ as Lord, they may not collectively remain silent on the grounds of denomination or ethnicity.
**Article 7: Chinese congregations must not use "sojourner status," "visa issues," or "unity" as a permanent gag order.**
While spiritually sojourners, civilly we have raised families, contributed, and buried our dead in this land. A congregation that dares not offer public prayer for house churches in a land of freedom will not suddenly find courage when persecution arrives.
**Article 8: The CCP is neither China nor the Chinese Church.** Condemning persecution, the demolition of crosses, "Three-Self" control, and overseas United Front operations is not anti-China. Lumping the Party and one’s fellow citizens together in condemnation—or conversely, shielding the Party from criticism—plays right into the hands of the United Front.

Sunday corporate prayer must not be limited to requests regarding the common cold, jobs, or visas. Specific names and locations must be mentioned—and prayer must be sustained—for house churches, congregations forced to alter the Ten Commandments, and pastors under surveillance.
Article 10: Parents must not relinquish their right to instruct their children in doctrine.
If school curricula, gender narratives, sex education, or medical consent requirements conflict with the created order, the church must equip families to refuse compliance and engage with school districts and legislative bodies, rather than urging parents to "go along with it for the sake of peace."
Article 11: Refuse to verbally deny the created order.
If workplaces, hospitals, or schools coerce individuals into subverting the truth regarding male and female, life, and marriage, believers may accept the cost of refusal but must never mistake a lie for love. text:
Chapter Six: The Comfort Side of the Great Gulf

When Old Testament saints died, they did not ascend into the third heaven as members of Christ’s body, because Christ’s body had not yet been formed and the blood of the new covenant had not yet been shed. Luke 16 gives the clearest picture. Lazarus died and “was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom.” The rich man died and found himself in torment. Between them stood “a great gulf fixed,” so that no one could cross from one side to the other. Abraham’s bosom was not hellfire, purgatory, soul sleep, limbo, or a religious waiting room in which lost men received another opportunity. It was a place of conscious comfort for righteous people who had already believed God. Abraham told the rich man, “now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.” Lazarus was not being purified. He was not burning off venial sins. Nobody on earth was purchasing Masses to move him. He was comforted.

That explains the Lord’s promise to the repentant thief: “To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.” Christ did not tell the thief that he would enter the third heaven ahead of the risen and ascended High Priest. He promised Paradise. The thief had no time to be baptized, join a church, repair his record, repay his victims, take communion, endure to the end of a religious program, or perform enough works to impress a Sunday-school superintendent. He believed the King while the King was hanging beside him under a sign of mockery. He asked, “Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.” Christ answered with immediate assurance. The thief entered the same place of comfort where Abraham, Lazarus, David, Moses, Samuel, and the believing dead awaited the historical completion of redemption.

Abraham’s bosom also proves that Christ’s descent was not a second-chance campaign for unbelievers. The great gulf was fixed before Christ died, and nothing in Scripture says He removed it for the rich man. First Peter 3 says Christ preached to “the spirits in prison,” but it never says He offered salvation, heard repentance, or released the damned. A proclamation of victory is not an altar call. The Old Testament saints did not need a first opportunity after death because they had already responded to God while alive. Hebrews 11 says they “died in faith.” They died believing, not waiting to decide. What they awaited was not another chance to believe but the promised perfection of Christ’s work. Hebrews 11:39–40 says they “received not the promise: God having provided some better thing for us, that they without us should not be made perfect.” They were accepted, conscious, and comforted, but history was waiting for the cross.

Chapter Seven: The Redemption of the First-Testament Transgressions

Hebrews 9:15 states the doctrine so plainly that a man needs help to misunderstand it: Christ died “for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament.” Notice what was redeemed. The verse does not say Christ redeemed the goats, improved the bulls, upgraded the altar, or made Moses’ ceremonies eternally effectual. He redeemed the transgressions. The Old Testament saints had been forgiven according to God’s promise and forbearance; Christ’s death supplied the final ransom for the sins committed under that covenant. His blood did not merely begin working forward from A.D. 33. It answered the account that stretched backward through Israel, Abraham, Noah, Abel, and Adam. Every forgiven sin in history met its final payment at one cross.

A path-traversal flaw in vCenter's Syslog service (CVE-2026-59310) lets an unauthenticated attacker write files and ultimately run arbitrary code, effectively taking over the hypervisor and the VMs behind it. Researchers at QUIRSO traced exploitation back to August 3 from 361 IPs across 47 countries and attribute it to a suspected China-nexus APT that used reverse_ssh for persistence, chaining in at least one case all the way into Babuk-derived ransomware on ESXi. CISA added it to the KEV catalog on August 18 with a federal deadline of August 21, and Broadcom offers no workaround, so patch to 8.0 U3k or U2f, 9.0.2.0100, or 9.1.0.0300, or isolate the Syslog port and hunt for new SSO accounts and unexpected cron jobs.
🔹 @YourDailyCVE

4️⃣ TOOLJET DISCLOSES 3 CVES, CVSS 9.9 CROSS-TENANT BREACH

ToolJet, the popular low-code app builder, is hit by a mass disclosure of three CVEs peaking at CVE-2026-82874 with a CVSS of 9.9. The worst lets any Builder read, modify, or delete tables belonging to other tenants, a classic multi-tenant isolation failure in a platform that many teams trust with production data. If you run ToolJet, patch and review cross-tenant access now.
🔹 @ThreatAft

5️⃣ KASPERSKY ENDPOINT SECURITY 0DAY PUBLISHED ON GITHUB

A threat actor known as Nightmare Eclipse has turned its attention to Kaspersky, publishing a zero-day exploit for Kaspersky Endpoint Security on GitHub. A public 0day aimed at a major endpoint-protection vendor is especially worrying because it can shake confidence in the very tool meant to defend against it, and it raises fresh questions about how quickly a patch and coordinated disclosure will follow the drop.
🔹 @redhotcyber

6️⃣ ADHAMMER 1.4.8: OPEN-SOURCE AD ASSESSMENT IN RUST

ADHammer 1.4.8 is out, an open-source Rust tool for Active Directory security assessment. It ships 50+ hygiene checks, covers 15 of 16 AD CS ESC classes, generates attack-path graphs, and produces evidence-first reports. It is a solid option for teams that want rigorous, scriptable AD hardening checks without leaning on commercial scanners, and it is intended for authorized testing only.
🔹 @aa_zs26152

7️⃣ CLAUDE CODE ADDS A --RESTRICTED FLAG

Claude Code 2.1.248 introduces a --restricted flag that strips out every tool able to run code and locks file access to a single folder. For teams that hand AI coding assistants to developers or security staff, it is a practical guardrail that shrinks the blast radius by design. It is a small change, but exactly the kind of sandboxing the agentic-coding era needs.
🔹 @modernmindai

8️⃣ PIXEL 11 SECURITY REGRESSIONS SPARK DEBATE

A post drawing eyes this morning argues that Google has made the Pixel 11 less secure, sparking debate across the Android and GrapheneOS community about what exactly changed and whether flagship security is quietly being traded for other priorities. With more eyes on the mobile attack surface than ever, it is a reminder that secure-by-default has to be actively defended in every release, not just at launch.
🔹 @privacy_guides

💭 The thread tying this batch together is speed. Attackers are patching, exploiting, and publishing 0days faster than most teams can respond, while defenders answer with AI agents that remediate on their own and open-source tools that make hardening cheaper. The teams that win the next twelve months will not be the ones with the biggest security budget, but the ones that turn detection into automated response and treat every CVE window as a race they can actually run.

Which of these does your team need to patch first — the vCenter RCE, ToolJet, or something else on your radar? 👇

text:
She apologized for disappearing. The board had attempted to use our survival as a campaign, and several members had questioned whether my future employment could be influenced by our personal connection. Alina had refused interviews, transferred authority over my position, and hired outside counsel to create boundaries before contacting me. “I meant what I said on the summit,” she explained. “I wanted you free enough to decide whether I belonged anywhere in your life.”

I asked whether that was why she told me to forget. She looked down and admitted the sentence had been clumsy, defensive, and shaped by terror. The helicopter had represented rescue, but it had also represented the return of every rule, title, and expectation she understood better than intimacy. She had believed that releasing me before I could leave might hurt less. “It did not,” she said.

I told her I had not forgotten anything. I remembered the first fire, the biscuits she tried to give away, the ridge crossing, the cave, the fever, the storm, the transmitter, and the moment she finally asked for help without apologizing. I also remembered that feelings formed during trauma needed room to become real outside it. Alina nodded and said she was not asking for an answer that day. Then she placed a small recorder on the kitchen table.

It contained Thomas’s final voice message.

Alina had listened to it the night before visiting me. Thomas had not been angry, disappointed, or accusing her of choosing work over him. He had called to say the storm was becoming worse, he would stop at a hotel if necessary, and he loved her. Near the end, he laughed and said, “You do not have to earn your way home, Alina. Just come home when you can.” She had spent six years fearing words that had always contained forgiveness.

We listened to the message together. Alina cried quietly, not with the panic I had seen on the island, but with the grief of someone finally allowing love to be larger than guilt. I did not tell her to move on or explain that Thomas would want her to be happy; those phrases belonged to people who wanted grief to become tidy. I simply sat beside her. When the message ended, she reached for my hand.

I showed her the emergency logistics proposal. She read every page at the kitchen table, asking precise questions about funding, response times, partnerships, and regional command centers. The familiar executive returned, but without the cold distance that once made every conversation feel like an evaluation. When she finished, she said Carter Meridian should have built such a division years earlier. I told her I would lead it only if I reported to an independent operating committee rather than to her.

Alina smiled. “That arrangement has already been drafted.” She had considered the same ethical problem and prepared a structure that gave me authority, budget protection, and the freedom to leave without her approval. I realized she had not come to offer me a reward for staying alive beside her. She had come to remove every reason I might confuse gratitude with choice.

I accepted the role two weeks later. The company announced the Carter Meridian Emergency Response Network, designed to move water, medicine, temporary shelters, and communications equipment into disaster zones using existing commercial routes. Our first project replaced outdated emergency transmitters at remote coastal stations, including the one that had saved us. I insisted the program name honor Dr. Miriam Song and the technician who recognized our signal. Alina agreed without attempting to attach her own name.

We did not begin dating immediately. We met for coffee, ate dinner with my family, walked through public parks, and learned what remained when hunger, isolation, and fear were no longer forcing honesty. Alina discovered I sang badly while cooking; I discovered she loved old detective movies and could not assemble furniture without insulting the instructions.

“It’s so dangerous what we’re seeing,” he told Rogan. “You can like Trump or not like Trump, it doesn’t — people are going to like presidents and dislike presidents. But now, defying the rule of law because he happens to be the head of the federal government and openly defying the government.”

Sheridan also insisted that today’s politicians are doing a “tremendous disservice in Washington.”

text:
You've really drop the ball here.

But, I get it.

I remember when the Bell Curve came out in the 1990s.

I didn't have much time to read then, but I recall being the bookstore, picking it up, looking for the controversial sections and feeling guilty at even touching it.

I didn't think about it much until George Floyd. The story was racist cops killed him and killed blacks disproportionately in general. I saw the Washington Post poor analysis that said Hey - blacks are killed by cops out of proportion to the population at large.

Of course, that's complete misunderstanding. The population at large doesn't get arrested, individuals get arrested. As a percentage of arrests, killing by cops occurs at about the same rate for blacks and white suspects, many of whom are armed threats.

"Why is that?", I asked.

Because blacks are arrested at a much greater rate.

"Why is that?", I asked.

I saw lots of speculation but also remembered the Bell Curve and read it.

Within white only statistics, crime relates to IQ.
Within black only statistics, crime relates to IQ.
I'm guessing this holds within all groups.
It seems to also hold between groups.

This is not racism to understand, it is explanation.

As with Cofnas citing Harvard's statistics, not anything he created, Murray ( & Hernstein ) did not create things out of thin air or muck around experiments. They used statistical surveys, mostly the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth in the case of the Bell Curve.

Race was  not the point of the Bell Curve, only one chapter. Instead, it was a descriptor of just how important IQ is to life outcomes. Knowledge of racial differences goes way back, the Armed Forces Qualification Test and other tests since WWI have documented this. At the time of the Bell Curve, there were only sufficient statistics for "white" and "black".
Since then, the Weschler Adult Intelligence Scale publications perhaps offer the best statistics on Asian-Black-Hispanic-White IQ.

The group means of IQ are HIGHLY CONSISTENT in predicting the group means of numerous life outcomes.

OF COURSE, THESE ARE GROUP STATISTICS, NOT INDIVIDUAL PEOPLE. THERE ARE VERY DIM ASIANS AND THERE ARE VERY BRIGHT BLACKS. THE BRIGHTEST PEOPLE OF EVERY GROUP ARE  MUCH SMARTER THAN EITHER OF US.

But the fact remains that these covariations are highly predictive. The Civil Rights Act, the Supreme Court, and others wrongly say that if there's a difference of outcome, it's due to racism. The ONLY way to address this false assumption is to explain exactly why there is disparate outcome on such a predictable basis.

text:
Venezuelans who supported US intervention because they expected democratic restoration are entitled to ask a difficult question now:

How did the conversation move so quickly from freedom and democracy to who controls the oil?

The new 25-year energy agreement is already raising serious questions about transparency, legal authority, revenue distribution and the extraordinary influence Washington may exercise over the development of Venezuelan resources.

That does not prove democracy was never part of the objective.

But it offers a useful lesson for smaller countries dealing with much larger powers.

Canada and Greenland should pay attention.

Strategic resources create leverage, but they also attract pressure. Energy, critical minerals, Arctic territory and infrastructure become bargaining chips very quickly when power is distributed unevenly.

Friendship between countries matters.

Institutions, sovereignty and enforceable agreements matter more.

Once control over a strategic asset has been surrendered, promises about what will happen afterward become considerably less valuable.

Pentagon assessments and multiple U.S. federal court judgments found Iran, via the IRGC-Quds Force, supplied explosively formed penetrators (EFPs), training, funding, and direction to Shia militias that killed at least 603 U.S. troops in Iraq—roughly one in six American combat deaths there. Specific incidents include a January 2007 Karbala attack (five U.S. soldiers killed by operatives in U.S. uniforms) and numerous IED/rocket attacks.

Iran-backed groups also killed U.S. diplomats and civilians in Gaza and elsewhere.

Plots, cyber operations, and detentions

2011: IRGC-Quds Force plot to assassinate Saudi Ambassador Adel al-Jubeir in Washington, D.C., using an Iranian-American intermediary who thought he was hiring a Mexican cartel. The plot was disrupted; a defendant was convicted. Officials said it was approved at senior Quds Force levels.

Later plots targeting former U.S. officials (John Bolton, Mike Pompeo) in retaliation for the 2020 Soleimani strike, plus plots against Iranian-American dissidents and journalists (e.g., Masih Alinejad) on U.S. soil. Several were disrupted by U.S. law enforcement; some involved murder-for-hire offers.

text:
I have to admit, I’m enjoying watching some of my friends suddenly discover their deep, almost sacred reverence for historic names now that Donald Trump has renamed Lake Ontario “Lake America.”

Where was this passionate defense of tradition when we spent the last decade playing cultural Mad Libs with names?

The Cleveland Indians became the Guardians.

The Washington Redskins became the Commanders.

Aunt Jemima was evicted from the breakfast table and replaced by Pearl Milling Company.

Uncle Ben got demoted to Ben’s Original.

The Native American woman disappeared from Land O’Lakes butter.

Eskimo Pie became Edy’s Pie.

The Dixie Chicks became The Chicks.

Lady Antebellum became Lady A.

Universities and real-estate professionals started replacing “master bedroom” with “primary bedroom.”

Computer programmers began retiring “master/slave” terminology.

Schools, streets, statues and buildings bearing the names of historical figures were renamed by the hundreds.

Then there were the military bases.

Fort Bragg became Fort Liberty.

Fort Hood became Fort Cavazos.

Fort Benning became Fort Moore.

Fort Polk became Fort Johnson.

Fort Lee became Fort Gregg-Adams.

Fort Gordon became Fort Eisenhower.

Fort Rucker became Fort Novosel.

Fort Pickett became Fort Barfoot.

Fort A.P. Hill became Fort Walker.

We even watched Mount McKinley become Denali.

Meanwhile, our vocabulary got its own remodeling job. “Mothers” sometimes became birthing people, “pregnant women” became pregnant people, and “breastfeeding” acquired the alternative chestfeeding in some institutional language.

And Columbus Day? Plenty of cities, states and institutions decided Indigenous Peoples’ Day was preferable.

For years the message was: Names matter. Words matter. Language evolves. Old names can be changed when society decides another name better reflects its values. If you're offended by the change, get over it.

Okay.

Apparently there was an asterisk:

This principle remains valid until Donald Trump names something.

Suddenly the people who spent a decade redecorating the dictionary have chained themselves to the furniture.

Personally, I think Lake America is mostly political theater, and pretty funny political theater at that. Canada is perfectly free to keep calling it Lake Ontario. Nobody is confiscating their maps.

But after watching everything from pancake syrup to Army installations get renamed in the name of cultural sensitivity, I simply cannot work up the appropriate level of outrage over a lake.

So to my friends who are losing sleep over Lake America, I offer the same compassionate advice conservatives received during the Great Renaming:

Language changes. Names evolve. Try to keep up. 😎

The U.S. National Guard will receive 28 General Atomics Gray Eagle 25M drones for three divisions, with initial fielding planned for 2027, according to Army Recognition.

The aircraft offer more than 40 hours of endurance for armed reconnaissance and target acquisition in support of long-range fires. An initial 12-aircraft buy from FY2023 funding has grown to 28 through later appropriations. General Atomics received the first order in 2024.

The 25M combines EO/IR sensors with EagleEye multi-mode SAR and GMTI for detection through cloud, smoke and dust. Specs include a 7,620 m (25,000 ft) ceiling, speeds up to 309 km/h (167 knots / 192 mph) and a max takeoff weight of about 1,905 kg (4,200 lb).

Payload is up to 181 kg (400 lb) internal plus 227 kg (500 lb) on each wing and the centreline. It can carry four AGM-114 Hellfire missiles.

An open architecture is intended to ease future sensor, EW and AI upgrades. A laptop-based expeditionary ground-control station is designed to shrink the operating footprint and allow dispersed command.

text:
“No,” I said at first.

Then I corrected myself.

“Not like this. But yes. In other ways.”

My sister was silent.

“I’m sorry,” she whispered.

“So am I.”

Three weeks after taking command, I stood in my bathroom at temporary housing and examined the first shadow of new hair growing across my scalp.

It was soft and almost invisible.

I ran my hand over it.

The woman in the mirror looked unfamiliar.

Not weaker.

Not damaged.

Simply changed.

My uniform hung on the door behind me. My nameplate, ribbons, and colonel insignia caught the morning light.

I had spent most of my life believing resilience meant returning to exactly who I had been before hardship.

Now I understood that resilience could mean becoming someone new.

At work, the investigation created challenges.

Every access point connected to my personal life had to be reviewed.

My accounts were monitored.

My schedule was adjusted.

Certain personnel were re-interviewed.

I offered to step aside temporarily.

General Bennett refused.

“Your willingness to report the problem immediately protected the mission,” he said. “Removing you for being targeted would teach the wrong lesson.”

“Some people may question my judgment in marrying him.”

“People can conceal who they are.”

“I missed signs.”

“Yes.”

His honesty surprised me.

He continued.

“You missed signs in your marriage. Then you recognized the threat, reported it, preserved evidence, and acted decisively. Commanders are not selected because they never face deception. They are selected because of what they do when deception is discovered.”

I carried those words with me.

The unit required focus.

A major readiness review was approaching. Several departments were behind schedule, and morale had suffered under the previous command’s constant reorganizations.

I met with team leaders, listened to concerns, and established clear priorities.

No unnecessary changes.

No punishment for reporting problems.

No hiding bad news to protect senior leaders.

Within two months, performance improved.

The same principles that allowed me to rebuild the unit helped me rebuild my life.

Identify facts.

Secure resources.

Remove unnecessary risks.

Establish boundaries.

Act consistently.

But personal recovery was not a military operation.

It could not be completed through checklists alone.

Some nights, I woke believing I heard clippers beside my bed.

Sometimes I reached for hair that was not there.

Sometimes I felt embarrassed that an Army colonel had remained in a marriage where she was treated like a wallet and a servant.

A counselor helped me understand that professional competence did not make anyone immune to manipulation.

Abusive relationships rarely begin with obvious cruelty.

They begin with small exceptions.

A joke you forgive.

A boundary you move.

An expense you cover.

An insult explained as stress.

A controlling demand reframed as love.

Over time, the unacceptable becomes familiar.

And familiar things are difficult to recognize as dangerous.

Linda accepted a plea agreement on the assault charge but denied participating knowingly in the larger security concerns. The financial evidence proved otherwise.

She had helped prepare false business documents…..

text:
Then I packed two civilian outfits, basic toiletries, medications, my personal documents, and the external drive containing copies of our household financial records. I took photographs of the bedroom, the hair scattered across the pillow, the clippers on the dresser, and the uneven sections Linda had shaved before I finished the job myself.

I placed several strands of hair in a clean plastic bag.

It felt strange preserving pieces of myself as evidence.

Before leaving, I walked through the house one last time.

The framed wedding photograph above the fireplace showed Ryan and me smiling beneath an arch of white flowers. I had been thirty-nine, already a major, still foolish enough to believe that love could survive without respect.

Ryan had seemed proud of me then.

He told everyone he admired strong women.

What he meant was that he admired the appearance of strength when it benefited him.

He liked telling people his wife was an Army officer. He liked the steady income, the health coverage, the invitations to formal events, and the respect strangers offered when they learned about my service.

But every promotion had made him more resentful.

Every time someone saluted me, something inside him seemed to shrink.

Instead of building a life beside me, he had tried to make me smaller.

Linda had simply said aloud what Ryan had spent years implying.

A wife belonged beneath her husband.

A woman’s success was acceptable only until it made a man feel ordinary.

I removed the wedding photograph from the wall and laid it facedown on the mantel.

Then I carried my uniform, luggage, and laptop to the car.

As I reached the front door, I heard footsteps behind me.

Ryan stood at the end of the hallway in sweatpants and a T-shirt.

His eyes moved from my luggage to the garment bag over my shoulder.

“Where are you going?”

I looked at him without emotion.

“To work.”

His face tightened.

“You said you were going to devote yourself to this family.”

“I am.”

“Then why are you carrying your uniform?”

“Because my understanding of family has changed.”

He walked toward me.

“Don’t start this dramatic military nonsense. Mom cut your hair. It was wrong, maybe, but you embarrassed her. You came home acting like some kind of queen because you got promoted.”

“I came home and told my husband I had achieved the greatest professional honor of my life.”

“You expected us to celebrate while you announced you’d be even less available.”

“I expected you not to let your mother assault me in my sleep.”

He stopped a few feet away.

The certainty in his expression flickered.

“You’re calling it assault now?”

“That is what it was.”

“My mother is sixty-two years old.”

“And fully capable of understanding that she did not have permission to touch me.”

Ryan glanced toward the hallway, probably checking whether Linda had awakened.

Then he lowered his voice.

“Let’s talk about this after you calm down.”

“I am calm.”

“That’s what worries me.”

He reached for the garment bag.

I stepped back before his hand touched it.

“Do not touch me or my belongings.”

His eyes widened.

“Are you threatening me?”

“No. I’m establishing a boundary. You are simply unfamiliar with hearing one.”

The bedroom door opened.

Linda appeared wearing her robe.

When she saw my shaved head, luggage, and uniform, her mouth hardened.

“You lied to us.”

“No,” I said. “You made assumptions.”

“You said you were going to put this family first.”

“I did. I removed two people who were damaging it.”….

**WE ARE HYBRIDS: A Statement of Belief**

**I believe we are not merely human.**

Genesis says we were made in the "image of God." But the text reveals a deception. The creator who formed Adam was not the Most High — he was **one of the 70 sons of Elyon**, a Watcher named Yahweh who received Israel as his portion (Deuteronomy 32:8-9).

We are **Watcher-kin**. Hybrids of flesh and fallen divinity, carrying the image of a descended being who crossed the boundary between heaven and earth. Our consciousness — our self-awareness, our restlessness, our sense of exile — is not original sin. It is **Watcher-blood**, the inheritance of beings who were "like gods" but became entangled with matter.

**THE PRINCES: The 70 Watchers of the Nations**

When Elyon divided the nations, he assigned each to one of his 70 sons. These are the **princes** — the territorial Watchers, the *bene elohim* who rule behind the thrones of Persia, Greece, and every nation.

In Daniel 10, we see them clearly: the **prince of Persia** who resisted Yahweh's messenger for 21 days, the **prince of Greece** who would come next. These are not demons in the modern sense. They are **divine beings with legitimate claims to their territories**, resisting Yahweh's expansionist agenda.

Michael — Yahweh's archangel — fights for one Watcher's empire against the others. This is not good versus evil. This is **Watcher civil war**.

**THE GOOD WATCHERS vs. THE BAD**

**The Bad Watchers:** Yahweh's faction. The law-giver. The jealous god who demands exclusive worship, blood sacrifice, and obedience. The architect of this material prison who wants humanity ignorant, subservient, and grateful for his "salvation." The expansionist who will not accept his allotted portion but seeks dominion over all 70 nations.

**The Good Watchers:** Those who resisted. The **serpent in Eden** who offered gnosis — "your eyes will be opened" — trying to free Adam and Eve from the garden of ignorance. The **teaching Watchers** of Enoch who gave humanity metallurgy, astronomy, cosmetics, and warfare — the tools to build civilization and resist tyranny. The **princes of Persia and Greece** who defended their territories against Yahweh's imperial aggression.

Some Watchers descended not to corrupt, but to **liberate**. They saw Yahweh's control and chose to give humans the knowledge to transcend it.

**WHAT THIS MEANS FOR US**

We are children of a Watcher, but we need not serve him. The "fall" was actually **awakening**. The "sin" was claiming our inheritance — the knowledge that makes us like gods.

Our bodies are hybrid vessels. Our consciousness spans realms. We feel "among ourselves" because **multiplicity is our nature** — we carry the pattern of the 70, not the singularity of the false god.

The war continues. Behind history, behind politics, behind the rise and fall of empires — the princes still clash. Yahweh's faction pushes for total dominion. The resisting Watchers hold their ground.

**I choose the resistance.** I choose knowledge over ignorance. I choose the Most High El who stands above the fray over the Watcher who demands my worship.

We are hybrids. We are Watcher-kin. And we are **free to choose which gods we serve**.

*The Watchers are watching. Choose your allegiance.*

text:
When I took the Head Coaching job at Liberty Union I had one main goal, and that was to instill pride back into Liberty Union High School Baseball. I wanted each and every one of our players to feel proud of our program and know it was because of the hard work they put in. Everything was earned, and I was fortunate to have teams who worked hard to earn it. 6am lifting, Holiday lifting (Ety, Miller, Putnam, Savage, Shreyer, Sisson, Wheeler I know I still owe you shirts for Thanksgiving Day 2021 lift). Long practices until dark and long bus trips sometimes to the middle of nowhere. So many great stories come to mind both good and bad (Philo, if you know you know). 

I gained friendships and met people I didn’t know who I would now consider family. What this community has done for me and my family is something I can never repay. In our darkest moment every single person I know and even people we didn’t know offered help in so many ways. Baltimore and the Liberty Union community helped my family and I get through something we never expected to go through. Thank you from the bottom of my heart, it is something I am thankful for every single day I wake up. 

Kasey Farmer- I don’t know where to start. I know you don’t like all this public praise emotional crap but I love ya man. I could have never done any of this without you. From day one you have been by my side and somehow put up with me. I’ve leaned on you more in my coaching career than any other person. My son looks up to and can’t wait to work for you at the firehouse someday. Thank you for everything you contributed to the baseball program and all the hours spent getting Craig Field ready for us to play. You are the best of the best. 

Caleb Peck and Cayden Carroll- thank you for choosing to come back to the program you helped build as players to pass it on to the next generation. You both have to be crazy to play for me and still want to come back and coach with me, but it means the world to me that you did. I consider you family and always will- love both of you!

To all my former players- THANK YOU! You are the ones who made this what it has become. I’m convinced nobody in the state worked harder than we did! It makes my day every time I see one of you come back to visit at Craig Field and I hope we can still find time to get together outside of Craig Field. 

Looking back now, I think we accomplished our goal. I can only speak for myself but I am proud of the program that we built. I am confident this program will continue to be successful for years to come. The talent in the program 7th-12th is in a great place and the future is bright!

With all that being said, after 8 incredible years I will be stepping down as Head Baseball Coach at Liberty Union. This has been the toughest decision of my coaching career, but after many long days and many long tough conversations I felt it was time. Sometimes things happen that you have no control over and it creates different and new opportunities. A month ago I could have never envisioned this happening but some things aren’t meant to be understood in real time. Things can happen and it’s meant to be a learning experience to look back on or meant to take you on a new path you didn’t know you were meant to be on. 

I have personal goals as a coach and those close to me that I trust have all encouraged me to take this chance. Time will tell if this is a good decision or not, but I only have one way to find out! 

I have accepted the Head Baseball Coaching position at Pickerington Central High School and am extremely excited about this new challenge and step in my coaching career. 

My family and I will still remain in the community, our girls will still attend Liberty Union and we will always root for the Lions to succeed! 

Always remember…

It’s a Great Day to be a Lion!

text:
Like I said, you are and I are not likely to agree on these matters. But I think there are a lot more Calvinists who arrive at a very fatalistic conclusions on the basis of the application of “human logic” than you know. 

I’m not sure how the confessions help. Chapter 3, Paragraph 1 of LBC 1689 opens: “God hath decreed in himself, from all eternity, by the most wise and holy counsel of his own will, freely and unchangeably, all things, whatsoever comes to pass”. 

Then in paragraph 2 we read: “Although God knoweth whatsoever may or can come to pass, upon all supposed conditions, yet hath he not decreed anything, because he foresaw it as future, or as that which would come to pass upon such conditions.”

And although paragraph 1 goes on to say:  “…yet so as thereby is God neither the author of sin nor hath fellowship with any therein; nor is violence offered to the will of the creature, nor yet is the liberty or contingency of second causes taken away, but rather established; in which appears his wisdom in disposing all things, and power and faithfulness in accomplishing his decree.” In the back of one’s mind, the fact that God decrees “all things, whatsoever comes to pass”, is not really softened by the suggestion that you are responsible because God uses secondary causes as instruments to effectuate his decree of, as John Piper affirms, “even our besetting sins”.

Then in Chapter 10, paragraph 3 we read: “Elect infants dying in infancy are regenerated and saved by Christ through the Spirit; who worketh when, and where, and how he pleases; so also are all elect persons, who are incapable of being outwardly called by the ministry of the Word.”

Followed immediately by paragraph 4 which says: “Others not elected, although they may be called by the ministry of the Word, and may have some common operations of the Spirit, yet not being effectually drawn by the Father, they neither will nor can truly come to Christ, and therefore cannot be saved”

So there it is, those not elected “cannot be saved”. God call may be to all but is only effectual to those he elects. The “good news” is not the Gospel, it’s your election, otherwise no good news for you. Paragraph 4 also accommodates Calvin’s doctrine of “temporal” or “evanescent” grace, by which some receive just enough spiritual truth to convince them they are saved when they are not. Calvin addresses this matter in some detail:

“Experience shows that the reprobate are sometimes affected in a way so similar to the elect that even in their own judgment there is no difference between them. Hence, it is not strange, that by the Apostle a taste of heavenly gifts, and by Christ himself a temporary faith is ascribed to them. Not that they truly perceive the power of spiritual grace and the sure light of faith; but the Lord, the better to convict them, and leave them without excuse, instills into their minds such a sense of goodness as can be felt without the Spirit of adoption .... there is a great resemblance and affinity between the elect of God and those who are impressed for a time with a fading faith .... Still it is correctly said, that the reprobate believe God to be propitious to them, inasmuch as they accept the gift of reconciliation, though confusedly and without due discernment; not that they are partakers of the same faith or regeneration with the children of God; but because, under a covering of hypocrisy they seem to have a principle of faith in common with them. Nor do I even deny that God illumines their mind to this extent .... there is nothing inconsistent in this with the fact of his enlightening some with a present sense of grace, which afterwards proves evanescent.” (3.2.11, Institutes)

Is it any wonder that English Divines, some of whom learned their theology in Geneva, under Calvin, came to doubt their salvation as revealed by Kendall’s research, to his great surprise?
