text:
She had impersonated me during at least one telephone verification call.

She had used my personal information to open an insurance account.

The recording from that call was played in court.

Her voice was calm as she claimed to be me.

She gave my date of birth, home address, Social Security information, and military employer details.

When asked whether she understood the financial obligations, she said, “Yes, I approve everything my husband has arranged.”

My husband.

She had erased me so completely that she spoke as though she were the wife in my marriage.

Ryan’s case took longer.

His attorneys argued that he had been manipulated by Victor Hale, that he did not understand the broader implications, and that he believed he had informal permission to use our financial information because we were married.

The forged signatures disproved that claim.

People do not forge permission they believe they already possess.

During a recorded interview, Ryan finally admitted the truth.

He had wanted to build a business before I became a colonel.

He was tired of being introduced as “Colonel Marshall’s husband.”

He believed that if he became wealthy, people would respect him.

Hale offered money and connections.

At first, Ryan shared only details he considered harmless.

Then Hale requested more.

Each payment made the next request easier.

When Ryan realized the situation might be dangerous, he did not report it.

He kept accepting money.

He hoped my promotion would allow him to refinance the failing business and repay everything before I noticed.

Linda believed forcing me to resign would solve two problems.

I would no longer have access to information Hale wanted.

And I would remain home to help repair Ryan’s business.

That was why she shaved my hair.

She believed public humiliation would make me too ashamed to report for duty.

She thought I would call the Pentagon, decline the command, and disappear from military life.

She had mistaken my dignity for something she could cut away.

The divorce hearing occurred seven months after I left the house.

Ryan looked older when he entered the courtroom.

His suit hung loosely on him. His face had lost the confident fullness it once carried. He avoided looking at me until the judge asked whether reconciliation was possible.

“No,” I said.

Ryan finally raised his eyes.

“Your Honor, I still love my wife.”

The words produced no feeling in me.

The judge looked at him.

“Colonel Marshall has filed extensive evidence of fraud, coercive behavior, and unauthorized financial activity. On what basis do you believe reconciliation is realistic?”

Ryan swallowed.

“We were under pressure.”

The judge waited.

Ryan continued.

“My mother interfered too much. I should have defended my wife.”

It was the closest he had come to admitting personal responsibility.

But even then, he placed his mother between us.

The judge turned to me.

“Colonel Marshall, do you wish to respond?”

I stood.

“For years, I believed marriage required me to keep repairing damage I did not cause. I believed patience would create respect. I believed providing more would eventually make them grateful.”…..

text:
Quick thoughts on biggest fantasy relevant cutdown day roster moves (pending Monday 1pm waiver deadline). Some bigger than others.

There will be more moves, but as we stand now...

ARZ - James Conner IR - boosts Tyler Allgeier short-term projection, eliminates chance of Conner upending another RB depth chart soon (trade possible/unlikely, still out 4 wk min, old/rehabbing).

ATL - Tyler Goodson cut - Brian Robinson fine, ATL beat writers in shambles.

BAL - Adam Randall to IR-R - Justice Hill primary Henry handcuff. Move smells of roster circumvention after promising rookie balled out Friday. Coach’s pet Chris Moore also cut (bullish young WRs)

BUF - Frank Gore cut - Good vibes for Ty Johnson’s health - soon, even if not ready to go Wk 1. Caps Ray Davis contingent handcuff appeal.

CAR - David Moore/John Metchie cut - Bodes well for Xavier Legette foot outlook, points to relatively tight WR rotation. Cokeheads rejoice.

CHI - Kyle Monangai avoids IR - Roschon Johnson RB3, might be short-term top backup. Also currently a tight 5-man WR corps.

CIN - Charlie Jones/Mitch Tinsley cut - Clears runway (to a definite WR3 point) for rookie Colbie Young and camp standout Dohnte Meyers. Kept a fantasy-facemelting five TEs.

CLE - Taylen Green makes team - Candles remain lit.

DAL - Jayden Blue cut - 4.3 speed in Louis Vuitton cleats can’t outrun The Turk. Phil Mafah also cut. Makes Malik Davis attractive backup, pending practice squad (re)signings.

DEN - Jaleel McLaughlin/Cody Schrader cut - Jonah Coleman stuck in 4-man backfield (Tyler Badie survives). Still 4-man TE room for Payton to play with despite trimming Krull, Joly, Prentice (FB).

DET - Greg Dortch cut - Isaac TeSlaa big winner despite bad vibes from challenging camp. Will likely add, but currently just 4 WRs (3 TEs). Jacob Saylors worth watching as short-term Gibbs cuff.

GB - Josh Jacobs to Exempt List - Strong chance league saw tape. Good chance Jacobs is done. MarShawn Lloyd clear winner. More backfield moves to come. Also currently no backup WRs to speak of = tight rotation = sexy.

HOU - Shepard/Zay/Watson/Bond cut, Dell IR - streamlined WR roles around Nico Collins. Kayshon Boutte clearer path to early routes.

IND - DJ Giddens kept …for now - Often projected as a cut after injury riddled camp, Giddens may still be replaced by available vet RB. Seth McGowan’s positive outlook also contingent on current backfield status quo.

JAX - LeQuint Allen avoids IR - Pass-catching back DeeJay Dallas also cut, offers hope Allen ready sooner than later. Ameer Abdullah kept for contingency/special teams value.

KC - Emari Demercado cut - Everything’s coming up Emmett! Rookie Johnson moves further into strong handcuff territory.

LAC - Jaret Patterson cut - Good news for Keaton Mitchell’s injury outlook, even if the hammy-prone Missile is not out of woods.

LAR - Five TEs kept - Terrance Ferguson has crowded TE room and another “WR3” to contend with in Tutu Atwell. Also, unkillable Ronnie Rivers outlasts 2025 fourth-rounder Jarquez Hunter (traded/cut) as RB3.

LV - Roman Hemby/Dare Ogunbowale cut - Removal of veteran backfield depth strengthens health outlook for Ashton Jeanty, shows faith in Mike Washington, Dylan Laube.

MIA - Cleaned out vet WRs - Traded Tutu Atwell, cut Terrace Marshall/Jalen Reagor. Vote of confidence in rookies Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell with little in front of them. Also insta-cut Jarquez Hunter, simplifying backfield outlook.

MIN - Demond Claiborne kept - Useful pass catching back Zavier Scott cut, leaving Claiborne with tangible path to meaningful touches in lightly talented backfield.

NE - Traded for Corey Kiner - Scrappy fan favorite Lan Larison gets cut. Plenty of work coming for Mondre and Tre. Thin TE room continues to bode well for rookie Eli Raridon.

NO - Alvin Kamara not put on IR - Perhaps only due to saving the two IR-R slots, it’s still better for AK than alternative. Kendre Miller backup to own off solid camp. Jordyn Tyson starts on IR-R as expected.

NYG - OBJ makes thin WR room - Only five WRs streamlines projected roles - with four TEs, four RBs, and a FB kept. This clearly is now a Harbaugh operation, right down to the Old Yeller WR roster spot.

NYJ - Vet QBs cut - It’s Geno Smith and an, at times, overwhelmed rookie as the only QBs on the roster with questionable coaching. What could go wrong?

PHI - TE room stays crowded - Four kept tight ends, plus Grant Calcaterra set to return from IR-R, underscores how buried Eli Stowers really is off an underwhelming first offseason. Dynasty option only.

PIT - Kaleb Johnson traded / Travis Homer cut - With only Eli Heidenreich behind Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle, the vets will be plenty busy and should comfortably pay off depressed current draft cost.

SEA - PUP for Zach Charbonnet - Was clear to anyone paying attention to the non-news being interpreted as hope for miraculous recovery from February ACL surgery. Jadarian Price has significant runway to stake claim to backfield before Charbs returns.

SF - Backfield vets cleared out - Sincere McCormick and Khalil Herbert cut and Isaac Guerendo on PUP clears the deck for Kaelon Black as the CMC handcuff to own. James Jordan behind, at least to start.

TB - Sean Tucker renegotiates - With Josh Williams cut and Tucker cutting $1M from his salary, he stays - but the assumption he will have the goal line role is shattered. That unknown boosts Bucky Irving’s value, even if Tucker getting cut would’ve been better.

TEN - Will Levis cut - Drunk Drew Bledsoe will ride again, somewhere. Also, Michael Carter should resurface in another backfield after getting cut.

WAS - Jeremy McNichols on IR-R - Robert Henry was also cleared out of a backfield that Kaytron Allen will have at least four games to make enough of an impression to stick around in. Also did they really need seven WRs ( #FreeTreylon )

A man got so bored after selling his company for half a BILLION dollars that he accidentally became the single greatest source of casino revenue in Las Vegas history losing over $200 MILLION while the house kept his vodka full and his pills hidden in candy boxes.

– Terrance Watanabe ran his family's party-favor import empire out of Omaha, Nebraska, for over two decades, turning it into one of the biggest mail-order retailers in the country.

– He sold his stake in 2000 and walked away roughly $500 MILLION richer.

– With nothing left to build, he wandered into a casino across the Iowa border just to kill time.

– By 2006 he'd relocated to Las Vegas permanently.

– Steve Wynn spotted him on the floor and pulled him into a private meeting.

– Wynn recognized the signs immediately, alcoholic, compulsive gambler, and banned him outright, since Nevada law forbids letting a visibly intoxicated person keep playing.

– Harrah's called him within the week.

– Their offer was $12,500 a month in airfare, concert tickets, $500,000 in gift shop credit, 15% cash back on losses past half a million, and a free three-bedroom suite at Caesars Palace.

– He said yes and over the course of 2007 he wagered $825 MILLION across Caesars Palace and The Rio, the single largest amount ever bet by one person in Vegas history.

– $127 MILLION of it disappeared. That single man accounted for 5.6% of Harrah's entire yearly gambling revenue in Las Vegas.

– Staff made sure his preferred vodka never ran out.

– When a painkiller addiction developed, staff started slipping his pills to him at the table, tucked inside boxes of candy.

– He played for stretches of 24 straight hours. One day alone cost him $5 MILLION.

– At his peak he ran three separate blackjack hands at once, $50,000 riding on each.

– His sister finally caught up with him at Thanksgiving 2007.

– She had no idea any of this had happened. She brought him back to Nebraska and got him into rehab.

– When his lawyers subpoenaed Harrah's internal records, the real total wasn't $127 MILLION, it was $204 MILLION.

– He sued the casino for $20 MILLION, arguing they'd deliberately kept him drunk and medicated to keep the money flowing.

– There's no federal agency that oversees how a casino treats a gambler like Watanabe, only individual state gaming boards, and casinos have spent decades lobbying to keep it that way.

– That patchwork is exactly why a single state fine of $225,000 was the entire consequence for a $200 million binge that one company profited from directly.

Every criminal charge against him quietly disappeared in a confidential settlement. The house, as always, made sure the story ended on its terms.

text:
After NBC's @kwelkernbc said Trump's endorsement of candidates in primaries this cycle got "mixed results," Trump took to social media, said his real record is "99% SUCCESS," and asked FCC Chair Carr to take action.

First, of the 313 congressional and state candidates he endorsed, 96% won, but of the 12 that lost, 9 were in the past few weeks, forming a cluster that makes it look like his record is taking a hit. So they're both kinda right.

Second, but actually first, this story is bigger than Welker. Or Trump.  Or any of this.

The media is under enormous pressure these days. There are people who actually think reporting on the Jason Arday story is tantamount to murder, and that we should enact prior restraint on the press to prevent such "hate journalism."

For more on that, see:
https://t.co/8AyWYzWkuZ

Or consider Catherine Herridge, formerly of Fox News, being ordered to reveal her sources because a suspected Chinese spy subpoenaed her. 

Or cast a glance over at our own White House, where the supposed leader of the free world, and self-proclaimed defender of free speech, is simultaneously waging war against ABC, NBC, CBS, AP, NYT, WSJ, BBC, THE ATLANTIC, BLOOMBERG, NPR, PBS, VOA, RFE, RFA, MBN, even Stars and Stripes. 

For more on that last one, see:
https://t.co/kjJd4Gh2PP

Not to mention Pentagon access restrictions against WaPo, CNN, Politico, Reuters, the Hill, the War Zone, and Newsmax, and others.

For more on that:
https://t.co/98s1zR9U3z

But Trump is not just pushing back on bad reporting. He's part of a larger trend that seeks to erode the very purpose of even having a free press in the first place.

It is, of course, wonderful that the press offers a public forum for debate. It is also virtually a sacred societal good that the press nourishes the public mind with facts about current affairs (to the extent that they still do so).

But, as Supreme Court Justice Potter Stewart famously argued, these things are not the primary purpose of a free press. Otherwise, we wouldn't need to explicitly carve out space for journalism in the Press Clause of the First Amendment.

Today, Stewart is mostly remembered for his famous remark on obscenity, from the case Jacobellis v. Ohio: "I know it when I see it." 

But he should rather be more fondly remembered for  his 1975 essay "Or of the Press," in which he argued that the Press Clause exists to protect an institutional press.

That means an autonomous Fourth Estate, not just "a kind of Hyde Park Corner for the community," which we can think of today as X, or "a neutral conduit of information," which today is arguably AI more than it is the press (and even that isn't neutral). But instead, he said, the true telos of the press is stand as a check on government power, a leash on abuses no less than the Speech Clause itself, and often more.

As the British management cybernetician Stafford Beer once said, "The purpose of a system is what it does," and what Trump is doing is dismantling the institutional role of the press over bad reporting, or merely reporting he doesn't like. That's like trying to dismantle free speech over stupid opinions, or opinions you dislike. So what is the purpose of doing such a thing? Why silence the only organized private business that enjoys explicit constitutional protection in order to check government power and abuse? 

And while you consider the thought, maybe also take notice of the fact that it's a fairly woke and authoritarian impulse to try to silence reporting, or deport people, or have them fired, for saying things you don't want to hear. Or, perhaps just as often, for saying things you don't want anyone else to know.

As for deporting people for having opinions, a federal judge ruled Friday that such efforts are, as my Bahamian mother would put it, "a pile of foolishness."

For more on that, see FIRE's victory:
https://t.co/z2VgjsH2cN

text:
Hebrews 9:26 says, “But now once in the end of the world hath he appeared to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.” Animal blood could not take away sin; Christ appeared to put it away. Hebrews 9:12 says He entered the holy place “by his own blood” and obtained “eternal redemption for us.” Eternal redemption required eternal worth. Christ was not one more victim in a procession of sacrifices. He was the fulfilment that ended the procession. He was the Priest and the Offering, the Temple and the Sacrifice, the Son of man and the Son of God. He did not carry another creature’s blood into the true sanctuary. He entered by His own blood. When heaven examined the payment, nothing was missing. When holiness measured the sacrifice, nothing fell short. When death attempted to hold the One who bore sin without committing sin, death lost its prisoner.

Ephesians 4 says that when Christ ascended, “he led captivity captive,” and identifies His descent into “the lower parts of the earth.” The Captain of salvation entered the realm of the departed, not as a defeated sinner but as the conquering Redeemer. He had paid for the transgressions under the first testament. The righteous captives in Paradise did not need to be converted; they needed the redemptive work upon which their faith ultimately rested to be completed. Christ brought captivity captive and ascended. Paradise is later associated with the third heaven in Second Corinthians 12. The way was open because the blood had been shed, the veil had been rent, sin had been put away, and the Redeemer had risen. The Old Testament saints did not pray their way out, work their way out, suffer their way out, or receive financial assistance from living relatives. Jesus Christ brought them out because Jesus Christ had paid.

Chapter Eight: One Sacrifice, One Payment, One Finished Redemption

The contrast between the Levitical priest and Jesus Christ is one of the most magnificent contrasts in Scripture. Hebrews 10:11 says, “And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.” The priest stood because the work continued. There was no chair at the altar because an unfinished sacrifice has no right to sit down. Then verse 12 announces, “But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God.” The Levitical priest stood daily; Christ sat down forever. The priest returned tomorrow; Christ said, “It is finished.” The priest offered another animal; Christ offered Himself. The priest worked inside a shadow; Christ entered heaven itself. The priest handled blood that could not take away sin; Christ presented blood that obtained eternal redemption.

The Church Age believer therefore receives a position no Old Testament worshipper possessed during his earthly life. The moment a sinner believes the gospel, he is justified, redeemed, reconciled, regenerated, spiritually circumcised, sealed by the Holy Ghost, and baptized by the Spirit into the Body of Christ. He does not enter a yearly arrangement that depends upon another Day of Atonement. He is “complete in him.” He does not possess forgiveness while awaiting somebody to make the final payment. He has “redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins.” His soul is joined to Christ, his life is hid with Christ in God, and his standing rests upon the righteousness of the risen Son of God. When a believer dies now, he does not descend to Abraham’s bosom and await Calvary. Calvary is finished. To be absent from the body is to be present with the Lord, and to depart is to be with Christ, “which is far better.”

text:
The first reading for Saturday August 15, 2026: Book of Revelation (Revelation 11:19A; 12:1-6A, 10AB)

A woman appears in heaven clothed with the sun and crowned with twelve stars.

She wails in the pains of childbirth while a red dragon stands before her to seize the child.

The male child is taken up to God and heaven announces that salvation and power have come.

This is the vision of Revelation 11:19A 12:1-6A 10AB

Finding Eternal Hope in the Visions of Revelation

In the sacred scriptures the book of revelation stands as a profound source of encouragement for those who seek to live out their Catholic faith with dedication and devotion. This text which was written during times of persecution offers timeless lessons that resonate with believers today as they navigate the complexities of modern life. Through its symbolic language and powerful imagery the apocalypse reveals the ultimate victory of good over evil in a way that strengthens the resolve of the faithful. Catholics can draw upon these teachings to deepen their relationship with Christ and the church he established. The message invites all to remain steadfast in prayer and in the sacraments even when faced with trials that test their commitment.

What Does the Symbolic Language of Revelation Teach Us About Perseverance?

The opening chapters of this book present letters to seven churches that highlight both commendations and corrections for the early Christian communities. These messages underscore the importance of remaining faithful amid temptations and hardships that can distract from the path of righteousness. By examining these words Catholics today can reflect on their own spiritual lives and identify areas where greater vigilance is needed to avoid complacency in their practice of the faith. The imagery of lamps and stars serves as a reminder that the light of Christ must continue to shine through the actions and words of his followers in every generation. Such insights encourage a renewed commitment to the virtues that sustain the soul through difficult seasons.

The letters also warn against false teachings that might lead believers astray from the true deposit of faith handed down through the apostles. This caution remains relevant as contemporary culture presents numerous challenges to orthodox belief and moral living. Faithful Catholics find in these ancient words a call to examine their consciences regularly and to seek the guidance of the holy spirit in all decisions. Through this process individuals grow in wisdom and become better equipped to witness to the gospel in their families and communities. The emphasis on endurance points toward the reward that awaits those who hold fast to the end.

How Can the Heavenly Throne Room Scene Deepen Our Understanding of Worship?

The vision of the heavenly court with its elders and living creatures gathered around the throne provides a model for liturgical prayer that Catholics celebrate in the mass each week. This scene illustrates the continuous praise offered to God and invites believers to participate more fully in the sacred liturgy as a foretaste of eternal glory. By meditating on these images the faithful come to appreciate the connection between earthly worship and the heavenly reality that sustains it. The presence of the lamb who was slain reminds all that the sacrifice of Christ remains central to every act of adoration and thanksgiving. Such reflections help Catholics approach the sacraments with greater reverence and awe.

This heavenly perspective also reveals the unity of the church triumphant with the church on earth as both join in the same song of praise. Catholics who struggle with feelings of isolation in their faith journey can find comfort in knowing they are part of a vast communion of saints. The details of the vision such as the sea of glass and the multitude of angels emphasize the majesty and holiness of God which calls forth humble adoration from every heart. Regular contemplation of these truths fosters a deeper love for the eucharist and the other sacraments that nourish the soul. In this way the apocalypse becomes a practical guide for enriching personal and communal prayer.

Why Does the Apocalypse Emphasize the Final Victory of Christ for Our Daily Lives?

The later chapters describe the ultimate defeat of evil forces and the establishment of a new heaven and new earth where God dwells with his people forever. This promise offers Catholics a source of hope that transcends the sufferings and uncertainties of the present age. Believers are encouraged to live with an eternal perspective that influences their choices in work family and society. The imagery of the river of life and the tree of life points to the healing and renewal that flow from Christ to all who remain united with him. Such teachings motivate a life of virtue and charity as preparations for the joy that awaits the faithful.

The call to perseverance in the face of opposition reminds Catholics that their struggles have meaning within the larger story of salvation history. This understanding helps individuals face illness loss or persecution with courage rooted in the resurrection. The book underscores the role of the church as the bride of Christ prepared for the wedding feast which inspires a deeper appreciation for the bonds of faith and the sacraments that strengthen them. By keeping this victory in mind the faithful avoid despair and instead cultivate gratitude and trust in divine providence. The message ultimately directs attention back to the person of Jesus who holds the keys to death and the netherworld.

The entire narrative of revelation weaves together judgment mercy and promise in a tapestry that speaks directly to the hearts of practicing Catholics. It challenges readers to examine their readiness for the return of the lord while assuring them of his constant presence through the holy spirit. This balance prevents both presumption and fear allowing for a mature faith that grows through study and prayer. The text serves as an invitation to ongoing conversion and deeper union with the church. In all these ways it continues to inspire generations of believers to live with hope and fidelity.
Revelation 12 and the Call to Radiate Faith in Everyday Encounters

How Does the Opened Temple Guide Interactions at Home with Family

The reading begins with the temple in heaven being opened and the ark of the covenant revealed. This vision invites Catholics to see their own households as sacred spaces where faith becomes tangible through daily choices. In family settings the emphasis falls on nurturing patience when tensions arise over shared responsibilities like chores or schedules. One might recall the temple imagery to approach a disagreement with a spouse by first pausing in prayer before responding which fosters an atmosphere of mutual respect and understanding. Such an approach turns ordinary moments into opportunities for building lasting bonds grounded in divine presence.

The woman clothed with the sun with the moon under her feet and on her head a crown of twelve stars appears as a powerful sign of protection and glory. Parents can draw from this to model resilience when guiding children through challenges such as school pressures or peer influences. By embodying quiet strength and trust in God's plan family members learn to support one another without judgment. This leads to deeper conversations where faith is shared naturally rather than forced.

What Lessons from the Dragon and the Child Offer for Conversations with Friends

Moving into the account of the great red dragon and the male child the passage highlights conflict and ultimate divine rescue. With friends this section encourages Catholics to stand firm in values during discussions about current events or personal struggles. The child's snatching away to God's throne reminds one to offer encouragement that points toward hope instead of despair when a friend faces setbacks. Specific quotes like the loud voice proclaiming salvation and the power and the kingdom of our God can be woven into talks to affirm shared beliefs without confrontation.

Friends often engage in lighter exchanges so the wilderness nourishment for one thousand two hundred sixty days suggests providing steady support over time. This means checking in consistently rather than offering quick fixes which builds trust and opens doors for spiritual sharing. The breakdown of the dragon's threat shows how external pressures can be met with inner resolve drawn from scripture. Catholics thus become sources of calm in social circles.

In What Ways Might the Wilderness Nourishment Benefit Exchanges with Neighbors

The flight into the wilderness where the woman is nourished points to times of preparation and reliance on God amid uncertainty. For neighbors this inspires acts of quiet service such as helping with yard work or sharing resources during difficult seasons. One can reference the birth pangs and agony to empathize with a neighbor's hardships creating connections based on compassion rather than obligation. The temple opening earlier in the reading reinforces viewing community spaces as extensions of sacred trust.

Neighbors may hold differing views so focusing on the authority of his Messiah allows gentle reminders of higher purposes in casual greetings or block gatherings. This approach avoids division and instead highlights common ground like care for local families. Breaking down the child's rule with a rod of iron translates to advocating fairness in neighborhood matters with humility. Over time these interactions reflect the protective crown of stars by fostering safety and belonging.

How Can the Proclamation of Salvation Shape Workplace Dynamics with Co-Workers

At work the loud voice from heaven declaring now have come the salvation and the power and the kingdom of our God and the authority of his Messiah serves as a call to integrity in professional tasks. Catholics might apply this by handling deadlines or team projects with a sense of eternal perspective that reduces stress for everyone involved. The dragon sweeping stars to earth warns against gossip or negativity which can be countered by redirecting conversations toward constructive solutions. Specific quotes from the passage like the woman giving birth to a son can inspire reflections on new beginnings in career discussions.

Co-workers benefit from consistent reliability so the nourishment in the wilderness encourages mentoring others patiently during transitions. This differs from family by remaining more task-oriented yet infused with grace that builds professional respect. The overall vision of the woman prompts one to carry dignity into meetings ensuring decisions align with ethical standards. Such practices turn the office into a place where faith subtly influences outcomes for the good of all.

Spotlighting Quotes for Real-Life Application Across Relationships

Several lines stand out for direct use in daily talks. The temple in heaven was opened reminds individuals to invite divine wisdom before any exchange. The woman was pregnant and was crying out in birth pangs helps express empathy when others share burdens. Then the dragon stood before the woman who was about to bear a child encourages vigilance against divisive influences in groups. Finally the child was snatched away and taken to God and to his throne offers reassurance of protection in uncertain times. These elements together equip Catholics to respond thoughtfully in varied settings.

The reading calls believers to integrate these heavenly signs into ordinary routines with care and consistency. Each relationship gains from tailored applications that honor the passage's layers from temple to wilderness to proclamation. Over time this practice deepens personal faith while enriching connections around them.

text:
Fuel Subsidy: The Debate Nigeria Never Finished

By Halimah Nuhu Sanda

For three years, Nigerians have been told to endure the pain of fuel subsidy removal because the country could no longer afford the old system. We were told that the resources previously spent subsidising petrol would be redirected towards infrastructure, healthcare, education, security and other investments capable of producing a stronger economy. Three years later, the subsidy debate has returned with renewed force, this time as one of the emerging fault lines of the 2027 presidential contest. Atiku Abubakar says he will restore subsidy. President Bola Tinubu says bringing it back would be economically reckless. Peter Obi says subsidy removal was necessary but its proceeds have been badly managed. Other presidential contenders have offered variations ranging from targeted intervention to a complete rejection of the assumptions underlying the current policy. Beneath all these political arguments, however, lies a much simpler question ordinary Nigerians have every right to ask: what exactly are we getting in return for the sacrifice?

Atiku’s intervention has reopened a wound that never really healed. He has insisted that if elected, he would restore petrol subsidy, although his position has subsequently been framed as targeted support rather than a return to the old import-subsidy regime. Atiku argues that Nigerians are carrying the consequences of higher energy and transportation costs and that government must restore purchasing power. His argument resonates because the consequences of subsidy removal have travelled far beyond the price displayed at filling stations. Fuel costs have affected transportation, food, small businesses and household budgets. For many Nigerians, the reform is experienced not as an abstract fiscal adjustment but as the reason virtually everything costs more.

Yet Atiku’s position deserves scrutiny as much as the government’s does. He supported subsidy removal during the 2023 presidential campaign, making his current position an obvious target for criticism. His camp has also spent part of this week clarifying whether the proposed subsidy would be temporary or open-ended before Atiku himself reiterated that his position had not changed. A subsidy may provide relief, but Nigerians deserve to know how much it would cost, who would benefit, how it would be funded and how the country would prevent the corruption and opacity that characterised the old system.

President Tinubu’s argument, on the other hand, is that Nigeria could not continue with a system that placed an enormous burden on public finances while creating opportunities for abuse. The administration maintains that subsidy removal was a necessary reform and that returning to the old model would simply recreate the problems Nigeria had decided to confront. According to the Finance Ministry, the reforms associated with subsidy removal and foreign-exchange liberalisation generated ₦15.8 trillion in additional resources for the Federation between June 2023 and December 2025, with ₦5.4 trillion accruing to the Federal Government and ₦10.4 trillion distributed to states and local governments.

But this is where the government’s argument encounters the reality of the Nigerian household. A fiscal improvement is important, but it cannot be the only measure of a successful economic reform. If government tells citizens that a painful policy is necessary because it will free resources for development, citizens are entitled to ask where the development is. Government has explained that the resources have been absorbed by increased expenditure, debt servicing, higher wages and other fiscal pressures. Yet the ordinary Nigerian is not measuring the reform by government accounting. They are measuring it by the cost of getting to work, feeding their families, sending their children to school and accessing healthcare.

Peter Obi’s intervention is therefore significant because he refuses to accept the easy argument that hardship automatically proves subsidy removal was wrong. Obi has explicitly said that he still supports subsidy removal and that the mismanagement of the proceeds should not be a reason to reverse the policy. His criticism is that Nigerians were not given an adequate alternative use for the resources recovered from subsidy.

That distinction deserves much more attention. Perhaps the greatest weakness of Nigeria’s subsidy reform was not that the government removed the subsidy, but that it failed to build a sufficiently visible social contract around the reform. When citizens are told that they must pay more today so that the country can become stronger tomorrow, tomorrow cannot remain an indefinite promise. People need to see the connection between their sacrifice and better public transportation, functioning hospitals, stronger schools, food security and opportunities for productive enterprise.

The other presidential contenders make the debate even more interesting. Omoyele Sowore represents the argument that subsidy itself should not necessarily be treated as the enemy and that the real problem is the corruption and inefficiency surrounding its administration. His position provides an important counterpoint to those who regard subsidy removal as inherently necessary.

Seyi Makinde, meanwhile, has criticised the simultaneous removal of subsidy and floating of the naira as a double shock that required stronger cushioning measures for Nigerians. His argument moves the conversation towards sequencing and social protection rather than simply asking whether subsidy is good or bad. Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim has offered another variation, arguing for a more targeted and transparent intervention rather than a return to the old system. These positions remind us that the choice is not necessarily between unlimited subsidy and complete abandonment of government intervention.

And then there is Donald Duke, whose argument I find perhaps the most intellectually provocative. Rather than simply accepting the language of the debate, Duke has challenged the premise itself, questioning whether what Nigeria called fuel subsidy was ever a genuine and transparent subsidy system in the first place. His intervention forces us to ask a more fundamental question: what exactly are we trying to remove or restore? If the system itself was opaque and corrupt, simply arguing about whether to bring it back may be missing the point.

Taken together, these positions reveal that Nigeria’s political class is not actually debating one question. They are debating several. Should government subsidise petrol? Should it subsidise vulnerable Nigerians instead? Should the savings from subsidy removal be invested in public services? Should domestic production be supported to bring prices down? Should government intervene temporarily during periods of economic shock? And perhaps most importantly, how do we protect citizens from the consequences of necessary economic reform without recreating the fiscal leakages that made the old system unsustainable?

This last question deserves to become the centre of Nigeria’s conversation.

Subsidising petrol is not necessarily the same thing as subsidising Nigerians. A universal subsidy benefits everyone who buys petrol, including those who can comfortably afford its true market price. A targeted social protection system could instead concentrate scarce public resources on poor households, public transport users, farmers, small businesses and other groups most exposed to energy-price shocks. Such a system could be accompanied by investment in mass transportation, domestic refining, food production, healthcare and other measures that reduce the transmission of fuel prices into the cost of living.

This is where the subsidy debate should ultimately take us. Nigeria does not have to choose between pretending that petrol can remain artificially cheap forever and abandoning citizens to absorb every consequence of market reform. There is a middle ground, but it requires something Nigeria has historically struggled to provide: transparent, accountable and disciplined government.

The question, therefore, should no longer be simply whether subsidy should be removed or restored. The harder and more important question is what kind of economy Nigeria wants to build after subsidy.

If government chooses to remove subsidy, it must demonstrate what Nigerians are receiving in return. If an opposition candidate promises to restore it, that candidate must explain how it will be financed, targeted and protected from the corruption of the past. If another candidate supports its removal, that candidate must explain how the resulting fiscal space will translate into better lives. And if someone proposes a middle path, Nigerians deserve to see the numbers, the safeguards and the implementation plan.

Because Nigerians do not necessarily need cheap petrol forever. They need an economy in which they can afford the petrol they buy.

The success of subsidy removal was never going to be measured simply by whether government could stop paying the subsidy. It should be measured by whether the country could turn that difficult sacrifice into a more productive economy, stronger public services and a better quality of life. Until Nigerians can see that connection, the subsidy debate will continue to return, election after election, because the real issue has never been only the price of petrol. It is the price Nigerians are being asked to pay for reform, and whether anyone can convincingly show them what that sacrifice is buying.

text:
Infold: Between a Rock and Hard Place.

Many of us know the story of The Odyssey, one of Homer's most iconic works of ancient Greek literature.

Let's step back.
Hubris. 
Feeling far too prideful and confident in oneself.
There was one mistake that Odysseus  made that follows him throughout his entire quest to get back to Ithaca.

For this interpretation I will be relying on a few major sources of work, such as the Iliad, the Odyssey (both by Ancient Greek poet Homer), The Trojan Women by Euripides, and, for fun, Jorge Riveras-Herrans Epic the Musical. This is an interpretation of said works in relation to Infold’s past and current mistakes. Greek mythology is notorious for being inconsistent across surviving sources, so I will draw from these rather than treating the whole thing as definitive.

When Odysseus allowed his hubris to dictate his choices, the consequences followed him far beyond the moment that he made them.

Infold, has likewise, been steering that exact same ship since June 30th.  
In order for us to see how they got there, we have to go back a ways. 

Back to the Trojan Horse, which in this case, is Love and Deepspace. Released in January 2024, LaDS was the first of its kind in the CN/Global market. An otome with high-end 3D modeling, intimacy systems, cinematic presentations, gacha monetization, all wrapped together. They have no competition at this stage. 

This gets them inside the walls of the market (Troy in the Iliad) where they can technically define it themselves.

On June 30th, they made the first of many mistakes that would follow them through this odyssey that we are all still on as of writing this on August 31st, 2026.
We will, canonically, be using the Odyssey as a framework but for this to make sense, the initial problem arose with the introduction of the 6th Love Interest, Valko. 

Valko, much like Astyanax, the son of Hector, was killed simply for what he represented, not for what he did or is. Astyanax was but a child, yet Odysseus urged for his death or else Astyanax would avenge Troy when he reached adulthood, and rebuild his home city to be much stronger and lead them himself. 
In the retelling of the story of Troy, Euripides’ tragedy The Trojan Women, Odysseus argued for the child's death, out of fear of what he could become. 
I am not suggesting the situations are equivalent,and we can’t know every consideration behind Infold's decision. The parallel lies in the thought of perceived risk. Astyanax is condemned not for anything he did or has done, but for what others fear he may eventually represent.
Sound familiar? 

Consequences have a way of gaining momentum though, as every Greek epic focuses on.
Most of the sailing for Infold was mildly choppy before the introduction of Valko. Some of the rougher seas occurred when Infold released the 5th Love Interest, Caleb. 
Yet, after the release, the player base settled back into a wave of semi-normalcy. 

For this reference, I am going to use the cyclops, Polyphemus. Polyphemus here will represent growing player complaints, unanswered survey suggestions and overall dissatisfaction with the company as a whole. 

Stranded in the cave with Polyphemus , Odysseus uses his wit to convince the cyclops to share wine with them. In this case, Infold quickly reassures current players it will focus on the five current love interests after the cancellation. After the cyclops falls asleep, Odysseus and his men blind him, but here comes the vital part. 

When sailing from the island, he lets hubris get the better of him. He tells the cyclops his name.
Odysseus’s hubris is speaking when he should be silent. 
Infold’s hubris is remaining silent when they should speak up. 

In doing so, Infold as well as our doomed King of Ithaca, both encountered an outlying force neither saw coming. 

Fed up with being ignored by a company who refused to listen to them, many Chinese players spoke out, some well within their reason while others took it to the extremes. 

The seas were becoming increasingly unstable for Infold. Being unrivalled in the industry lets them think too highly of themselves and thus enters Poseidon. In our parallel, he will represent Chinese narrative and reputational pressure. 

The aggrieved Polyphemus does indeed tell his father, Poseidon the name of the king who blinded him. This begins the biggest hurdle of the journey so far, as the god of the oceans and seas is not easy to escape from, nor is he known for his leniency. |

Once Poseidon has taken notice of Odysseus, the ship's stability and the safety of his crew, become a bigger tackled objective. 

In this situation, CN narrative comes down quite hard on Infold, and very quickly. The ship rocks violently. Many men are lost (players) from the inability of Infold to handle the situation in a timely manner.  Many ships are also lost in his fleet (strength and scale of the game).

After their encounter with Poseidon, Odysseus and his men go through many more trials and tribulations. 

Banners, solos, incentivized paywall aesthetics. Each one of these represent a monster that they have to face. 
Like Odysseus, Infold did not travel directly from one crisis to the next. Banners came and went. Solo events released. New monetization incentives appeared. Some temporarily steadied revenue while others made their own controversies. The ship continued forward, but the conflict persisted. 

The pressure from CN narrative was slightly less by this point, and as such they were still on rough seas. Men did die, and men were hungry and tired and just wanted to get off this damn boat. 

Which brings us to the moment of Scylla and Charybdis. Two choices but each having their own cost. 

On one side of the Strait of Messina, there lay a monster named Scylla. 
Her fate of being a monster was not her own choice, I should let you know. She loved the sea-god Glaucus, and in many retellings, so did Circe. Circe, in her anger and jealousy, turned Scylla into a massive monster with six dog heads who were always hungry. 
For this story, Scylla will represent those in favor of returning Valko. 
To sail close to her, Odysseus would have to lose 6 men off his ship. 
(For transparency, this origin of Scylla is pulled from Ovid, which is a later Roman retelling)

On the other side was a giant whirlpool monster, Charybdis. 
She was also not originally cursed to be this way. She aided her father, Poseidon, in the paternal war against his brother Zeus. As such she was cursed with becoming a ravenous ocean maw.
For this story, Charybis is the faction against his return. 
To sail close to her could mean the entirety of the only ship could be lost. 
Men and all. 
Game and all. 

Infold, as of writing this, August 31st 2026, is at the proverbial Strait. Staring two losses in the face. 

Scylla, Valko supporters, do not equate to victory. 
Neither is Charybdis.
Neither offers Infold a painless passage at this point. 
Neither monster represents the morality of either faction. They represent business risks Infold faces in choosing a course. 

There is no escape without some loss. 
The opportunity may have already sailed long past.  

So now Infold has to ask.

Which loss leaves enough crew- and enough ship- to make it back home to Ithaca?

OGcom Review - USA Prediction Markets platform
Guide: Fees, Bonus, App, and CryptoCom Rails

OG is a standalone prediction market from CryptoCom that lets me trade Yes/No contracts on sports, politics, culture, and economics, and this OGcom review 2026 covers fees, banking, and how the product feels after live tests.

I opened an OG account on OGcom, claimed the trade-$10-get-$10 path, checked sports markets beside thinner culture boards, and compared fills with other prediction market sites before I sized up.

   - Key Takeaways

        - OG is a prediction market powered by CryptoCom | Derivatives North America, a CFTC-registered designated contract market that clears US prediction activity under federal exchange rules.

        - You trade Yes/No prediction contracts priced in cents; if your prediction is correct, the market settles near one dollar, and you can exit early at the current market price when depth allows.

        - OG offers a strong new-user path, often framed as a $10 welcome offer after a qualifying first trade, plus referral ladders that can stack extra bonus credit.

        - The OG app is mobile-first with App Store and Google Play listings, live chat on event pages, and parlays on eligible sports legs, though limit orders are still missing.

        - Fees are easy to model on a flat per-contract schedule, cash-outs lean on ACH, and Call 1-800-GAMBLER prediction trading remains real-money risk if you size poorly.

   - What is OG dot com?

OGcom is a prediction market brand CryptoCom launched in February 2026 as a focused sister experience beside the main wallet.

OG operates through CryptoCom Derivatives North America, so the consumer-facing side is OG while exchange and clearing functions sit with the registered venue behind it.

In practice, OG works like other binary boards: I pick a question, buy Yes or No, and hold until the market resolves or I sell to another trader.

An event contract usually sits between one cent and ninety-nine cents, and that cent figure is the crowd's implied read before fees.

Winners pay one dollar per share when settlement posts, and losers go to zero, which keeps max loss equal to what I paid plus fees.

Friends still ask the OG legit question after week one; I say the corporate and regulatory story is solid, while sports depth and order tools decide daily fit.

OG allows early exits when another trader is willing, which beats waiting on a house cash-out button.

Using OG feels closer to a clean consumer trading platform than to a crowded multi-product wallet, and that focus is what sets OG apart for me.

   - Legal Status and Access

OG is available across most of the United States for adults who pass KYC, with notable gaps such as New York and Arizona called out in recent access guides.

Sports event contracts can be blocked in extra states even when culture or economics boards stay open, so I confirm eligibility inside the product.

CryptoCom Derivatives North America sits under Commodity Futures Trading Commission oversight, which is why reviewers describe federal exchange oversight rather than an offshore book.

A CFTC-regulated prediction market label matters because fund rules, surveillance, and settlement standards follow exchange practice.

Sign up for OG with email or an existing CryptoCom sign-in, finish identity checks, then fund before you make your first prediction. New York, California, Miami, and 40 other states.

   - How Trading Works

Prediction markets work by turning a real-world event into tradable Yes and No shares that other people can take the other side of.

I read market prices as probabilities, then I only trade when my view differs enough to cover fees and slippage.

Sports prediction markets on this board borrow language fans already know (moneylines, spreads, totals, and props) so a sports betting refugee can learn the ticket quickly.

Combo-style legs appear on eligible games, which is a consumer feature many prediction platforms still underplay.

Non-sports markets include politics, economics, crypto prints, companies, and culture, though market coverage there is thinner than on the deepest rivals.

Market categories are easy to browse, and I start on thick game boards before I touch quieter economics ticks.

Contract horizons matter for risk: short-dated games recycle capital fast, while long-dated politics can lock cash for weeks, so market types should match your holding plan.

Depth also swings hard by kickoff time and headline heat, including market volatility around injury news and sudden polling swings, which is why market liquidity checks come before size.

OG supports quick ticket entry for beginners, yet I still size thin overnight props tiny until I see clean exits.

New prediction listings appear often around big calendars, and offering prediction access on both sports and culture is the growth push CryptoCom is making.

   - Fees and Banking

OG charges a flat fee when I open a position and again if I close early, while holding through settlement usually avoids an extra settlement cut on the schedule I tested.

That simple math helps beginners even if high-volume traders may still prefer maker-friendly curves elsewhere.

ACH-style funding is typically free, while cards and wallets can add percentage fees that eat small bankrolls.

Withdrawal timing depends on bank rails, and cash-outs I tracked often landed in one to three business days after approval.

A second withdrawal request in the same week taught me to finish verification early and avoid same-day expectations after a fresh deposit.

CryptoCom balances can help funding habits, yet I still treat trading cash as risk capital rather than spending money.

   - Bonuses and Codes

An OG promo code hunt is often unnecessary when partner links already unlock the standard path, but campaign pages still circulate codes during push weeks.

The OGcom promo code conversation usually points to a trade-$10-get-$10 style 10 bonus after a qualifying ticket within a short window.

OG offers layered referral milestones that can pay both sides as settled volume climbs, which is more aggressive than many rival venues.

A referral code can matter for those ladders, so I check the rewards tab before I invite friends.

OG welcome bonus terms change, and some periods push larger multi-day boosts that reviewers summarized as an up-to-$100 welcome bonus.

I treat every bonus as practice capital, because fees and soft prices can erase the gift if I chase noise.

Promo code pages go stale fast; I always re-read the in-app offer card before I count on credit.

Welcome offer value is one reason casual users try OG first, yet the product still has to clear on fees and fills after the credit lands.

For a 10 welcome offer to pay off, I make a planned trade instead of tapping the first flashing board I see.

   - OG Prediction Markets App Experience

This app review focuses on speed, clarity, and what is missing for serious order control.

The OGcom app feels built for thumbs: market lists load quickly, tickets are short, and social chat on event pages adds noise or signal depending on the room.

Store scores sit in the solid-four range in several roundups, with Android sometimes trailing iOS in early samples.

A dedicated prediction market app matters because the main CryptoCom wallet is crowded; OG choices favor a clean prediction-first home screen.

Leaderboards and parlay hubs are fun extras, yet the lack of resting limit orders still frustrates me when prices jump mid-tap.

I want depth stats before I trade event contracts in thin books, and classic order-book tooling still lags exchange-style rivals.

Even so, the mobile app is where I place most live sports tickets because the flow is faster than desktop for game-day adjustments.

   - Trustpilot Reviews about OG prediction markets platform

Public feedback on Trustpilot for related OG Network pages is mixed, so I read patterns instead of chasing any single star rating.

Paraphrased themes I kept seeing include:

   - "Verification took longer than I expected, but once funded the ticket felt simple for sports contracts."

   - "Chat answered a cash-out timing question, though I still waited on the bank side."

   - "I liked the bonus credit, yet I wish limit orders existed for volatile games."

   - "Interface is clean compared with heavier crypto wallets I tried before."

OG customer support paths lean on in-app chat and email, and my test questions cleared faster than email-only desks I have used elsewhere.

Human help quality will decide retention for banking edge cases more than any marketing banner will.

   - Pros and Cons

   - What I Like

       - Clear CryptoCom backing and Derivatives North America exchange plumbing.
       - Strong sports menu plus emerging prediction coverage in culture and macro.
       - Useful bonus and referral ladders versus many dry prediction market apps.
       - Fast consumer UI that helps newcomers place a first trade without a finance degree.

   - What Holds Me Back

       - No limit orders and thin book visibility hurt precision entries.
       - Non-sports depth still trails the widest rival menus.
       - Card funding fees can punish tiny deposits.
       - State sports limits can change what you can trade overnight.

       - Who It Fits

I recommend OG for US adults who want a CryptoCom-linked prediction market platform with sports-first energy and simple fee math.

Active traders who need resting orders may prefer venues like OG rivals with fuller books, while still keeping this account for bonuses and mobile speed.

Casual fans who already bet game lines will pick up cents-as-probability in one session.

If you only want politics density, other boards may feel deeper; if you want a polished consumer prediction market platform with promos, this brand belongs on the shortlist.

Markets at OG reward people who check settlement rules, confirm state access, and size for liquidity instead of vibes.

       - A Final Word

This OG review lands positive on legitimacy and product focus, with deductions for missing pro order tools.

Sports boards are ready for everyday games and headline events, and CryptoCom's exchange stack is the trust anchor behind the brand.

An OG prediction market review has to weigh bonus value against fee drag and state limits, and on that scorecard I still keep the account funded.

Prediction markets review roundups keep ranking this entrant as a serious US option, and my live tests agree on UX while asking for limit orders next.

Listing growth will continue if the parent company pushes more markets, partnerships, and tooling through the year.

For now I trade smaller on thin ticks, I trade larger on liquid games, and I only risk cash I can lose.

       - FAQs

   - Is this platform safe for eligible adults?
Yes, for eligible adults who complete KYC. Trading runs on Derivatives North America rails, a CFTC-registered exchange and clearing stack. You can still lose funds, and some sports listings are state-limited.

   - How do I place a first trade?
Create or reuse a CryptoCom sign-in, finish identity checks, deposit, then buy Yes or No. Many new users aim for the qualifying ticket that unlocks the standard $10 style credit.

   - What fees should I expect?
Plan for a flat fee when you open and again if you close early. Holding through settlement often avoids an extra settlement fee on the published consumer schedule. Card deposits can add percentage costs.

   - Are signup credits available?
Yes, offers rotate. The common path is a small matched credit after a qualifying trade, plus referral milestones. Always read the live rewards card because terms change.

   - Is there a phone client?
Yes. iOS and Android clients plus a mobile web flow are available. Store ratings are generally solid, with Android sometimes trailing iOS in early samples.

   - Can I trade sports and other categories?

text:
Social media algorithms are military grade mind control weapons and you walk in everyday unarmed.

Everybody knows the feeling. You are locked in on work, emails, a lift at the gym, real momentum building. Then you open the phone for thirty seconds and all of it drains out of you. Thirty seconds turns into five minutes, then ten minutes, and soon that life force called 'momentum' is gone.

That two minute scroll is not a mindless break. That is your brain being hijacked by an AI built by the smartest engineers alive, and nothing like it has existed at any other point in human history.

That foggy brain rot feeling afterward is the price you paid for a "quick" doom scroll. Most people pay it twenty times a day and wonder why they can't focus or why they feel stuck. The ones who learn to manage that power have an edge over an entire generation losing their minds to slop on X, Instagram, and TikTok. That advantage compounds daily.

Here is what I do to manage this modern day trap.

Firstly, you must be able to detox for six months minimum, especially Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook. Deactivate Instagram and TikTok outright. Don't just delete the apps. Make it hard for you to just do a "quick scroll". Set app limits on whatever survives so opening it forces a deliberate click instead of a reflex, and turn your iPhone action button into a black and white on demand button so nothing colorful and shiny pulls you in.

Notifications off for everything except money. Not even your girl gets a ping, she can call if she needs something. Parents and friends too. We were not designed as humans to have notifications pinging every 2 seconds. Find the flow state and protect it.

Next, delete X when you are not posting, and when you are on it, scroll, read, learn, and reply. Don't just endlessly consume. Replying, even random shit, instead of consuming rewires the brain from a spectator to participant, and hitting not interested on anything lustful, sports highlights, or slop starves the feed until it has nothing left to offer you aside from something knowledgeable.

YouTube, turn off search history and watch history so there is no content being pushed to you. You should have as little algorithms steering your brain one certain way as possible. If you go on YouTube you should be going on there for an exact reason to look up, not to just click in and check the feed. Even Snapchat, takes two seconds to hide friend suggestions with random public stories popping up on your feed.

Every one of these takes two minutes to set up and pays back hours of clear thinking every week.

In the beginning you will reach for those apps without thinking.. this is a clear sign of an addiction. Don't be alarmed as the vast majority of the population has this issue. It's just part of the game in 2026. Once you delete TikTok and IG you will see that you'll start scrolling on LinkedIn. Don't fight it. Just be aware of it and laugh it off and tell yourself, "close the fucking app and go do something productive." Even 10 pushups or 10 pull-ups after catching yourself scrolling works to rewire the brain not to do it again.

Create, post, close the app, touch grass. That is the whole system. Your competition can't do this, that is why they are stuck. The quicker you control your mind, the quicker you can take advantage.

Your attention and life force are scarce assets.

Protect them, invest them, and compound them the same way you would with cash, Bitcoin, gold, or any other asset.

That's how winners win.

#ASCO 2026 HR+ #BreastCancerAdjuvant #olaparib is prioritized over CDK4/6 inhibition in gBRCA1/2 and PALB2 carriers with 4+ nodes, or high-risk residual after neoadjuvant chemo. Strength: Strong.
OlympiA HR+/HER2-negative subgroup: OS 0.90 (0.45 to 1.78) NS. Abemaciclib OS in monarchE is 0.84 (0.72 to 0.98) at high certainty, same subtype. 
The Strong rec appears to derive from the overall OlympiA population, mostly triple-negative, where OS certainty was rated low.
On sequencing. Offered with no data, based on entry windows. monarchE allowed abemaciclib within 16 months of surgery, NATALEE within 12 months of starting ET. A year of olaparib ends near 21 months post-op, past monarchE and at the edge of NATALEE, and overlapping cytopenias add a recovery interval that closes the rest. The bigger caveat is biological: PARPi can select BRCA reversion, restoring HR and cross-resistance to PARPi and platinum, so the order affects what is left for MBC.
What I do. Node-negative: consider ribociclib only in a young, high-risk patient, grade 3 T2N0 or high genomic risk. 1 to 3 nodes: ribociclib, or abemaciclib if grade 3, T ≥5 cm, or Ki-67 ≥20%. 4+ nodes is not straightforward: abemaciclib has the survival benefit, but if gBRCA the guideline steers to olaparib, and it won’t be easy to get both.
We need a trial of which goes first. Not Strong. #bcsm

text:
The men who bolted Atlanta's segregation wall into the road were mostly Black city workers. That is in the record, and it happened six days before Christmas 1962 on Peyton Road in southwest Atlanta. A Black surgeon had bought a house on the far side of that road, and the city answered by closing two of them. Somebody's granddaddy came off that job and never said one word about it at the table.

The next morning, somebody on the white side of those boards walked out to the road carrying wrapping paper and ribbon.

They decorated a segregation barricade. Underneath the words Road Closed, somebody added, "Thank the Lord!"

Peyton Road and Harlan Road had both been shut by order of the mayor and the Board of Aldermen. That much has been told before, when it gets told at all.

By that December, the mayor's office had already been handling this exact situation street by street all year long, and was keeping a running count.

The letters had started arriving at City Hall in the summer, five months before anybody put a board in a road.

On July 20, 1962, a man living at 681 Fielding Lane wrote to Mayor Ivan Allen Jr. about the fear moving through a proud community. Then he listed his evidence.

Cars rolling slowly through the neighborhood, stopping while people pointed at houses. A lot of them carrying out-of-town plates, which he took to mean the drivers were being paid to agitate.

Night calls from a Black realty company to fifteen or twenty homes on every street, asking whether anybody wanted to list. Houses in Peyton and Utoy Forest ran from twenty-one to twenty-eight thousand dollars, he noted, and every single owner had signed a petition.

The petition said they wished "to remain all white."

Five days later a woman named Barbara M. Farmer wrote from 512 Haldane Drive, speaking for the neighborhood. She reminded the mayor how much tax money Atlanta stood to lose if families like hers got pushed out to the suburbs.

No Black family had moved in yet. This was still July.

By December they had a name to put in the file.

A typed memo went up to the mayor's desk. A man named Sid Avery had telephoned to report that Foster Eugene Bennett had sold his property at 483 Fielding Lane to Dr. Clinton Warner, who was then living at 2491 Dale Creek Drive on the other side of town.

Fielding Lane was the same street the July letter had come from, about two hundred house numbers down.

Bennett had been getting threatening calls of his own. He was already moving out to a house he owned on Columbia Drive over in Decatur.

Avery wanted a police captain alerted about the danger he saw coming. And he wanted the mayor of Atlanta to "take immediate action to see that Dr. Warner does not move in," because otherwise there would be trouble.

That memo is still in the file, typed up neat and passed along like any other piece of city business. The man it asked the mayor to stop was a surgeon named Clinton Warner.

Warner had already gone a long way for this country before he ever went looking for that house.

He served in the Army from 1942 to 1946, and both his obituary and his oral history place him in the D-Day landings in France. He came home to Morehouse, then to Meharry Medical College in Nashville, where he finished summa cum laude in 1951.

By 1962 he was a surgeon in Atlanta and the college physician at Spelman, running the infirmary there. He had a practice, a reputation, and sixty thousand dollars for a house.

The builder who sold it to him was in financial trouble and had not been able to find one white buyer for it. Warner put it plainly in 2003, when a reporter asked him what he had been trying to prove.

"I just needed a home," he said. He added that it was an expensive home, and nobody else was there to buy it.

He moved in. That was the exact thing the telephone call had been made to prevent.

His new neighbors dumped garbage on his lawn. They left messages at his office and told him they would burn the house down.

Then they went downtown and asked City Hall for a wall, and City Hall gave them one.

The Board of Aldermen approved it on December 17. Ivan Allen Jr. signed it into law the same day.

Rodney Mims Cook Sr. was one of the few aldermen who voted no, and he said so out loud at the State Capitol. According to his son, the Klan came and burned a cross in the Cook family's front yard afterward.

City maintenance crews built the thing, and those crews were made up mostly of Black workers. They arrived on Peyton Road on the morning of December 18.

Black men on the city payroll, out in the December cold, bolting down a wall designed to keep families who looked like them on the far side of a road. Six days before Christmas, with the paychecks that fed their own children depending on finishing the job.

What they bolted down were beams painted black and white, fixed to steel I-beams and sunk into the pavement. The whole thing stood roughly three feet high.

A grown man could step over it without effort. He simply could not drive through it.

The crew packed up its tools and went home that evening. The next morning, on the white side of the boards, the people it had been built for came out and wrapped the work in Christmas paper.

On the other side of those boards, Bette Graves Thomas was seventeen years old.

She told the Atlanta Journal-Constitution decades later that 1963 was the year her family could not turn left. "I remember it being inconvenient," she said.

The way around added as much as five miles to a trip that had been one turn of a steering wheel. She also said, without any hedging, that she believed they were being treated unfairly because of the color of their skin.

She was not the only one saying so out loud that winter.

On December 22, four days after the boards went down, a wire came into City Hall from Atlanta University. It was signed by Ralph Moore, chairman of the Committee on Appeal for Human Rights.

The students opened by telling the mayor he had made a serious mistake. Then they told him exactly what they could put in the street.

A hundred and seventy-five picketers a day in the West End business district. No fewer than fifteen hundred students on the steps of City Hall, enough, they said, to turn the eyes of the world onto what they were already calling the Atlanta wall.

The mayor wrote back at length. That letter is still sitting in his papers at Georgia Tech.

Allen wanted the students to see the complete record before they embarrassed anybody. Peyton and Harlan, he explained, was the fifty-second area or street in Atlanta to undergo what he called neighborhood expansion, penetration or encroachment since the first of that year.

Fifty-second.

"The record is almost flawless," he wrote, meaning the city's record on protecting the rights of its Black citizens. And then he told the students he was enclosing the list.

Fifty-one streets. Handled inside twelve months, to what he described as the complete satisfaction of the Black community, and he hoped the students would read it over carefully and say they were satisfied too.

He called what was happening on Fielding Lane agitation, stirred up by unscrupulous people, white and Black alike. He wrote that closing the two roads inconvenienced mostly white citizens and practically no Black ones.

Allen finished by asking the students not to damage Atlanta's record with unnecessary demonstrations. If they insisted on picketing City Hall for the publicity, he offered to come out and receive them on the steps himself.

Bette Graves Thomas was seventeen and sitting in a car on the other side of the sentence about inconvenience. She was adding five miles to every trip her family made, and her own mayor had put it in writing that it cost her nothing at all.

Out on Peyton Road, one night, Black residents pulled the barriers out of the pavement and dumped them in a creek. The next day white residents rebuilt them out of trees and rocks.

That version was burned to the ground.

Early the following Monday, city crews came back and sank fresh beams into the scorched asphalt. This time they bolted steel rails onto them so the thing could not be burned again.

Monday night and Tuesday night, small groups of robed men walked that street to guard it. They carried signs reading "Whites Have Rights, Too."

The robed men made the record. The people who had carried the first set of boards down to the creek did not, and there is no list of their names anywhere.

The record kept better track of City Hall. On January 7 the aldermen voted to keep the barricades exactly where they were, and the attorney for the residents opposing them took the case to Fulton County Superior Court.

Four days after that vote, a local television station ran an editorial calling Peyton Road a "symbol of failure for Atlanta," and said it would be dishonest to read it any other way. Then the same script told everyone to settle down, insisted this was not a Berlin Wall situation, and warned that dramatizing it would only make the problem worse.

Black Atlanta did not settle down. Students picketed City Hall, shoppers pulled their money out of West End stores, and the Committee on Appeal for Human Rights, SNCC and the Atlanta Committee for Cooperative Action ran the campaign together.

Martin Luther King Sr. called it one of the gravest mistakes the city had ever made. The Atlanta Urban League's R. A. Thompson quietly wrote a New York attorney in February to say a visiting United Nations delegation should probably stay home, because Atlanta could not be shown off in that condition.

Ordinary people wrote in too. On February 11 the Calloway Drive Community Club, speaking for a set of neighborhood churches and clubs, sent the mayor a short, careful letter calling the barricades "this stigma on the City of Atlanta."

The mail was coming from outside Georgia by then. A college student in Maryland wrote that same month for the mayor's side of it, because she had a term paper on the Peyton Road barricade due on March 8.

Her deadline landed a week after the case was decided. She told the mayor she had always been proud of Atlanta's race relations.

The case was argued in Fulton County Superior Court by attorney Donald Hollowell. On March 1, 1963, Judge George P. Whitman ruled the closings "unreasonable, arbitrary, and capricious."

The city did not appeal. The barricades came out in about twenty minutes, and a city that had spent two and a half months defending them needed less than half an hour to make them disappear.

Seventy-two days, start to finish. The neighborhood they were built to hold together lasted five months longer.

Inside a month, most of the houses in Peyton Forest were listed for sale with Black real estate agents. One of them belonged to Virgil Copeland, a Lockheed employee who headed the homeowners' association and had personally gone to the mayor to ask for the barricade.

Copeland told a reporter that once the barricades came down, the whole thing collapsed, and that it was finished for people like him out there. He said they were hunting for somewhere past the city limits to buy, and that everybody he knew was leaving Atlanta.

By the end of July 1963, fifteen white families were left in the entire neighborhood.

Five months after the boards came out of the road, Ivan Allen Jr. flew to Washington at President Kennedy's request.

On July 26, 1963, he walked into the Senate Commerce Committee hearing room in a dark suit and testified in favor of the public accommodations bill. He was the only Southern elected official in the country willing to do it, and he was certain it would end his career.

He wrote later that he had been "completely in error" on Peyton Road, and that he had gone at the whole problem in a crude way.

Atlanta made very sure to remember him for the trip to Washington.

There is an Ivan Allen Jr. Boulevard downtown and an Ivan Allen College of Liberal Arts at Georgia Tech. There is a hundred-thousand-dollar Ivan Allen Jr. Prize for Social Courage.

In November 2019 the city dedicated a bridge in his name and built it out as an open-air walking museum, so younger generations would understand what he had done for Atlanta.

Fifty-one streets got none of that.

No ruling. No headline, no photograph in a research center, no argument in the newspapers about what to call them.

They were handled. That is the word the record uses, and the record was proud of it.

Somebody's grandmother lived on one of those fifty-one streets. Whatever happened there got settled without a headline, and she never told the story afterward, because on her street there was nothing left standing to point at.

The fifty-second street got boards, a ribbon, a creek, a fire, a night patrol and a judge. That is the only reason anybody can point at it now.

That list is real. It went out with a letter in December 1962, and it sits today in a box in Atlanta with a call number on it.

So go ask the oldest person in your family what street they were living on in 1962, and write the name of it down somewhere it will keep.

In December the people on the white side tied a bow on it. By July fifteen of their families were left, and the crew that had bolted the thing into the road was mostly Black.

Atlanta built a museum you can walk across for the man who closed the road. The road is just a road now, and the left turn takes about four seconds.

Image credit: Atlanta Journal-Constitution Photographic Archives / Georgia State University Library.
