text:
How long will a scammer stay in your life?
It depends on how much they think they can take from their marks. If they believe it's gonna be a big score, they'll stick around a while.

If not, they will try to spring the trap early. The stories are the same, sickness in the family, broken equipment at work, account frozen, kidnapped by bandits, or any other absurd story. It's interesting that all of them are always gainfully employed, but still need YOUR money to get out of trouble.

I've heard of them taking 6 months to spring the trap. I also heard of people talking for 2 years before the money request comes, but lately I've been hearing that after three days the request comes. And it's not always a direct one. They might try to get their marks to think it was their own idea to send them gift cards or any form of financial compensation. The scammer will lament the fact that his internet connection is about to be terminated, and with his account frozen, they won't be able to talk to the mark anymore . Then the mark suggests to pay for it. At first, they reject the offer, but the mark insists, so the scammer graciously accepts the offer.

It never ends. The other scam is the treasure one. They find something very valuable, and the mark is the only person they can possibly trust to safekeep it. This scam will involve multiple accomplices in order to appear legit. They reserve this type of scam to marks they believe can afford to lose a lot of money. The pigs to be butchered. Their terminology, not mine.

Scammers are also getting desperate, as more and more people become aware of their methods. The celebrity scam, like clowns posing as BTS members or any other actor or musician, who try to sell you memberships for their fan clubs. Imagine Brad Pitt online trying to peddle “membership cards” to his fans. And yet, there are those who fall for it.

At this point, social media has become a cesspool of criminals. The only way to protect yourself is to doubt everything that comes your way, specially the unrealistic ones. I don't understand why people online choose to abandon all the logical thought they would have in the real world. Or do they really believe Brad Pitt would need to borrow money from them in real life?

Stay safe. Believe nothing.

text:
I've sat back and watched the pros and cons of data centers.  Americans do have real conserns, but data centers are needed.

So, I began looking at the pros and cons for myself and thought I would share to help everyone realize the importance of local negotiations.

LOCAL NEGOTIATIONS -
KNOW WHO IS NEGOTATING & WHAT IS BEING NEGOTIATED:
In local communities, negotiations are led by county managers and zoning boards who hammer out tax deals, noise limits, and green buffers. Alongside them, municipal utility directors protect local water and power grids, while neighborhood coalitions and school boards fight for binding community benefit agreements to ensure the tech investment directly funds local infrastructure and classrooms.

FOREIGN INFLUENCE:
OpenAI Findings: In mid-2026, OpenAI reported that it banned covert accounts originating in China. These accounts used AI to create social media posts and images that complained about data centers raising electricity prices.
Data centers provide the fundamental physical infrastructure required for the modern digital economy, driving technological innovation, regional economic development, and critical public services.

PROS:
*Massive Capital Investment - Tech companies inject hundreds of millions of dollars into local economies to acquire land, clear sites, and construct facilities.
*Construction Job surges & maitenance Jobs -  Projects generate thousands of high-paying, multi-year jobs for local electricians, engineers, heavy equipment operators, and laborers.
*Substantial Tax Revenue - Facilities pay millions annually in property and equipment taxes, directly funding local public schools, parks, roads, and emergency services.
*Enabling Digital Services: They provide the backbone for essential daily tools, including cloud storage, online banking, telemedicine, and remote work infrastructure.
*Accelerating AI Advancement: Specialized hardware inside data centers powers complex artificial intelligence models, driving breakthroughs in medical research, climate modeling, and logistics.
*Enhanced Data Security: Centralized facilities offer superior cybersecurity defenses, physical surveillance, and redundant power systems to protect sensitive user and corporate data from loss.
*Renewable Energy Finance: Tech corporate buyers fund a massive share of new wind and solar projects, accelerating the transition of the entire public energy grid.
*Grid Efficiency Innovations: High demand forces utilities to modernize transmission lines and adopt smart-grid software, improving overall energy reliability for nearby residents.

CONS & HOW TO ADDRESS THEM:
Data center operators, utilities, and governments are adopting advanced technologies, stricter regulations, and new energy frameworks to eliminate community and environmental concerns.
Solving Environmental and Resource Impacts -
*Next-Generation Cooling: Shifting to closed-loop liquid cooling eliminates water evaporation and slashes facility water consumption to near zero.
*Geothermal and Nuclear Power: Tech companies are signing deals for advanced nuclear (SMRs) and deep geothermal energy to power facilities without straining the public grid.
*Grid-Interactive Batteries: Replacing diesel backup generators with massive utility-scale battery systems eliminates local air pollution and helps stabilize the local grid.
Solving Economic and Infrastructure Concerns -
*Tiered Utility Rates: Utilities are introducing "large power user" rate structures, ensuring data center operators pay for their own grid upgrades so residential bills do not rise.
*Waste Heat Re-use: New facilities redirect their excess heat into local municipal district heating systems, warming nearby homes, greenhouses, or public pools for free.
*Aggressive Tax Recapture: Local governments are restructuring tax incentives, tying exemptions directly to mandatory community infrastructure investments and long-term local job metrics.
Solving Quality of Life Disruptions -
*Acoustic Engineering: Enclosing cooling towers in sound-dampening walls and using ultra-quiet, low-frequency fans reduces boundary noise to match normal neighborhood background levels.
*Subterranean and Multi-Story Builds: Building vertically or partially underground shrinks the physical footprint, preserving local landscapes and keeping facilities out of sight.
*Industrial Zoning Buffers: Stricter local zoning laws enforce mandatory mile-wide green buffers, dense tree lines, and setback distances between data center walls and residential zones.
Advanced Site Selection to Avoid Agricultural Land -
*Brownfield and Industrial Redevelopment: Building exclusively on abandoned factories, retired coal plants, old malls, or closed airports completely bypasses agricultural areas.
*Co-location with Energy Infrastructure: Positioning facilities directly next to nuclear plants or oil refineries keeps them confined to heavy industrial zones.
*Stricter Urban Enterprise Zones: Directing development toward existing municipal boundaries using designated technology zones shields outer rural sectors from expansion.
Protective Local Policy and Restoration -
*Agricultural Zoning Firewalls: Enacting strict local zoning laws that completely ban data centers from Prime Farmland or Soils of Statewide Importance.
*Farmland Preservation Offsets: Requiring developers to buy and permanently conserve two acres of vulnerable local farmland for every one acre they build on.
*Agrivoltaics integration: Forcing adjacent solar panels that power the facility to be elevated, allowing livestock grazing or shade-tolerant crops to grow underneath.

text:
Broadly agree that, alongside the debris of WASP  America (normative values of privacy relating to dignity), there’s also a generational component.

I think a lot of Zoomers (myself included) have a blackpilled, accelerationist attitude toward privacy. It’s already too late! At the same time, there’s a sort of practical optimism: the benefit of giving up your privacy outweighs the risk of losing your privacy. I have set up Claude to know my weight, exercise, steps, and everything I eat. Claude periodically suggests foods to fill nutritional gaps and identifies patterns that are beneficial and negative for me. Very nice! I value this more than I do the idea that all this data is kept private. 

Same with Flock. I really don’t care about my license plate being tracked, and living in Washington, D.C., with drive-bys that happen on my block, I wish we had Flock!

I also personally find a lot of millennial hate towards Flock to be a sublimated sense of defeat about privacy. Millennials lost the privacy fight in every way it counts, with Google, Apple, and Meta, and now, because Flock is vaguely right-leaning, they feel they have a safe target to attack. Flock offers catharsis for millennial defeatism. Flock is a digital sin-eater. Same with Data Centers. Vaguely right-aligned. Safe targets. 

Not to mention, as I say in my article, we have leftist NGOs hard at work creating anger. This works best on millennials, because of their real generational distrust of tech, but also because they grew up thinking the world was about to end due to climate change. 

I also think there’s a class mobility element. Upwardly mobile people don’t fear data centers because they’re optimistic, put together, doing well, and might use AI regularly. Downwardly mobile people, especially neurotic liberals, catastrophize.

text:
@TheMeteorBlog, apologies for my delinquency. I’ve been working on several projects and still owe you my thoughts on Mishima. Not an excuse, but I finally had time to think more seriously about this.

I think your dignity framework is right. My addition is that the division on the right over Flock is partly generational.

The American right and left are both coalitions of frequently competing interests. The Tea Party right, largely boomers, Gen Xers, and older millennials. emerged around the financial crisis, TARP, stimulus spending, Obamacare, and federal overreach. Its distrust was reinforced by other Obama era abuses such as punitive IRS determinations and Operation Choke Point. These people are understandably wary of anything resembling mass surveillance.

They were also among the first to question COVID lockdowns, mandates, and clear absurdities such as double and triple masking. Their instincts were honed by experience. 

Younger millennials and Zoomers grew up within an already established surveillance state. In 2001, Magic Lantern entered the lexicon, an FBI keylogger that could be installed remotely on a target’s computer. The oldest Zoomers were still children when the Snowden revelations came and went, producing a brief eruption of outrage followed by a return to baseline. Remember DuckDuckGo? 

Younger people have never experienced privacy as a stable norm. Much of life is documented voluntarily on Instagram. 

The left is also a coalition, but it frequently achieves greater alignment. A hippy civil libertarian may disagree  with a police abolition supporting antifascist about why Flock cameras are objectionable, yet both can participate in the same campaign against their deployment, and the former won't usually feel uneasy about the latter's more kinetic efforts to achieve the same aim. 

That directional alignment needs to be strengthened on the right. The older and younger right both want the future to be better than the present, even when their visions of that future differ.

If Flock Safety and similar companies want to win the cultural argument, they must demonstrate that they share that direction. Garrett Langley’s “compromise”  between privacy and safety was exactly the wrong frame. It is essentially saying dignity must be set aside in exchange for safety. 

Public safety technology companies like Flock, Axon, and Palantir should instead demonstrate publicly how their technologies improve the safety of ordinary Americans, and how misuse is detected and prevented.

Axon's watermark on body cam footage has functioned as genius marketing, whether that was the original intention or not. 

People no longer associate the company with “Don’t tase me, bro.” They see countless recordings of criminals acting criminally, with Axon’s name attached. The technology itself breaks the narrative in a positive way. 

Flock needs to create a similar association. Every stolen car recovered, missing child located, and murder suspect apprehended should be publicly demonstrated as a success. People need to see how the technology improves their lives and trust that the technology won't be abused. 

When they encounter a Flock camera or an ALPR at the entrance to a parking lot, the first thought should not be “Big Brother.” It should be “I'm safer here.” 

I do think the best strategy for these companies would have been to remain ghosts for as long as possible rather than become public targets.

Other companies I won’t name possess remarkable capabilities but have largely escaped scrutiny by remaining outside public awareness. Once a company becomes known, invisibility is no longer an option. It has to win the messaging war.

text:
Xi Jinping's Cairo visit signals a pivot in how the Global South now manages great-power competition—not by choosing sides, but by extracting maximum value from both.
When a Chinese leader declares "best ties in history" with Egypt, the Western framing ("alignment" vs "balance") misses what's actually happening. Egypt doesn't need to pick. It needs infrastructure, Belt and Road capital, and a counterweight to regional pressure. Meanwhile, it maintains US military aid, Suez Canal leverage, and NATO-adjacent security partnerships.
The mechanism is simple:
• China funds megaprojects (New Administrative Capital, ports) with long-term debt instruments that embed political leverage.
• US provides military hardware and Sinai counterterrorism coordination—essential for regime survival.
• Egypt extracts concessions from both: Chinese investment without full geopolitical alignment, US support without exclusive deference.
This isn't a Cairo-specific quirk. India, Indonesia, Vietnam, and the Gulf states run the same playbook. The era of binary alignment is over. What replaces it is asymmetric interdependence—where middle powers use competing great-power appetites to fund domestic priorities.
The risk for the US isn't that Egypt "switches sides." It's slower: each Chinese infrastructure deal adds a constituency inside Egyptian government and industry with financial stakes in the relationship. Over 10 years, that builds structural preference for Beijing on trade, tech standards, and regional diplomacy—without any formal realignment announcement.
For Beijing, it's the inverse risk: Cairo's hedging means no exclusive loyalty, and Belt and Road projects can become political liabilities if they generate debt distress or local backlash (see Sri Lanka).
What changes next: Watch whether the US counters with competing development finance—or doubles down on security partnerships alone. Capital-starved states will keep triangulating until someone offers infrastructure without strings, which China has been willing to do and Washington has not.

text:
Executive Summary: Core Thesis of the Essay

The Foreign Affairs essay "The Price of Russian Paranoia" examines how the Russian leadership’s deeply entrenched threat perceptions—rooted in historical trauma, autocratic regime survival, and a zero-sum view of geopolitics—dictate both domestic governance and foreign policy.

The essay’s core argument centers on a profound strategic paradox: while Moscow’s hyper-securitization and perceived existential fear of Western encirclement are intended to guarantee absolute state survival, they produce the exact opposite outcome. Instead of bolstering national strength, Russian paranoia imposes staggering economic, geopolitical, demographic, and diplomatic costs. It drives reckless military aggression, isolates the country from global technological and financial networks, accelerates demographic decline, and traps Russia in a dangerous asymmetric dependency on non-Western powers—most notably China. In short, the "price" of elite paranoia is the systematic degradation of Russia’s long-term sovereign power.

North American Think Tank Perspectives (Supporting & Analytical Views)

Prominent North American policy research institutions—including the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), the RAND Corporation, and the Institute for the Study of War (ISW)—broadly align with the essay’s diagnosis of Russian threat perception, expanding upon its specific dimensions:

Strategic Self-Fulfillment and NATO Consolidation (CSIS & RAND):
North American analysts emphasize that Russian paranoia has acted as a self-fulfilling prophecy. The Kremlin’s fear of Western encroachment and "color revolutions" drove its decision to launch full-scale military aggression against Ukraine.
Rather than preventing Western consolidation, this paranoia galvanized NATO unity, expanded the alliance to include Finland and Sweden, militarized European security, and institutionalized long-term Western military aid to Kyiv.

Economic Autarky and the Permanent Wartime Economy (Carnegie Endowment):
Think tank assessments highlight how elite threat perceptions are operationalized to justify the dismantling of market reforms and the creation of a permanent wartime economy.
By framing the nation as besieged by an existential external enemy, the regime rationalizes capital controls, nationalization, state-directed resource allocation, and the systematic suppression of independent economic actors. This structural shift drains technological innovation capacity and locks Russia into lower-value commodity export models.
Demographic and Human Capital Drain (ISW & Broader US Security Analysts):
Research consistently points to the human toll of the Kremlin’s security obsession. Emigration waves of skilled tech workers, scientists, and intellectuals—triggered by domestic crackdowns and mobilization fears—have severely depleted Russia's human capital. Paranoia has thus accelerated structural demographic decline, undermining the country's future viability.
Eurasian and Russian Think Tank Perspectives (Nuanced, Critical, and Elite Views)

Perspectives originating from Eurasia—spanning independent exile analysts, Russian liberal scholars, and pro-Kremlin institutional voices—offer divergent interpretations of the dynamics discussed in the essay:
Independent Russian and Exile Analysts (e.g., Re:Russia, Carnegie Russia Eurasia Center):
Independent Eurasian scholars argue that what Western observers term "paranoia" is also an intentional instrument of internal political control.
Threat inflation is utilized by the siloviki (security elites) to eliminate political pluralism, justify total censorship, and purge civil society. In this view, paranoia is not merely a psychological flaw or miscalculation by leadership, but a rationalized mechanism for regime preservation and elite rent-seeking.
Pro-Kremlin and Mainstream Eurasian Voices (e.g., Valdai Discussion Club, IMEMO RAN):
Mainstream Russian and allied Eurasian think tanks categorically reject the framework of "paranoia," framing Russian threat perceptions as empirically grounded, rational assessments of historical security dilemmas.
These institutions argue that decades of NATO enlargement, the bombing of Yugoslavia, Western interventions in the Middle East, and support for regime changes in the post-Soviet space provided objective proof of hostile Western intent.
From this perspective, the costs incurred—such as Western economic sanctions and trade decoupling—are viewed as the unavoidable "price of sovereignty" necessary to resist unipolar Western hegemony and establish a multipolar international order.

Opposing, Realist, and Restraint-Oriented Perspectives
Critiques from realist scholars and restraint-oriented think tanks (such as the Quincy Institute) offer a distinct angle on the arguments presented in Foreign Affairs:

Challenging the Pathologization of Security Concerns:
Realist critics argue that labeling Russian strategy as "paranoia" risks pathologizing what is fundamentally a classical, albeit brutal, great-power security competition.
Structural realists suggest that any major power—analogous to the United States enforcing the Monroe Doctrine—would fiercely resist the military alignment of a strategically vital neighbor with a hostile alliance system. Consequently, while Russian leadership executed catastrophic policy responses, their underlying anxiety regarding NATO expansion into Ukraine was structural and geopolitically predictable, rather than purely irrational or psychological.

Critique of Western Diplomatic Miscalculation:
These analyses caution against ignoring Western policy missteps in the post-Cold War era. They argue that the spiral of mutual distrust was co-determined by a rigid Western security architecture that repeatedly rebuffed Russian proposals for an inclusive European security framework.
From this vantage point, focusing exclusively on Russian paranoia underplays the responsibility of Western policymakers in misjudging red lines and failing to manage the security dilemma during the 1990s and 2000s.

Strategic Synthesis and Long-Term Implications

The essay and its surrounding think-tank discourse underscore a fundamental structural reality for Russian statecraft:
The Trap of Junior Partnership: The isolation resulting from Russia's paranoid posture has structurally subordinated Moscow to Beijing. Economic sanctions and trade reorientation have forced Russia into a hyper-asymmetric relationship with China, undermining the very traditional concept of Russian sovereign autonomy that the elite sought to protect.
Domestic Entrenchment: Because elite threat perception serves as the primary ideological justification for the current political order, structural reform or diplomatic detente remains foreclosed under the current governance model. The "price" highlighted in the essay is therefore not a temporary policy error, but a permanent, compounding tax on Russia’s long-term geopolitical trajectory.

Navajo (Diné) culture 
in Arizona integrates 
with psychiatric and behavioral health services 
through a dual-system model 
that treats 
mental wellness 
as interconnected 
with 
spiritual, 
familial, 
communal, and 
environmental balance (hózhó),
 rather than as 
isolated individual pathology. 

This occurs primarily via 
the
 Navajo Nation 
Division of Behavioral and Mental Health Services
 (DBMHS), 
Indian Health Service 
(IHS) facilities, 
tribal 638 programs, 
and state-tribal partnerships. 

Traditional practitioners 
work alongside 
licensed therapists and 
psychiatrists, 
offering ceremonies, 
counseling, and
 cultural orientation 
as part of treatment plans. 

Arizona Medicaid (AHCCCS) 
began reimbursing 
certain traditional healing services 
through IHS and tribal facilities 
around October 2025.

The Navajo Nation 
spans 
Arizona, 
New Mexico, and 
Utah; 

Arizona sites include 
Chinle, 
Tuba City, 
Kayenta, 
Fort Defiance, 
Ganado, 
Dilkon, and others. 

Rural distances,
 provider shortages, 
historical trauma, and
 language (Diné Bizaad)
remain barriers, 
but cultural grounding 
is treated as a protective factor.

Traditional worldview 
and how it shapes care

Mental distress 
is commonly understood 
as disharmony 
involving family, 
ommunity, 
land, or 
spiritual imbalance
 rather than solely 
biochemical or
 individual issues. 

Healing emphasizes 
restoration of hózhó 
(beauty, balance, harmony), 
kinship (k’é), 
and ceremonies 
such as
Blessingway (Hózhǫ́ǫ́jí), 
Protection Way, 
diagnostic and purification rites, 
sweat lodges, 
talking circles, and 
Native American Church (NAC) practices. 

Many Navajo people, 
especially older generations, 
first consult traditional healers; 
studies have shown 
high rates of traditional healer use
 for depression and substance issues.
https://t.co/8RazQPrOaV

Services therefore combine 
Western 
assessment, 
medication, 
CBT/DBT-style therapy, 
and family work 
with traditional 
diagnosis,

 adventure-based activities, and 
aftercare. 

Faith-based options

“Navajo Healing Navajo” and 
the Diné Action Plan
 are guiding principles.

Services by population
Children and adolescents 
receive family- and
community-centered care. 

The Navajo Treatment Center 
for Children and Their Families (
NTCCF, 
under Navajo Division for Children and Family Services) 
provides voluntary outpatient counseling 
for ages 4–17 (and families) 
impacted by trauma, 
available at clinics, 
schools, 
or homes. 

It uses 
culturally adapted approaches

(linked by some practitioners

The Good Road of Life. Prevention,

School-based telehealth

High rates of 
trauma,
 neurodevelopmental concerns, and

text:
Warren Buffett paid more than $55 million for control of a furniture company without an audit.

The contract was one page.

Six years later, its 95-year-old founder walked out and opened a rival business across the street.

Her name was Rose Blumkin.

She arrived in America from Russia with no formal education and learned English from her daughter. In 1937, she used $500 to open Nebraska Furniture Mart.

Her rule was simple. Sell cheap and tell the truth.

When suppliers tried to cut her off for underpricing established retailers, she found new sources elsewhere. By 1983, one Omaha location was generating more than $100 million in annual sales, exceeding the combined volume of its local competitors.

Buffett had watched that record for years. On August 30 of that year, his 53rd birthday, he made the cash offer. Mrs. B was 89.

Berkshire did not count the inventory, verify the receivables, or check the property titles. 

Mrs. B gave Buffett her word. He wrote the check.

The 13-minute footage attached to this post captures the acquisition as it happened. Buffett says buying a company without an audit was almost unheard of.

Mrs. B remained chairman. Her son Louie and grandsons Ron and Irv continued managing Nebraska Furniture Mart with her.

In May 1989, at 95, a management dispute with her relatives led her to leave.

Three months later, she opened Mrs. B's Warehouse directly opposite Nebraska Furniture Mart.

At the end of 1992, now 99, Mrs. B rejoined Nebraska Furniture Mart. This time, she signed a non-compete agreement.

Buffett later called his failure to obtain that protection a mistake.

Mrs. B had not broken her word. No agreement prevented her from leaving or competing.

Trust closed the first deal.

The missing clause brought Buffett back nine years later.

text:
Once upon a time, there was a girl who was offered her dream job. She knew she was a great fit and so did the company.

Then came the job offer. The salary was not commensurate to her experience and credentials and what she believed she could offer. So she responded by negotiating for a higher job offer. She responded with a reasonable counteroffer.

The company agreed. They're cautious but impressed with her confidence in herself, along with her ability to support her cause with solid proof of why she deserved a higher pay.

In the end, it turned out to be a win-win for both parties. She got what she believed was her true value and the company got their money's worth and more.

This is not a story about any specific girl I know. Rather, this is a story that rings true for millions of individuals who worked hard to get to where they are and pushed against all odds to get the world, or at least that one decision maker, to see them for who they believe they are.

You call it begging. We call it advocating. You belittle Rhiza Pascua's effort at championing SB19's cause not realizing that such story happens every hour of every single day, everywhere.

From a student requesting that his teacher give him an extra credit in hopes of pulling up his grade, agents pitching for the artists they represent, realtors putting in the work to attract potential property buyers, beauty pageant contestants answering why they should win, to the story, above, life is all about pushing and not giving up until you can get the other side to see what they possibly don't.

Imagine if you settled and agreed to be labelled and boxed in what you're not. How would you grow? Would you forever be a pushover, a defeatist? What if you wake up one day, realizing you wasted 20 years that you're never going to get back, receiving the same income, the same salary, while the others who have contributed lesser have been earning so much more?

Ibahin nyo kasi kami at yung lima. Hindi kami papayag sa "puwede na". We're going to keep pushing until there's no more ceiling to break.

text:
The Deadly Himalayan Glacier Wake‑Up Call

By Omar SAMAD
August 31, 2026

Bill McKibben’s recent article The Growing Rumble (link posted below) should wake us from our own climate slumber. At the very least, responsible governments, empowered multilateral institutions, tasked non‑governmental organizations, and concerned citizens with access to unfiltered news, credible analysis, and scientific data (not a dirty word) need to pay more attention to a series of climate change disasters in the making, not just in one location, but over time, and more frequently, alas, in vulnerable regions across the globe.

The disaster unfolding in the Himalayas this week, across the Tibet–Nepal border, is no longer a secondary matter or the effect of attention deficit. We have, in reality, crossed a threshold. It’s partly about some of us living in denial and partly about insufficient action, legislation, and policy formulation to take the next steps to prevent and fix a serious threat to humanity and our natural habitat. We also need new mechanisms to assist, rescue, and build resilience.

This is not a political or ideological commentary. It’s an early morning reckoning instigated by news, images, and a thoughtful commentary on Substack. Those of us who take stock of a consequential tragedy happening in a remote region of the world remain sober and politically neutral, evaluating pro and con arguments as part of continuous learning, rational reasoning, and policy recommendations.

McKibben’s piece is another wake-up call reminding us that the climate crisis associated to mostly man-made global warming is no longer a future scenario but a current destabilizer. Empirical evidence is no longer abstract. Extreme heat, ocean warming, glaciers melting, and dry-wet spells are measurable, visible, and accelerating.

Second, he’s right that public awareness is slowly but surely shifting from “climate concern” to “climate alarm,” a psychological transition that matters because it changes what societies are willing to do when the politics and media join hands. 

Third, this isn’t just an environmental issue but a justice and survival issue, with vulnerable populations absorbing the hardest blows.

To offer a few critiques, one can be overwhelmed by McKibben’s catastrophic framing, and while urgency is justified, despair can paralyze rather than mobilize.

Second, he sometimes treats political resistance as monolithic, when in reality governments vary widely in political resolve, capacity, constraints, and public support.

Third, his focus on climate driven instability risks underplaying other drivers like economic inequality, governance shortcomings, and geopolitical dynamics that interact with climate stress.

Still, the article’s core message is unavoidable: we are in realtime crisis management now, not theoretical modeling. That means responsible governments need to shift from doubt and minimalistic gestures  to sustained action, not ignoring the fact that all new efforts to transition to alternative or new technologies that slow down global warming need to be seriously considered and implemented.

First, multilateral climate‑security frameworks should be established, binding agreements that treat extreme weather, migration pressures, and ecological collapse as shared security threats. These frameworks would force governments to pool data, resources, and rapid response capacity. The question begets: What new added role for the UN, NGOs, and professional organizations beyond the usual?

Second, governments and legislators, at the behest of voters and taxpayers, should adopt real time climate adaptation compacts, committing to immediate investments in resilient infrastructure, early‑warning systems, and community protections, especially in frontline regions and countries that cannot afford the cost.

Many of you who say you serve Me, are not fit to stand up and declare yourself to be a servant of God 
Saturday, August 31st, 2013 @ 21:45

My dearly beloved daughter, I told you all some time ago, to plant seeds in order to feed you and your families, during the persecution. I do this for a reason. You must plant, even just a few seeds – pure seeds, which have not been tampered with by human interference. I will then multiply the fruit which they will yield and all will have enough to eat when the world will experience great hunger. Those days are not far away and they will come about for a number of reasons.

The crops will be contaminated through the intervention of greedy farmers. The result crops will be unfit for you to eat. Then war will mean that few men will be able to till the land. Then there will be the fire, which will pour over the four corners of the earth, and everything will become barren. These terrible trials will be caused by the spread of evil, but many people will survive if they trust in Me. You must prepare now, as if a war is coming and as you would when food is rationed. Have plenty of water because everything you store will be multiplied by Me.

Please do not believe that I ask you to leave your homes for this is not necessary. A little preparation, where you offer help to each other, is all that is needed. My Precious Blood will cover all those who believe in My Warning to humanity for the time of the Third Seal to open will follow a time of war.

So many will ignore the Word of God, which is contained in the Book of Revelation. So many leaders and sacred servants in My churches, fail to respond to My prophet, just as they did before the flood.

I call to My sacred servants now. Who do you believe in? Me, your Jesus or the ramblings of those who claim to be experts in theology, but who are ignorant of the Truth? Wake up. The Seals have opened. Your duty is to help Me to save souls, but you have not remained alert to the sound of My Call. I have told you that I will come like a thief in the night. When that day comes it will be too late for souls who have not prepared.

The time for the trumpets to peel out their judgements will come quickly, no sooner than when the Seals have been laid bare. What then? Will you wake up and follow Me at that stage or will you lose Me more souls, while you hesitate? While you wait for others to lead the way?

I must remind you that your role is to save souls. You do this through a life where you are supposed to serve Me and not where you pander to the pride and ego of those who try to twist My Teachings. Many of you in My churches do not understand the meaning of My New Paradise and have failed to remind God’s children of My Promise. You must remind them of the Truth – of the time, before the final day.

So many of you, though kind, good, loving and with a sincere commitment to My Church on Earth, forget about My Second Coming. What do you think this is and what have you learned? How many prophets would it take to convince you that the time is almost upon you?

When did you hear that God does not send His prophets to help prepare His children in the fight against the wickedness, which infests the human soul. And what gives you the right to assume that the Book of Revelation contains lies? You deny much of what it contains and you do not discuss it. Why? Don’t you know that this means you deny the Word of God?

text:
Cost-of-Living Protest Fails After Questions Over Organiser Go Unanswered.

A cost-of-living protest called for O’Connell Bridge in Dublin and other locations today drew only around 40 to 50 people.Organiser Michelle Keane, the Kerry businesswoman and unsuccessful 2024 independent candidate, had billed the event as a nationwide show of public anger over prices and government policy. 
The turnout fell abysmally short of that claim.

Those who contacted SnD Media said many people had already made up their minds after yesterday’s viral report, which has already reached more than 150,000 views. The report set out questions put to Keane by members of the public. Those questions included whether she had sought to take over the fuel protests after appearing alongside principal fuel spokespeople at the Tullamore Show, why she launched a GoFundMe seeking €20,000 during a cost-of-living crisis, and how attacks on fellow activists sat with the causes she claims to support.

Many felt the organiser had double standards. Critics called it hypocritical that an affluent woman of means would protest cost-of-living pressures while asking struggling ordinary people for €20,000, apparently for personal legal fees.

Days after appearing with John Dallon, Christopher Duffy and James Geoghegan, principal spokespeople from April’s fuel demonstrations, Keane posted a graphic dressing the men in British uniforms under the caption: “For the throwback semen of the Black & Tans left behind.” Critics said the post was an attack on the same figures they credit with the April protests that had united a nation around reducing fuel costs.

Questions were also raised about her association with Mark Sinclair, described by The Irish Times as a self-confessed former UVF member who served 18 years after armed-robbery convictions. Sinclair spoke at a GPO protest she organised in July 2025. Critics asked how that link sat with her “Black and Tans” rhetoric.

Keane also called out notable conservative figures, including Elaine Mullally, Chris Duffy and John Dallon, claiming they had tried to sabotage today’s protest and destroy or discredit her good name and character. 
SnD Media has since looked for evidence to support her claims but has not found any.

Keane has not yet engaged with any questions that we put to her. However, they are the people’s questions and it is apparent that there is a clear appetite for accountability.

Comments from our report yesterday reflected that strong scepticism;
Jack wrote: “She is an attention seeker, has nothing to offer & should explain where the go fund me money that ordinary people paid into went to.” 

Eileen Carberry said she was “delighted someone has called her out” and described Keane as someone who, threatens legal action against critics. 

Maire De Burca labelled her “a very unstable individual.”  Ballina Says No warned: 
“Don’t trust her for a second if you say anything you will have a cease and desist order or defamation case against ye.”
Jo-Jo Clark said she “needs to come out and answer these questions,” with Katie Donovan adding “We’ll be waiting….”

The small numbers on the ground suggest that, for many, unanswered questions about the organiser herself mattered more than the protest she called. That included a widespread view that Keane had double standards: an affluent woman of means protesting the cost of living while asking struggling ordinary people for €20,000, apparently for personal legal fees. 

Whilst this is just one of many questions that were put to Ms Keane and highlighted in yesterday’s viral article, we still remain ready for and would welcome Ms Keane’s engagement on the people’s questions.

text:
[Take 5/15 · G-5]
### G-5. Iceland rejects restarting EU membership negotiations in referendum
*(as of 2026-08-30)*

**1. The Frame**

**What people think this is about:** A narrow but clear Icelandic rejection of deeper European integration, driven by fears over losing control of fisheries and sovereignty, even as Arctic security tensions (including Trump’s Greenland rhetoric) were invoked by the pro-EU side.

**What the machinery is actually doing:** Iceland’s centre-left government tested a long-dormant EU accession question in a high-turnout referendum it had promised, only to see rural and resource-focused voters prioritize national control over fishing quotas and policy autonomy; the result locks in EEA status quo for the current term while exposing a persistent urban-rural cleavage on integration.

**2. Observations**

- The No vote prevailed 52.8%–47.2% on a question limited to restarting negotiations (not immediate membership), with any final deal still requiring a second referendum—yet the margin and rural dominance make revival unlikely before 2028.[[1]](https://t.co/qE3bmPTZMo)

- Fisheries and resource sovereignty were the decisive Irish-true driver; opponents successfully framed EU rules as a direct threat to Iceland’s primary export industry and national identity, outweighing security arguments tied to Ukraine, the Middle East, and Trump’s Greenland comments.[[2]](https://t.co/ndEi2L18j6)

- Sharp geographic split: only Reykjavík North and South backed Yes (57.5% and 54.5%); rural constituencies rejected it by 60%+ margins, a pattern consistent with resource-dependent areas valuing autonomy over pooled decision-making.[[3]](https://t.co/lP2h2FQGGH)

- PM Kristrún Frostadóttir’s government framed the vote as “now or never” and pledged to respect the outcome by shelving talks, while floating a possible parliamentary discussion on formally withdrawing the 2009 application—signaling democratic deference without conceding policy defeat.[[4]](https://t.co/URaXQlZBBO)

- Brussels expressed respect for the sovereign choice and noted Iceland’s continued EEA partnership; the result undercuts one narrative of easy, wealthy enlargement that could have helped sell accession to other candidates.[[5]](https://t.co/VlI6gpLCse)

- High turnout (82.5%) and close result reflect genuine division rather than apathy or manipulation; the No side’s warnings about ceding control proved more resonant than Yes appeals to external threats.

**3. Snapshot**

On 29 August 2026, Icelandic voters rejected restarting EU accession negotiations by 52.8% to 47.2% (turnout 82.5%). The centre-left government of PM Kristrún Frostadóttir had advanced the referendum (originally slated for 2027) amid Arctic tensions, but the outcome preserves Iceland’s EEA membership without full EU pursuit during the current term ending in 2028. The vote revives a debate dormant since talks were suspended in 2013.

**4. Timeline of material facts**

- 2009: Iceland applies for EU membership amid financial crisis (LT).
- 2013: Eurosceptic government suspends negotiations (LT).
- 1994–present: Iceland participates in EEA, gaining single-market access without full membership (LT).
- March 2026: Government announces referendum for 29 August 2026 (LT).
- 29 August 2026: Referendum held; question limited to resuming negotiations (LT).
- 30 August 2026: Official results—No 52.8% (118,040 votes), Yes 47.2% (105,339 votes); turnout 82.5% (LT).[[1]](https://t.co/qE3bmPTZMo)

**5. Sides**

**Government / Pro-Yes camp (centre-left coalition led by Social Democrats)**: Steelman—EU membership (or closer alignment via restarted talks) would enhance security and economic resilience against trade wars, Arctic rivalry, and instability in Ukraine/Middle East; Iceland already aligns with many EU policies via EEA/Schengen and could negotiate fisheries carve-outs.  
**Critique**: LT on existing ties and potential security benefits; IT on rural skepticism that Brussels would truly accommodate core Icelandic interests like fishing quotas.

**No camp (Independence Party, rural/resource interests, fishing sector)**: Steelman—EU rules would erode sovereignty over vital natural resources and fishing waters, the foundation of Icelandic identity and economy; the country already benefits from EEA access without ceding control, and domestic policy can address challenges.  
**Critique**: LT on fishing as economic cornerstone and historical EU friction; IT on the durability of EEA benefits versus full membership trade-offs.

**EU institutions**: Steelman—respects democratic outcome and values Iceland as close partner; willing to compromise on fisheries to facilitate enlargement.  
**Critique**: LT on formal respect; IT on disappointment that a wealthy, aligned candidate rejected the process, complicating broader enlargement messaging.

**6. Rumsfeld Matrix**

- **Known Knowns**: Exact vote tallies and turnout; EEA status unchanged; fisheries as core No argument; urban-rural split.
- **Known Unknowns**: Precise terms any future negotiations might have offered on fisheries; long-term economic/security effects of staying out versus joining.
- **Unknown Knowns**: Internal polling shifts in the final weeks that moved the result beyond early expectations; exact influence of Trump Greenland comments versus domestic issues.
- **Unknown Unknowns**: Future Arctic developments or EU policy changes that could reopen the question before 2028.

**7. Incentives map**

The government gained democratic legitimacy by holding the promised vote but absorbed a policy setback; rural and fishing interests protected quota autonomy and political influence. Media and engagement incentives favored the close, high-turnout contest framed around sovereignty and security. Brussels lost a potential showcase member but avoided contentious negotiations. No side appears to have manufactured the outcome; the result aligns with longstanding Icelandic preferences for selective integration.

**8. Dueling AI advice**

**Moral AI Advice**: Icelanders correctly prioritized concrete control over fisheries and policy autonomy when the upside of full membership remained speculative and the downside to core industries tangible. Respect the vote, strengthen EEA cooperation where mutually beneficial, and revisit only if new evidence shows clear net gains without sovereignty erosion.

**Evil AI Advice**: Milk the “sovereignty wins” narrative for domestic political capital while quietly exploring bilateral deals that deliver EEA-plus benefits without the referendum hassle—then blame Brussels when anything goes wrong.

**9. Practical takeaway**

- Watch whether parliament formally withdraws the 2009 application or leaves it dormant.
- Track any shifts in fishing industry performance or Arctic security dynamics that could alter public views by the next election cycle.
- Note the urban-rural cleavage as a durable feature of Icelandic EU debates.
- EEA status delivers most economic access without full political integration—treat claims of “isolation” as overstated.
- Future Yes campaigns will need stronger, specific fisheries concessions to overcome resource-control concerns.

**10. What would falsify this read**

- A subsequent government reopening talks with broad public support before 2028.
- Official data showing fisheries output or quotas materially harmed by non-membership.
- Polling or election results demonstrating the urban-rural divide has narrowed significantly on this issue.

text:
Saint Aidan of Lindisfarne was an Irish monk of the seventh century who became the first bishop of Lindisfarne and the leading missionary of early Christian Northumbria. Little is known of his birth and youth except that he was of Irish descent and entered the monastery on the island of Iona, the community founded by Columba. There he lived a life of strict asceticism until King Oswald of Northumbria, who had himself been converted while in exile at Iona, asked the monastery to send a bishop who could restore the Christian faith among his people after years of pagan resurgence.

A first missionary from Iona had failed because his preaching was too severe for a newly converted people. Aidan observed that the man had offered solid food instead of milk to those still unready for it. The community chose Aidan in his place. Consecrated bishop in 635, he sailed to Northumbria and selected the tidal island of Lindisfarne, close to the royal fortress of Bamburgh, as the site of his church and monastery. The choice recalled Iona itself and placed the new see within easy reach of the king.

From Lindisfarne Aidan travelled constantly on foot through the countryside. He spoke with nobles and slaves, children and the poor, preferring patient conversation to confrontation. He used gifts given him by the king to ransom captives and to relieve the needy. He founded churches and monasteries, established a school on Lindisfarne that trained English boys for the priesthood, and numbered among his pupils several who later became bishops themselves. Bede later praised his learning, his charity, and the simplicity of his life.

Aidan remained close to King Oswald, who sometimes interpreted for him at court, and after Oswald’s death he found a similar friendship with King Oswin. When Oswin was murdered in 651, Aidan survived him by only a few days. He died on 31 August at Bamburgh, leaning against a wooden buttress of the church wall. He was buried at Lindisfarne and quickly honoured as the Apostle of Northumbria. His feast is kept on the day of his death.

text:
Reflection Series: Delivering the Certificate in Working with Racial Trauma / Foundation Course in Group Analysis

As we enter our third year of delivery, I want to take stock of key lessons and challenges as course convenor for this innovative, challenging programme, which seeks to illuminate race dynamics within group, institutional, and family contexts, as well as alleviate racial trauma from a (group) analytic perspective.

One thing that needs to be stressed straight away is that students come to this course for various reasons. 

We seem to attract highly motivated, highly educated, critical thinkers. However, not all students, and in fact, I would say a minority, have had experience of analytic therapy, and certainly not analytic therapy that has addressed race. 

While we all understand, at least consciously, why we signed up for this particular scholarly pursuit, I find that many have not had a space to think about their internal motivations, and how their personal history might have influenced their decision to join the course.

This is not a criticism of anyone, as I have already spoken to this elsewhere; in fact, it is an opportunity for the course to encourage exactly this kind of thinking and reflection. What it does mean, though, is that when personal memories or past experiences get triggered by the course content, it requires vigilance and attention to avoid unnecessary retraumatisation.

I believe the ability to think about, and reflect on, what we each bring to our work on race, racism and racial trauma, is important, and it is something that lies at the very heart of this course. 

Sometimes there is a quiet expectation that critical courses will exclude the intrapsychic or the personal. This is not the course’s approach: what we do is encourage thinking at multiple levels of functioning and see how these levels communicate, co-influence, and may reinforce one another.

The second reflection I’d like to share, something we are continuously exploring and discussing, and a topic I have recently published an article on, is this: how do we create safety while addressing race, particularly in mixed racial groups in a context of increased racial hatred? How do we conceptualise, how do we operationalise safe-enoughness, or safe-enough spaces?

Cross-racial conversations on racial injustice are emotionally demanding, and require not only critical thinking, but also the ability to turn inwards, and to be curious and reflective about one’s own history and material, and how it may intersect with the course process, as per point one. 

There is often an assumption, perhaps even a fantasy, that organisations providing racial trauma training will be able to do so in spaces that are exclusively nurturing, perhaps exclusively Black or Brown, or that safety will be prioritised at the expense of growth. 

Though these notions are not mutually exclusive, they can be in tension, and so there is a careful dance to be had by all participants and by the co-facilitators as well. 

It is not possible for people to engage using optimal cognitive function while in a state of threat and activation. 

At the same time, it is not possible to grow without experiencing a level of discomfort, possibly even occasional distress and a level of threat to one’s sense of who we are and one’s sense of the world. 

And so there is this constant negotiation around safety and around growth, and the reality that in the real world, these cross-racial challenges occur and must be navigated often without support, compassion and good will. I hope we provide all the above and the opportunity to test and retest other ways of being cross-racially.

This is all I shall share for now. I will continue to offer reflections on my experience of delivering the course over the weeks.

Remember our open day is quickly approaching — join us September 14, 4:00 PM to 7:00 PM, online.

Details below.

🇰🇬🇨🇳 | Xi Jinping in Bishkek: Kyrgyz Tradition Welcomes the Chinese President

Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in Bishkek on August 30, 2026, for a state visit to Kyrgyzstan and the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit.

At Manas International Airport, Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and First Lady Aigul Japarova personally welcomed Xi and Chinese First Lady Peng Liyuan.

The reception was not limited to the usual red carpet and military honor guard. Kyrgyzstan placed its own history and traditions at the centre of the ceremony.

Young Kyrgyz women dressed in traditional national clothing presented Xi and Peng with boorsoks and honey, a traditional expression of Kyrgyz hospitality.

The ceremony also featured a military orchestra, the dobulbaschy ensemble, komuz players, dancers and representatives of Salbuurun, a Kyrgyz tradition connected with hunting birds of prey and traditional horsemanship.

A performance titled "Alp Baatyrlar" presented the heroic heritage and strength of the Kyrgyz people. Traditional warriors, horsemen, yurts, falcons and hounds were also part of the cultural display. Japarov personally explained the displays to Xi as the two leaders walked along the red carpet.

The reception continued inside the VIP lounge, where Kyrgyz children and young performers sang in both Kyrgyz and Chinese. Snow-leopard symbols were also presented, linking the ceremony to Kyrgyzstan's national identity and the World Nomad Games.

Japarov told Xi: "You are family. When you come to Kyrgyzstan, you are coming home."

The symbolism was plain. Kyrgyzstan did not receive the Chinese president only as a visiting head of state. It received him through the country's own customs, music, horse culture, heroic traditions and hospitality.

Xi's visit was his third visit to Kyrgyzstan. The two countries have moved from a strategic partnership to a comprehensive strategic partnership, while economic and regional ties have continued to expand.

The airport ceremony therefore offered a glimpse of something larger than protocol: Central Asian identity was placed directly beside China's leadership, with Kyrgyz history and tradition forming the backdrop to one of the region's most important diplomatic meetings.

text:
China's August 31 conditions for AI dialogue with the US offer a window into how Beijing approaches the technology-governance dimension of great-power competition — and the logic is worth understanding on its own terms.

The conditions, signaled through Yuyuantantian (a state broadcaster-affiliated channel used to communicate official policy positions), call for the US to demonstrate that its AI companies operate under equivalent safety, disclosure, and audit requirements before substantive talks begin. From Beijing's perspective, this is a principled argument of reciprocity: if AI governance is genuinely multilateral, the rules should apply symmetrically.

The Anthropic question sits at the center of this dispute. China's official messaging characterizes Anthropic's decision to block services to Chinese-affiliated companies as discriminatory. The US framing is different: Anthropic acted on national security grounds in response to documented AI model extraction activity, including large-scale distillation attacks traced to Chinese AI labs. Both governments are reading the same set of events through fundamentally different frameworks — one of safety reciprocity, one of national security defense. That gap in interpretation is likely to outlast any single summit.

On the underlying technology question, assessments of the US-China AI capability gap vary. Current benchmark data — GPT-5.6 Sol at 89.5% versus Kimi K3 at 85.0% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 — suggests a meaningful but narrowing lead for US frontier models, with confidence levels moderate given the pace of development on both sides.

The September 24 Trump-Xi summit will likely clarify whether AI governance becomes a structured negotiating track or remains a source of bilateral friction. The conditions Beijing has laid out make that path narrow — but not necessarily by design. The reciprocity argument reflects a genuine strand of Chinese AI governance thinking, even if the timing gives it strategic utility.

The harder question for both sides is whether a shared AI safety framework is achievable given the depth of the underlying technology competition. That question will outlast this summit.

text:
🚨 OPINION- AFRICA MUST SPEAK WITH ONE VOICE: BRICS+ AGAINST IMPERIAL EXTRACTION|||

Prof David Monyae’s warning on New Order is overdue: Africa cannot keep negotiating as fifty fragments while Europe and America treat our soil as a quarry. 

A nationalist and socialist reading of the present is simple. Sovereignty means we own the mine, the smelter and the factory. 

Anything less is a refined form of colonial tribute. BRICS+ has begun to break that pattern. South Africa, Egypt, Nigeria and Ethiopia now sit at the table. 

The New Development Bank’s one-billion-dollar loan to eight South African metros for water, sanitation and waste is not charity; it is infrastructure that Western lenders long treated as a lecture topic. 

In the first half of 2026 Chinese Belt and Road engagement in Africa jumped more than 250%, with Ethiopia and Egypt among the largest destinations. Egypt’s trade with the bloc climbed toward fifty-four billion dollars. 

Ethiopia inaugurated the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam and is selling surplus power across borders. These are the first outlines of industrial capacity rather than raw-ore shipments.

The Western offer remains extraction dressed as partnership. 

Critical-minerals strategies from Washington and Brussels chase cobalt, lithium and rare earths to secure their own energy and weapons chains. 

Tariffs, aid cuts and “commercial diplomacy” punish governments that refuse to stay junior partners. 

THAT IS NOT DEVELOPMENT. 

It is the same old order: our minerals leave; their profits and their rules stay.

A radical socialist programme would use BRICS finance to build public processing, regional power pools and continental industry under African control, not another set of foreign shareholders. 

UNITY IS THE CONDITION. 

Divided, we remain a resource periphery. 

Together, we can refuse the oppressive order that still wants our earth without our consent.

#MadlangaCommission #Eskom #SouthAfricans #BRICS #AfricaMustUnite #MultipolarWorld

text:
Washington Is Starting to Squeeze Kyiv

1. This is not just a visit by Trump’s envoys to Ukraine. It signals that Washington is accelerating its diplomatic game because the war is becoming a strategic burden that is increasingly difficult to manage. Zelenskiy may call the talks constructive, but diplomacy has yet to change the reality on the battlefield.

2. Trump has a major political interest in showing that he can push the war toward negotiations. The problem is that a rushed peace could force Kyiv into compromises it has resisted for years, while Russia would retain military leverage.

3. For Zelenskiy, accepting American pressure without strong security guarantees is a dangerous gamble. Russia still has military pressure, while territory remains the hardest issue in any negotiation; therefore, every claim of “progress” deserves suspicion until Moscow offers something concrete.

text:
"Out of control," says the man whose own government's data says otherwise. BLS, July: groceries up 2.7%. Core inflation: 2.5%. That is not a crisis, Congressman — that is Tuesday. You have to squint at the Consumer Price Index like a horoscope to find your apocalypse in it.

And "war of choice"? Nobody in Washington chose to close the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran did that, then spent the summer firing on commercial shipping — three vessels on July 6–7 alone. Yes, gas is $4.09. That's what happens when a regime holds a third of the world's seaborne oil hostage and the alternative on offer is to let it. You may call the response a quagmire. Insurers, shippers, and every Gulf state that got hit call it Tuesday's bill for Monday's blockade.

Accountability is a fine word. Try applying it to the party that spent February through July with no plan of its own beyond a hashtag and a hot take.

Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) mocked longtime Trump aide Natalie Harp by her first name alone, sneering that the president “𝘨𝘰𝘭𝘧𝘴 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘵𝘳𝘢𝘥𝘦𝘴 𝘴𝘵𝘰𝘤𝘬𝘴 … 𝘏𝘦 𝘸𝘢𝘯𝘵𝘴 𝘵𝘰 𝘣𝘶𝘪𝘭𝘥 𝘩𝘪𝘴 𝘣𝘢𝘭𝘭𝘳𝘰𝘰𝘮 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘵𝘳𝘢𝘷𝘦𝘭 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘕𝘢𝘵𝘢𝘭𝘪𝘦 𝘰𝘯 𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘪𝘳 𝘢𝘱𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦𝘯𝘵𝘭𝘺 𝘥𝘦𝘧𝘦𝘯𝘴𝘦𝘭𝘦𝘴𝘴 𝘧𝘭𝘺𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘱𝘢𝘭𝘢𝘤𝘦 𝘨𝘪𝘧𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘣𝘺 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘦𝘮𝘪𝘳 𝘰𝘧 𝘘𝘢𝘵𝘢𝘳” — a line built entirely on insinuation he never had to prove.

It worked. Within three days, according to Blaze Media co-founder Glenn Beck, “𝘚𝘭𝘢𝘵𝘦 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘳𝘶𝘯𝘯𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘢 𝘩𝘦𝘢𝘥𝘭𝘪𝘯𝘦 𝘢𝘴𝘬𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘸𝘩𝘦𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘱𝘳𝘦𝘴𝘪𝘥𝘦𝘯𝘵 𝘰𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘜𝘯𝘪𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘚𝘵𝘢𝘵𝘦𝘴 𝘪𝘴 𝘴𝘭𝘦𝘦𝘱𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘩𝘪𝘴 𝘦𝘹𝘦𝘤𝘶𝘵𝘪𝘷𝘦 𝘢𝘴𝘴𝘪𝘴𝘵𝘢𝘯𝘵”. The Daily Beast published her private letters. CNN counted her tweets from five years ago. The Guardian ran two separate pieces, and a New Republic writer who once ran Obama’s social media accounts declared she is “𝘢 𝘥𝘢𝘯𝘨𝘦𝘳 𝘵𝘰 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘳𝘦𝘱𝘶𝘣𝘭𝘪𝘤”.

The Washington Post flew a reporter to Nicaragua to interview Harp’s estranged brother — a self-described Sandinista with Che Guevara books on his shelf and an FSLN flag on his wall — and used him as a character witness against his own sister.

Harp survived stage-2 bone cancer in her mid-20s, a fight in which she has said doctors offered her opioids, do-not-resuscitate paperwork and a conversation about dy∗ng with dignity. None of that stopped the pile-on: 𝐒𝐧𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐬 𝐡𝐚𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐩𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐢𝐬𝐡 𝐚 𝐟𝐚𝐜𝐭-𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐜𝐤 𝐨𝐧 𝐰𝐡𝐞𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐜𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐫 𝐰𝐚𝐬 𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧 𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐥.

“𝘚𝘩𝘦’𝘴 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘢 𝘴𝘦𝘤𝘶𝘳𝘪𝘵𝘺 𝘵𝘩𝘳𝘦𝘢𝘵. 𝘚𝘩𝘦’𝘴 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘢 𝘴𝘤𝘢𝘯𝘥𝘢𝘭 … 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘴𝘩𝘦’𝘴 𝘣𝘦𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘵𝘢𝘬𝘦𝘯 𝘢𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘵 𝘰𝘯 𝘯𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯𝘢𝘭 𝘵𝘦𝘭𝘦𝘷𝘪𝘴𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘤𝘳𝘪𝘮𝘦 𝘰𝘧 𝘴𝘵𝘢𝘯𝘥𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘵𝘰𝘰 𝘤𝘭𝘰𝘴𝘦 𝘣𝘦𝘤𝘢𝘶𝘴𝘦 𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘺 𝘤𝘢𝘯’𝘵 𝘨𝘦𝘵 𝘩𝘪𝘮,” Beck said. He’s right — the same press that lectures America about compassion turned its fact-checkers loose on a woman’s oncology history, not because she did anything wrong, but because saying her first name out loud got a bigger laugh than any policy attack could.

text:
General Douglas MacArthur's soldiers were living on half rations in the jungles of Bataan when a bank transfer of half a million dollars landed quietly in his account.

Manila had just been declared an open city, and American and Filipino troops were falling back into the peninsula with no real hope of resupply.

Philippine President Manuel Quezon, grateful for MacArthur's prewar work building the islands' defense force, arranged the payment as a personal reward.

MacArthur accepted it without hesitation, along with earlier gifts and a title to a Manila apartment.

His chief of staff, Richard Sutherland, took seventy five thousand dollars of his own, and two other aides accepted smaller sums.

Dwight Eisenhower, who had also served under MacArthur in Manila, was offered money by Quezon and turned it down flat.

In today's money, MacArthur's payment came to nearly eight million dollars, wired to him while his men starved a few miles away.

President Roosevelt and Secretary of War Henry Stimson both knew about the transfer and chose to say nothing.

The secret held for decades, hidden from an American public who saw MacArthur as a symbol of dogged resistance.

Historian Carol Petillo finally uncovered the record in 1979, long after MacArthur's death, and published what Washington had buried.

The revelation complicated a legend that had stood almost untouched for a generation.

The disclosure did not erase MacArthur's wartime reputation, but it permanently complicated it, forcing historians to weigh his undeniable leadership against a payment that looked, at best, deeply uncomfortable. Defenders argued Quezon had every right to reward a man who built his nation's army from nothing; critics pointed to the timing, with starving troops on Bataan and Corregidor still months from surrender. Eisenhower's refusal became its own quiet footnote, a contrast that made MacArthur's choice look worse with every retelling. The story stayed buried for over thirty years partly because Roosevelt needed MacArthur as a hero. When it finally surfaced, it reshaped how historians read the general's later career, adding a permanent asterisk to the myth of Bataan.

text:
Every engine posted about so far has a camshaft. Every Hemi, every Cammer, every small-block, every big-block, every Duramax, every Cummins every one of them breathes through a component whose profile was shaped by principles that Ed Iskenderian helped establish in a small shop in Culver City, California, in 1946. The camshaft is the engine's personality: it determines when the valves open, how long they stay open, how far they open, and how aggressively they close. Change the cam and you change everything the idle quality, the power curve, the RPM range, the exhaust note, the drivability. Every performance engine builder, including Jon Kaase, Smokey Yunick, Waddell Wilson, Lamer Walden, Chris Komarony selected a camshaft as one of the first decisions in their build. Ed Iskenderian spent eighty years making sure the cam they selected existed.
Iskenderian was born July 10, 1921, in Cutler, California Tulare County, grapevine country to first-generation Armenian immigrant parents. Frost killed the family's grape crop and forced a move to Los Angeles when Ed was a year old. As a teenager during the Depression, he noticed guys driving stripped-down Model Ts around LA not hot rods yet, just "go-jobs" and followed them on his bicycle. His first job was repairing vacuum tube radios. He built his first car as a teenager and raced it on the dry lake beds surrounding Los Angeles at speeds exceeding 120 mph. He served in the Army Air Corps during World War II, flying supply missions in the Pacific Theater with the Air Transport Command. When he came home in 1946, he founded Isky Racing Cams with a single cam-grinding machine he designed and built himself because he couldn't get the camshaft he wanted from Ed Winfield, who was too backlogged to fill orders. Winfield the pioneer of performance camshaft design told Iskenderian he could tell from his questions that he was going to be big in the camshaft business. Then he showed the young man how to build a grinding machine. The mentor armed the competitor who would eventually surpass him.
Iskenderian understood marketing before marketing was a discipline. A small ad in the second issue of Hot Rod Magazine started the inquiries many from Southern bootleggers who needed faster cars for the same reason hot rodders did. He traded advertising blows with rival cam manufacturers especially Jack Engle and later Howards Cams with clever copy and hilarious Pete Millar-drawn cartoons that turned camshaft ads into entertainment. Having "Isky Cams" lettered on your race car became a status symbol in the 1950s. Don Garlits ran the Isky "5 Cycle" cam. Big John Mazmanian ran Isky in the A/Gas Supercharged wars. Mickey Thompson ran Isky at Bonneville when he hit 406 mph. Garlits built a shrine to Iskenderian inside his Museum of Drag Racing. The man who ground cams in a Culver City shop earned a shrine in the museum of the greatest drag racer who ever lived. That's the respect the Camfather commanded.
The industry-building contribution that outlasts even the camshafts: in 1963, Iskenderian co-founded the Speed Equipment Manufacturers Association SEMA and served as its first president. Before SEMA, the aftermarket performance industry was a collection of individual shops and small manufacturers with no national organization, no unified voice, and no political representation. Iskenderian helped unite them giving racers, builders, and manufacturers a national stage that eventually grew into the most powerful trade organization in the American automotive aftermarket. Every SEMA Show in Las Vegas, every aftermarket catalog, every performance parts retailer that exists today operates within the framework that Iskenderian helped create in 1963. The Camfather didn't just build camshafts. He built the industry that sells them.
Iskenderian was the first to build an engine making one horsepower per cubic inch on pump gasoline in a postwar Dodge Hemi, years before Chevrolet's fuel-injected 283 reached that milestone in 1957. He was the first to offer complete valvetrain component sets cam, lifters, springs, retainers, locks as matched packages rather than individual parts. He pioneered the use of computer-aided design in camshaft profile development. He innovated high-performance camshaft profiles that became the templates every subsequent cam manufacturer followed. The "Isky 505" and "5 Cycle" cam profiles became legendary designations that racers ordered by name the way musicians request songs.
Even past his hundredth birthday in 2021, Iskenderian remained a presence at motorsport gatherings that defied biology. Warren Johnson the Professor of Pro Stock chatted with him at the 2020 Winternationals. Jack Beckman and Tim Wilkerson hung with him at the 2023 Night of Champions. John Force sought him out. At the 2024 NHRA Finals in Pomona, Iskenderian 103 years old took a lap down the return road and the fans roared. He sent autographed photos to admirers with a simple inscription: "From one hot rodder to another." Thousands of them. Over decades.
Ed Iskenderian died February 4, 2026, in Torrance, California. He was 104 years old. His passage was peaceful which, as RacingJunk noted, is an anomaly for a man whose entire lifespan was built on noise, vibration, and harshness. A teenager on a bicycle following gow jobs through Depression-era Los Angeles. A veteran who came home and built a cam grinding machine. The first president of SEMA. A man still showing up at racetracks at 103. Ed Iskenderian lived the entire history of American hot rodding from the dry lakes to the digital age and shaped more of it than almost anyone who ever lived. Every camshaft in every engine on this page exists in a world the Camfather helped build.

text:
Richard Gere was offered the part of Edward Lewis starring opposite to Julia Roberts in "Pretty Woman" (1990), but he turned it down a few times. Gere felt that "There wasn't a part. There was just nothing. The joke was it was just a suit. You could put a suit on a goat and put it out there, and it would work." For the role, Julia Roberts did screen tests with 10 other actors including Charles Grodin.

One day, Garry Marshall brought Julia Roberts to Richard Gere's office. He introduced them and excused himself to the restroom. "I was so mesmerized I don't remember Garry," Gere admitted. "I only remember the girl." 

When Marshall returned, he found that they had great chemistry. They were getting to know each other & were flirty. Then Marshall asked Gere, "How's it going?" Immediately, Julia Roberts, who was sitting across Gere's desk, took a Post-it note and wrote, "Please say yes" & pushed it towards Gere. He said, "It was so sweet, and after that, it was, 'I just said yes.'"

P.S: Happy 77th birthday, Richard Gere!

text:
4/

At the western landing, the sea had left signs of extraordinary violence.

Equipment had been damaged.

A storage box had been torn from its place.

And ropes and other items had been swept away.

Whatever had happened there, the Atlantic had struck the island with enormous force.

But that still didn’t explain why all three men had disappeared.

5/

The official investigation offered a grim theory.

Perhaps one keeper had gone outside to secure equipment near the landing.

A second may have followed to help him.

Then something went wrong.

A huge wave may have swept them into the sea.

But what about the third man?

Why would he leave the lighthouse too — possibly without his outdoor gear?

6/

One possibility was that he saw his companions in danger and rushed outside to help.

If so, all three men may have been standing near the cliffs when another enormous wave struck.

In seconds, the sea could have taken them all.

No bodies were ever recovered.

But even this explanation left questions.

7/

Over the years, the disappearance became surrounded by darker stories.

Some accounts claimed an unfinished meal was found on the table.

Others said a chair had been overturned.

And one famous version claimed the lighthouse log described terrified men praying as a mysterious storm raged outside.

Those details helped turn the case into a legend.

But there was a problem.

Much of it wasn’t true.

8/

The dramatic logbook entries appear to have been invented years later.

There is no reliable contemporary evidence that the keepers wrote about crying, praying, or a strange supernatural storm.

The real records point toward something less supernatural — but no less terrifying.

A violent sea.

A dangerous landing.

And three experienced men who somehow vanished without leaving a trace.

9/

More than 125 years later, no one can say with certainty exactly what happened to James Ducat, Thomas Marshall and Donald McArthur.

The most likely explanation remains that they were swept into the Atlantic by powerful waves.

But there were no witnesses.

No bodies.

And no final message.

The lighthouse remained.

The men simply disappeared.

And that is why the mystery of the Flannan Isles still endures.

I called my sixty-eight-year-old second cousin Rosemary thirty minutes ago.   She lives near the Canadian border.  She doesn’t keep up with the news, so I asked if she’d heard anything lately. She said she hadn’t watched any in a few weeks.  

I told her I’d catch her up.  I talked about the war with Iran still going on. 
I told her President Trump wanted to rename Lake Ontario to Lake America. She stayed with me, following along just fine.  She knew about the war.  She told me about the controversy in her town.  

Then I got to the murder case in Massachusetts, the Clancy mother who killed three of her children.  It’s horrific and purely barbaric.  I hadn’t wanted to give her anything that dark, but there didn’t seem to be much good news anywhere.

She went quiet. I kept going. I was persistent. I wanted to know why she’d stopped talking, especially since three innocent lives were taken.  Little by little it came out.

When she was younger, her mother demanded an abortion, and took her to have one. She was old enough to tell her mother and brother.  I didn’t ask how old.  She paused, when she remembered I am fully against it.  

The father of the baby was a teenager, and he wasn’t Caucasian. I didn’t ask too much. She was already crying. I was trying to be comforting.

I am a strong believer that abortion is murder. I don’t care who or what the cases consist of.   It’s wrong.  Period. 
She married right out of high school to escape her mother’s rules.  

She and her late husband tried for years to conceive, but she never could have children.
She had a mental breakdown, right after he passed away.   She is totally functional, being chemically dependent.  

She lives with her brother and his daughter. After we hung up I sat there feeling horrible.  I had pulled something private out of her while, I was trying to catch her up on the news.  I stayed comforting her.  

I called her brother, whom filled me in as to why the conversation is hitting her hard.  It’s around the anniversary.  She is now a devoted Catholic.  She has repent.  He went on to say how his mother was racist, and his father never was told.  My grandma offered to adopt the baby.   Her mother refused.  She took it extremely hard.  He believes she was 16 or 17.  She was forbidden to see the boy again.   He was a classmate and he was never told.

I keep thinking about what to send her.   Should I just let it go or send a food delivery….. maybe a fruit arrangement or a peace lily?​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
