~Malaysia: 21.12 million (Jan–Jun), +2.5% YoY. Highest volume in SEA, but includes many short-stay / day visitors . Slowest H1 growth since the post-COVID rebound.

~Thailand: 20.32 million (1 Jan–22 Aug), −3.0% YoY. Still #1 by tourism spend. Through 15 Aug: 19.76 million (−2.9%). July was 2.55 million (−2.5%).

~Vietnam: 13.92 million (Jan–Jul), +13.8% YoY. Clear growth leader. About 56% of the 25 million full-year target after seven months. July: 1.67 million (+6.6%).

text:
Had the awesome privilege to get my hands on a @Bitkey this weekend , huge shout out to @JoelBomgar . Here are my initial thoughts . I’m going to try to offer some original insight beyond the typical reviews I’ve seen in the past few weeks (no seed phrase, etc). Not sponsored/endorsed/etc, DYOR

Very impressed with the hardware build. Feels like a stone in my hands. The touchscreen display is super crisp and clean, very bright and sharp. 

The NFC functionality is seamless. Definitely the easiest tap-to-phone tech I’ve ever used. The CCQ I had used before was always a little iffy with its NFC, so by comparison this thing is near perfect

The entire setup process was so easy my parents could do it. I opened the box and had funds on the wallet in less than 10 minutes. Incredibly user friendly and intuitive . 

As a Strike user, I definitely appreciate how easy it is to buy with Strike and automatically deposit into a Bitkey address. The built in integration is a huge plus. Given the cost of transferring however, I think the more effective strategy is to stack sats on Strike over time, and send a large UTXO to Bitkey using Strike’s free transfer feature. But again, for a beginner, this is a nice to have. 
App is clean and a good design, flows well with the device , no qualms 

Some other thoughts:
I’m going to shy away from apeing my entire stack onto this device , at least for a while, for a few reasons. Namely, UTXO management. I’m excited to see how Bitkey handles that in the coming weeks as I understand they’re working on something currently.

Similarly , I think the thought process of keeping your entire stack on one setup (no matter how secure, multi sig / passphrase or not) is soon to be an outdated way of thinking of self custody. I can see Bitkey being a great addition to a robust setup with multiple wallets of multiple styles of configurations.

The narratives around Bitkey’s increased marketing efforts in the wake of Coldcard is total doomerism to me. Not buying it at all. It’s a quality product.

If you are a paranoid Bitcoin sovereignty freakazoid who is chronically online and knows the ins and outs of every technology behind the protocol, then this probably isn’t meant for you. But then again, what exactly is the solution for those types of people? 

Overall very satisfied and excited about the product. Looking forward to putting it through more paces and seeing what the future of Bitkey has in store for the community.

text:
Building Community, one party at a time.

It is 5:00 am and the voice in my head is talking again. As authors, we call it the muse. I don’t really know whose voice it is. Sometimes, I like to think it is the voice of God himself, but then why, I am not that important. As always, I leave that to mystery. What I do know is that the voice is important and I need to listen and act on it. All my good, and often crazy ideas came from that voice. All my writings, books, moves, wines and companies came from that voice. I merely listened, wrote and acted, just like this morning.

For some time now I have been feeling that the world is heading in the wrong direction. AI, a tool I use, seems to have accelerated this. Not because of the tool it is, but because of the anti-Christ like religion that seems to have grown around it. It is treated like it is God or will become God, and what a folly and dangerous idea that is. I am certain that no matter how all knowing it might become, it will never wake me up at 5:00 am in the morning to start talking to me.

God sent his son, Jesus Christ onto this world so we would get to know Him and find our way to God. He showed us our path by helping humanity, by caring, forgiving and loving, by demonstrating what it is to be human. In the wake of this the largest community in the world was born to carry that word and example for humanity. I have observed that most spiritual leaders and prophets who are the seed of other religions have that in common in some form. And while we could argue about scripture and specific aspects of it, I see common ground among most spiritual paths. As a former negotiator, I have learned common ground is what we should focus on and how people come together.

AI on the other hand seems to have the promise of being all knowing like God, take all jobs away, empower robots with no spirit, heart or life, and is endowed with the power to exterminate humanity, so we should fear it like God fearing beings. When the Holy books were written, I don’t think anyone had this scenario in mind, but this very much sounds like an anti-Christ to me. Not necessarily the tool of AI, but the deliberate religion that is shaping around it.

I find that in my 60s I have a better capacity to look back and reflect on my life and the experiences I was offered than in my younger days. Somehow, I can see better how everything fits together, even though at times it takes me weeks or months of pondering until I wake up at 5:00 am with a voice and clarity that most certainly comes from beyond me.

I was raised Catholic, but left the Church behind in my teenage years. I audaciously questioned our priest on the emptiness of sermons in a church where congregation members would return to a life of sin the moment they left the building. I believed in a living Church and was too full of myself to properly listen to our priest. I don’t regret any of this and now know that God leads people in mysterious ways. Leaving the Church opened up my heart and mind to that of an explorer and I researched many text and practices of other spiritual paths where I often discovered common ground. Over the years all this opened me up to see God’s guidance into my every day life and build a direct relationship. I learned to see real value and meaning in the scriptures I had read during my childhood and early teens. When I came across the writings of the Archbishop of El Salvador, Oscar Romero, I knew their was a living Church within the Church, and that it is up to each of us to set such an example.

Again, I struggled to see how I could truly live a life of meaning in a world of materialism. Maybe I already was doing something for some time but knew there was more I could or should do. I have put my faith in the mysterious morning voice since my twenties and have followed it religiously even when it tells me to do the most crazy things, like moving my family, my wife and our 3 young children, to a different continent with no job or place to live in sight. I have many such examples and have come to understand that this is what is meant when sacred text talk about living a life of faith. My near death experience in my thirties, a gift I received after I decided to leave the corporate world with the intention to live a life of purpose, burned that faith deep into my soul. I guess my soul always knew, I should say it was burned into my mind, that part of us that often tends to question or fear faith.

In recent months, I have felt that all the experiences in my life, all the gifts I have been given, are pulling together into one focused mission: building community. And while, as a winemaker and story teller, I could see parts of how to do this for some time, only at 5:00 am this morning when the voice started talking it showed me the picture with clarity.

A number of things happened simultaneously over the last few months and while I could feel there was a connection, I could not see the full picture.

- I have been having this clear sense that their will be a backlash against AI, robots and social media because people crave human connection, interaction and being of service to each other.

- I started weaving my life’s story and the lessons I discovered along the way into my winery tour and tasting where I show people how we make flower wine. I named it the Wine & Wisdom Story. As part of that I started sharing how God has been leading me through life and I observed how the story inspires people.

- I have learned to answer the question my son asked me when he was seven, the question that led me to leave my corporate career, the question that inspired my first book: “Why do people have to pay for food?” After all, I needed an answer to this question in case my grand children would ask me this as well.

- I finally fully understood why God led me to start a winery. I had already learned that it was to bring our family together, but finally understood it was much bigger. The wine and winery were only a path to building community.

- I rewrote the company’s vision and mission as follows:
Vision: A world where people gather again, where sharing a glass of flower wine turns strangers into friends, friends into community, and moments into memories.
Mission: To bring people together through the sharing of exceptional flower wine, creating real human connection in an increasingly digital world, and enabling those who share it to build a rewarding life doing so.

- Then I developed the Florvino Flower Somm program which allows people to build community by sharing flower wine while making an income, one home party at a time.

When I woke up this morning the voice said exactly that. Follow the example, build community by sharing wine and breaking bread. At once I could see how everything in my life led up to this moment. My job became a calling. Flower wine making and teaching others in the craft will always be a critical part of it, but as of now it is intrinsically merged with being a story teller again. I will share my story, share how my life experiences led me to build the company I deep down always envisioned, a company that empowers and inspires, a company for the people by the people. The world craves it in a time when social media, AI and robots tear us apart and keep us isolated.

And so my story of a Catholic boy, audacious teenager, corporate executive, confused and moved soul in the face of poverty, near death experience, life of purpose, author, wine maker and entrepreneur all blend into one vision, one colorful painting, one life, one focus. Build community, bring people together, face to face, to have real conversations and hugs, share stories, tears and smiles. I will share and hope to inspire to rebuild community across the world by sharing wine and breaking bread. I hope many of you will join me in that effort, with any wine and bread. Let’s make humanity bloom again.

text:
What an extraordinary mixture of triumphalism, insecurity and nostalgia for an era when unionism expected to call the shots.

“Republicans seething”, “PUL stands tall”, “we’re pushing back”, “we keep winning” , this isn’t the language of reconciliation or a shared society. It’s the language of people who still seem to view equality as a contest in which one community must be on top and the other put back in its place.

You forget that what’s occurring in nationalism is actually equality, it’s your neighbours celebrating their culture, it’s called equality but you view it as sectarian, because your so called culture is all you believe should be able to be on show. 

And what exactly is the political offer here? Cost of living? Health service? Housing? Jobs? Investment? A positive vision for young people?

No — Drumcree. Again.🤦‍♂️ this is your offering to the younger generation? 

A dispute rooted in the 1990s is apparently the great project around which parts of loyalism want to mobilise in 2026. Rather than taking Northern Ireland forward, they are dragging everyone back towards one of the most poisonous disputes of the peace-process era.

And they might want to contain the celebrations. The court did not establish an unrestricted right to march down the Garvaghy Road. If a future application is again refused or restricted, what happens then? We already know how dangerous the rhetoric of “siege”, “victory”, “fightback” and “no surrender” can become when expectations are deliberately raised. If disorder follows in loyalist areas, those who spent months whipping people into believing they were entitled to march through a predominantly Catholic community shouldn’t pretend to be astonished.

That is what makes all this talk of “moving forward” so ridiculous. You don’t build reconciliation by resurrecting Drumcree and telling one community that another community’s desire to parade through its neighbourhood must take precedence.

The old supremacy politics are finished. The days when organisations could behave as though Catholics should simply stand aside and know their place belong in history. Those KKK-style notions of religious supremacy and triumphalism have no place in a modern society. Nobody is entitled to cultural dominance over their neighbours.

And then comes the funniest part: the United Ireland obsession.

Apparently Irish unity is a “fantasy”. Nobody wants it. It’s never happening. Unionists aren’t remotely concerned.

Yet they post about it every single day. 😂

Andy Burnham mentions it: meltdown.
Michelle O’Neill mentions it: meltdown.
Sinn Féin mentions it: meltdown.
Opinion polls appear: meltdown.
Someone waves a tricolour: meltdown.

For people supposedly laughing at the idea, they spend an incredible amount of their lives desperately reassuring each other that it will never happen.

Perhaps instead of trying to recreate the politics of Drumcree, they could offer people something worth staying in the Union for.

Because “NO SURRENDER, DRUMCREE AND THEM UNS ARE SEETHING” isn’t a political vision for the future.

It’s a tribute act to a past that thankfully isn’t coming back.

text:
Modest Turnout at Cost-of-living Protest as Questions about the Organiser Remain Unanswered

A cost-of-living protest called for O’Connell Bridge in Dublin and other locations today attracted a modest crowd. Photographs from the scene and accounts given to SnD Media put numbers in the dozens rather than the nationwide turnout organiser Michelle Keane had billed.

Keane, a Kerry businesswoman and unsuccessful 2024 independent candidate, had presented the event as a show of public anger over prices and government policy. Those who contacted SnD Media said many people had already decided not to attend after questions raised in yesterday’s report, which has been widely shared.

SnD Media is not adopting or endorsing the comments that followed that report. We are publishing them because they were put to us by members of the public, they concern a person who organised a public protest and a public fundraiser, and Keane has not yet answered the questions we put to her. We remain ready to publish her response.

The questions raised with us included whether she had sought to take a leading role in fuel protests after appearing with principal fuel spokespeople at the Tullamore Show; why she launched a GoFundMe seeking €20,000 during a cost-of-living crisis; and how public attacks on fellow activists sat with the causes she says she supports.

The GoFundMe page, titled “KEANE SAVE IRELAND FUNDRAISING,” states that money is sought for investigations and legal proceedings into alleged election irregularities, related court matters, and campaigning. Some members of the public told SnD Media they still wanted a clearer public account of how donations have been used. That is their question, not a finding by this outlet.

Days after appearing with John Dallon, Christopher Duffy and James Geoghegan, figures associated with April’s fuel demonstrations, Keane posted a graphic showing the men in British uniforms under the caption: “For the throwback semen of the Black & Tans left behind.” People who contacted us said they regarded that post as an attack on activists they credit with the April protests.

Questions were also raised about Mark Sinclair speaking at a GPO protest she organised in July 2025. The Irish Times has described Sinclair as a self-confessed former UVF member who served 18 years after armed-robbery convictions. Critics asked how that association sat with her “Black and Tans” rhetoric.

Keane has accused conservative figures including Elaine Mullally, Chris Duffy and John Dallon of trying to sabotage today’s protest and damage her name. SnD Media has not independently found evidence to support those sabotage claims.Comments published under yesterday’s report included the following, which we repeat as statements by those individuals and not as the view of SnD Media:

Jack wrote that she “is an attention seeker, has nothing to offer & should explain where the go fund me money that ordinary people paid into went to.”Eileen Carberry said she was “delighted someone has called her out” and that Keane threatens legal action against critics.Jo-Jo Clark said she “needs to come out and answer these questions,” and Katie Donovan added: “We’ll be waiting….”

We have not repeated every personal characterisation sent to us. SnD Media does not allege that Keane is unstable, dishonest, or misusing funds. Those are matters on which she is entitled to reply.

The modest numbers on the ground suggest that, for some people, unanswered questions about the organiser mattered as much as the protest itself. That does not settle those questions. It is why we invited Ms Keane to engage and why we would still welcome her response.

text:
I appreciate this side of the argument, but I think it only inflates the problems and kicks them down the road.

It isn't just about public transport, we all know there is a ton of infrastructure needed anywhere you put homes. We're behind on just about every one of them from school places and SNAs to GPs and Garda resources, from public spaces and playgrounds or sports pitches to other amenities like the horse clubs etc. Unless we actually want children stuck to Xbox and tiktok we need to offer something better as a society. Living in a third floor apartment usually isn't it.

Then there's the other issues. Yes young couples need new homes, and you're correct nobody is starting Remigration anytime soon. But the other thing that isn't happening is, nobody is stopping vulture funds or businesses from buying up these new builds, or foreigners. So as long as you build it, they will come. It's a self perpetuating cycle imo. 

Think of the other negative aspects. Banks keep screwing Irish people as long as we try prop this inflated market up. That or landlords living off of external demand and government subsidy propping up rental prices. Landlords might have to lower prices to acquire tenants, but not when HAP etc keeps picking up the bill. There is a relatively new build of apartments near Raheny village. 500 a week for a one bedroom and none were for sale. Who is that really helping?

We're living through a Celtic Tiger style holding bubble except it won't burst... because immigration and institutional investors are keeping it getting fatter and fatter.

There's no perfect answer here, so I resort to the one that gives the external problems we face the least oxygen

• May 2025 — The administration accepted a Qatar-provided Boeing 747-8 for possible Air Force One use, raising ethics, security and foreign-influence concerns. Qatar denied seeking influence.

Netanyahu: Herzi Halevi, Ronen Bar and Aharon Haliva Knew About the October 7 Attack and Did Not Wake Me

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said former IDF chief of staff Herzi Halevi, former Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar and former military intelligence chief Aharon Haliva knew there were signs an attack was imminent on October 7 and did not wake him. He added: “If they had woken me, everything would have looked different. That is the story of October 7. That is the story.”

Many warning signs, the public does not know

Netanyahu said the public does not know that “there were many, many indicative signs that an attack was about to happen.” He named the three officials: Halevi knew, Bar knew, and Haliva knew. The obvious step, he said, was to wake the prime minister, “but they did not wake me.”

With that account, Netanyahu recasts the night of October 7 as an administrative decision inside the security establishment: information reached the top of the army, the Shin Bet and military intelligence, and was not passed to him at the moment he considers decisive.

What he says he would have done

Netanyahu said the three officials “knew exactly what I would do.” He defined that as activating the air force there, waking the entire Israeli army, allowing no one to approach the fence, and “we would kill them immediately.”

The narrative he offers separates the existence of a warning from its political and military activation. He does not deny Hamas’s offensive preparations. He confines the supposed difference to the speed of the response: air power, a full mobilization, and killing at the fence before it was breached.

By spelling this out, Netanyahu places himself outside the strategic misjudgment that preceded the attack and shifts responsibility to the hour the alarm should have been sounded at dawn: who held the signal, and who declined to wake the prime minister.

A political account versus institutional inquiries

The remarks come after months of internal IDF and Shin Bet inquiries that acknowledged unusual signs on the night of the attack, without concluding that the political leadership knew an assault was imminent in the terms Netanyahu describes. In earlier interviews, including on Channel 14 on August 30, he repeated that the scene “would have looked completely different” had he been woken, and that the protocols “will reveal the truth” when they are published.

Military and media investigations, by contrast, have reported that Halevi was briefed in the pre-dawn hours on suspicious signs, that the Shin Bet held an assessment before the attack, and that Netanyahu’s military secretary received a late update. Netanyahu skips that sequence and fixes the charge on a single point: that he himself was not woken.

In election season, everything is permitted: reopening the October 7 file in the name of truth, and turning the names of army, Shin Bet and intelligence chiefs into a direct accusation — before the full protocols are released and before an official inquiry settles the sequence of that night.

The story of October 7 as he tells it

Netanyahu’s statement rests on four claims he wants fixed in place: there were many signs of an imminent attack; Halevi, Bar and Haliva knew them; the natural step was to wake the prime minister and it was not taken; and had he been woken he would have activated the air force, woken the army and stopped anyone reaching the fence. He then closes: “That is the story of October 7.”

With that ending, Netanyahu shifts the debate from “who failed to read Hamas?” to “who held the information and did not pass it to the prime minister?” That is the account he is seeking to make the official frame of the failure, against the security establishment’s account of a mistaken assessment rather than a deliberate withholding of warning from the prime minister.

text:
The economic consequences of American legislator’s retreat from hemp are no longer theoretical. States are beginning to calculate the bill.

Tennessee offers one of the clearest early examples. After banning popular hemp products, July tax collections reportedly came in at roughly $425,000 against $9.4 million projected. If that continues, Tennessee is on pace for at least a $110 million annual revenue shortfall.

Texas provides another warning. The state’s own analysis of proposed hemp restrictions projected millions in lost state and local government revenue, while an independent economic analysis estimated Texas’s cannabinoid-hemp market generates approximately $268 million in annual tax revenue and billions of dollars in economic activity.

These numbers should force a much larger national conversation.

In 2018, Congress created a federal framework legalizing hemp. For nearly eight years, farmers planted crops, businesses invested capital, lenders extended credit, employees built careers, states developed regulatory and taxation systems, and tens of millions of Americans became consumers of hemp-derived products.

Now Congress is reversing course, and the economic consequences are beginning to emerge. Lost tax revenue is only the most visible number. Behind it are farmers, manufacturers, retailers, testing laboratories, distributors, packaging companies, landlords, employees, lenders and consumers—all participants in a $40 billion economy Congress itself helped create.

There were legitimate problems Congress needed to address. Intoxicating products should be appropriately regulated and age-restricted. Products deceptively packaged to resemble candy or familiar commercial brands should never have been tolerated. Nor should synthetics. Reasonable regulation could address those problems.

Instead, Congress chose an extraordinarily broad approach that will wipe out the broader federally legal hemp economy—including non-intoxicating CBD products used by roughly 50 million Americans. 

Hemp will become illegal because a 0.3% total THC limit cannot be met by any current hemp strain when all forms of THC (Delta-9, Delta-8, Delta-10, THCA, THCP, and THCV) are combined to calculate total THC, as the law now requires. Of the hundreds of commercial hemp strain specifications reviewed not one was capable of meeting the new standard.

And that raises a much larger question. As America celebrates its 250th anniversary, we hear a great deal about government “of the people, by the people, for the people.” What does that principle mean in practice when legislators seem increasingly disconnected from the people affected by their decisions?

Congress created the legal framework. Americans relied upon it for nearly eight years. Billions of dollars were invested. Farms and businesses were built. States constructed regulatory and taxation systems around it. Consumers incorporated legal products into their lives.

Then Washington dramatically changed course, with enormously consequential language moving through must-pass legislation without anything approaching the public debate, economic analysis or deliberation that a policy reversal of this magnitude deserved.

Government has the right—and the responsibility—to change laws when circumstances warrant. But government also has an obligation to consider the people who relied in good faith upon the laws it created.

Tennessee’s projected $110 million shortfall should therefore be viewed as more than a state budget problem. Texas’s projected losses should not be viewed in isolation either. They are early measurements of something much larger.

Multiply the consequences across 50 states, thousands of businesses, American agriculture, stat/local tax bases, and tens of millions of consumers, and the real question becomes much larger than hemp.

Two hundred and fifty years after our founding, does government still work for the people—or have we become accustomed to government simply happening to us?

text:
The post is a facepalm emoji paired with a 2024 *Daily Mail* screenshot of a woman whose life collapsed into bedbound illness after COVID, even after three vaccine doses. Two years later, it is being recirculated as a punchline.

Luizmd’s entire bio is explicit germ-theory denial: viruses have never been isolated, sequenced, or shown to cause disease. He cites Stefan Lanka and Thomas Cowan. Lanka, a German biologist who once worked on marine viruses, later offered €100,000 for proof of the measles virus’s existence and diameter, lost related legal fights, and extended the claim to HIV, Ebola, and SARS-CoV-2. Cowan published a “Statement on Virus Isolation” arguing that standard lab methods (inoculating patient samples into cell culture, then sequencing) do not constitute true isolation because the sample is not first purified to a single particle.

Mainstream virology treats that definition as non-standard. SARS-CoV-2 was cultured from patient samples in multiple independent labs beginning in January 2020 (Wuhan, Germany, the first U.S. case in Washington state). Those isolates produced matching whole-genome sequences, cytopathic effects in Vero and other cell lines, and electron-microscopy images of spherical particles with the expected nucleocapsid. The genome was released publicly on 10 January 2020 and has since been sequenced tens of thousands of times. Adapted versions of Koch’s/Rivers criteria have been applied through controlled infection studies in animals and through the consistent recovery of the same virus from sick people.

Long COVID itself is a heterogeneous post-acute syndrome. Large observational studies and some biomarker work (persistent viral RNA in tissues, immune dysregulation, microclots, autonomic dysfunction) support a biological basis in a subset of patients; it also overlaps heavily with ME/CFS and can be amplified by deconditioning, anxiety, or other conditions. Vaccination lowers but does not eliminate the risk. The *Daily Mail* piece is a human-interest story, not a controlled study; the “despite three jabs” framing is what the denialist audience reads as proof that the official story is inverted.

Replies under the post mostly invert the headline: “because, not despite.” Several attach memes or call the woman a “CovIDIOT.” That reaction is consistent with the poster’s premise—if the virus does not exist, then both the original illness and the lingering symptoms must be caused by something else (the shots, fear, toxins, or the body’s own “detox”).

The deeper tension is definitional. One side requires a 19th-century purification standard that modern molecular virology no longer uses. The other side treats repeated isolation, sequencing, microscopy, and animal challenge as sufficient. The woman’s reported suffering is real either way; the disagreement is over what caused it.

text:
August 31, 1823. If you have ever taken a photo of the Eiffel Tower from the Trocadéro, you were standing on the name of a Spanish fort that fell on this day.

Spain had a constitution and Ferdinand VII did not want one. A liberal revolt in 1820 forced him to accept the constitution of 1812, and for three years Spain was a constitutional monarchy with the king essentially a prisoner of it.

The other monarchies of Europe found this unacceptable. At the Congress of Verona they handed France the job of undoing it. Britain abstained and looked at the ceiling.

France sent an army nicknamed the Hundred Thousand Sons of Saint Louis under the Duke of Angoulême. The Spanish liberals fell back to Cádiz and took the king with them, anchoring their position on the fort of Trocadero across the water.

On August 31 the French waded the channel at low tide and took it at bayonet point. French losses were 110 wounded. That is the entire price of ending constitutional government in Spain.

Cádiz surrendered on September 23 and Ferdinand got his throne back. He had promised an amnesty. What actually followed was a wave of executions and imprisonments running into the tens of thousands.

Angoulême was offered the title Prince of Trocadero and refused it, reportedly out of disgust at what Ferdinand did with the country he had just been handed.

Paris named a hill after the battle anyway. That hill is where the Palais de Chaillot stands, which is where every single photograph of the Eiffel Tower is taken from.

One footnote. Watching a European coalition send an army to restore an absolutist king made Washington deeply nervous about what those same powers might try in Spain's former American colonies. Three months later, on December 2, 1823, Monroe delivered the Monroe Doctrine.

🇨🇦🇺🇸 What can Canada actually do to influence Trump?

After the Trump administration promised new and even higher tariffs on Canadian cars and auto parts starting in January 2027, more Canadians are asking the obvious question: What pressure or leverage can Canada use to make Washington change course?

But there’s a harder question: is there anything Canada can do that is actually guaranteed to change Donald Trump’s mind?

Canada is negotiating with an administration whose policies often appear unpredictable. Today there’s a tariff threat. Tomorrow there’s an offer for a deal. The day after that, entirely new conditions may appear.

As Christopher Ragan, founding director of McGill University’s Max Bell School of Public Policy, put it: “Canada is negotiating with a party that seems unpredictable and unstable, so I don’t think anyone really knows what will work here.”

And that may be the biggest problem.

❓ Should Canada respond with tough retaliatory tariffs?
❓ Should it use more serious leverage — energy, critical minerals and other strategic resources?
❓ Or should Canada stop trying to “break” Trump’s position and focus instead on diversifying trade and gradually reducing its dependence on the U.S. market?

Perhaps the real question is no longer how Canada wins the next round of negotiations. Maybe Canada needs to address a much bigger strategic problem:

🇨🇦 How do we build an economy that depends less on the political mood of one person in the White House?

What do you think? What real leverage does Canada have — and should it use it? 👇

text:
🕯️🎨 A 1636 PIETER QUAST IN A 1944 BUDAPEST BANK SAFE — AND A PROVENANCE TRAIL THAT STILL HAS NOT CLOSED

On 28 June 1944, officials gathered inside the safe-deposit department of the Magyar Leszámítoló és Pénzváltó Bank in Budapest to take possession of artworks from safe compartment 361/I, rented in the name of Dr. Dobay Aurélné — Mrs. Aurél Dobay, Baroness Margit Madarassy-Beck. The surviving protocol, 126/1944, states that the action was conducted by the Government Commissioner responsible for Jewish-owned art under Hungary’s wartime confiscatory regime. Fifteen paintings judged to be artworks were taken from the compartment into state custody.

Among them, item 12 is unusually precise:

“Hollandi festő XVII. szd. Mandolinozó/P. Quast 1636-ból/olajf. fára, 26.2 × 19 cm.”

In English: “Dutch painter, 17th century. Mandolin player/P. Quast, from 1636/oil on wood panel, 26.2 × 19 cm.”

That combination—P. Quast, 1636, a musician with a plucked string instrument, oil on panel, 26.2 × 19 cm—can now be compared with a published painting recorded by the Netherlands Institute for Art History, the RKD. The correspondence is sufficiently close that this deserves treatment as a serious object-level provenance candidate rather than a generic similarity.

🔎 The candidate: Pieter Quast, dated 1636

The RKD record 33785 describes a painting by Pieter Jansz. Quast, the Dutch Golden Age painter active in Amsterdam and The Hague:

Man en luitspelende vrouw
Man and lute-playing woman
Signed and dated upper right: PQuast 1636
Oil on wood panel
26.7 × 19.1 cm

RKD record:
https://t.co/fzKhHJA6NC

The structured data derived from the RKD record independently confirms the artist, the 1636 date, the Dutch title Man en luitspelende vrouw, oil on panel, and dimensions of 26.7 × 19.1 cm. Quast himself was a specialist in Dutch genre scenes, conversation pieces, comic subjects, soldiers and other scenes of contemporary life.

The subject wording is not identical. The Hungarian clerk called the picture Mandolinozó — Mandolin Player, while the modern Dutch title identifies a lute-playing woman with a man. That difference should not be hidden, but it is also not the strongest evidence either way: short wartime inventories routinely used compressed descriptive titles. What makes this candidate exceptional is the convergence of the more objective identifiers.

🎯 The physical correspondence is unusually tight

The artist aligns: the wartime protocol says P. Quast, while the published panel is by Pieter Quast and is recorded as signed PQuast. Even more importantly, the year is exact. The Hungarian officials did not merely write “17th century”; they added “P. Quast 1636-ból” — P. Quast, from 1636. The RKD painting is itself dated 1636.

The support also corresponds. The 1944 document says olajf. fára—oil paint on wood—while the RKD records an oil painting on panel. And the dimensions are exceptionally close: 26.2 × 19 cm in 1944 versus 26.7 × 19.1 cm in the published record. The difference is only 5 millimeters in height and 1 millimeter in width, well within a plausible range for different measurement conventions, rounding, or measuring a visible painted surface rather than the entire panel.

Taken together, the comparison is unusually specific: artist + inscribed year + wooden support + musical subject + near-identical dimensions. Any one of those features could occur elsewhere. Their convergence in a small seventeenth-century cabinet picture is much harder to dismiss as coincidence.

This still does not prove that RKD 33785 and item 12 from the Dobay safe are the same physical panel. Quast repeated genre types, and another contemporary version or copy cannot be excluded from the public documentation alone. But the evidence is strong enough to require the provenance records that can resolve the question.

🏛️ The candidate already had a Budapest history before 1944

The provenance attached to the RKD record makes the comparison more significant because this was not a painting with no connection to Hungary. According to the RKD, the panel was formerly in the collection of Hugo von Kilényi, a Budapest ministerial councillor and collector, and was at one time deposited or lent to the Szépművészeti Múzeum — Museum of Fine Arts, Budapest, under historic inventory number 8533.

The painting was subsequently offered in the sale of the Hugo von Kilényi collection at the Ernst Museum in Budapest on 26 November 1917. Heidelberg University Library preserves the digitized catalogue for that auction, independently confirming the Kilényi sale and its Budapest setting.

https://t.co/f103qQwPSz

That prewar history creates an important, but presently unresolved, question. If the Quast recorded in the Dobay safe in 1944 is the same panel, then sometime after the 1917 Kilényi sale it entered another collection and eventually reached Margit Madarassy-Beck’s safe-deposit compartment. The public sources examined for this post do not establish that intermediate ownership chain, and no buyer from 1917 should simply be assumed.

That missing bridge is precisely what an annotated auction catalogue, dealer record, Museum of Fine Arts loan file, collection inventory or inscription on the back of the panel could establish.

🗽 The painting resurfaced in New York in 1997

The RKD provenance later records the same panel at Sotheby’s New York, Old Master Paintings, 22 May 1997, lot 127, where no sale is recorded. The existence of the May 22, 1997 Sotheby’s Old Master Paintings auction is independently documented, and its artist index includes Pieter Jansz. Quast.

The post-1997 ownership history of this particular panel has not been established in the public sources reviewed for this post. That creates a second provenance gap, but it is important to distinguish the two: the first question is how the Kilényi panel moved from the documented Budapest art market of 1917 to the Dobay/Madarassy-Beck seizure context of 1944, if it did; the second is what happened to the panel after its documented twentieth-century market appearance.

A 1997 auction file may contain photographs of the reverse, old labels, inventory numbers, dealer annotations or earlier ownership information that never appeared in a short public catalogue entry. Those materials could either strengthen the correspondence to the 1944 safe inventory or conclusively rule it out.

👤 Margit Madarassy-Beck and Aurél Dobay

The name on the 1944 bank record deserves to be restored alongside the painting. Dr. Dobay Aurélné was Baroness Margit Madarassy-Beck (1878–1949), daughter of banker Baron Miksa Madarassy-Beck and a member of one of Budapest’s prominent Jewish banking and collecting families. Hungarian biographical records expressly identify “Dobay Aurélné” as Madarassy-Beck Margit.

Her husband, Dr. Aurél Dobay of Nagyhanta (1871–1946), was a lawyer and bank executive prominent in Budapest’s commercial life. The Jewish Digital Cultural Recovery Project independently lists Aurél Dobay among persecuted Jewish collectors and specifically cites the surviving Government Commissioner file MNL OL K 643-1944-126/A—the archival case to which this June 1944 material belongs.

The terminology of protocol 126/1944 is bureaucratic: megőrzés, preservation or safekeeping; zár alá vétel, placing under seal. But the practical result was that fifteen privately held paintings left a bank compartment rented by a Jewish woman and passed into the custody of the state authority created to control Jewish cultural property. The receiving side of the protocol includes Dénes Csánky, the Government Commissioner who simultaneously headed the Museum of Fine Arts.

Later wartime records make clear that the Dobays did not simply abandon their property. The Zekelman Holocaust Center’s finding aid identifies subsequent papers in which Dr. and Mrs. Aurél Dobay requested the return of their confiscated artifacts, invoking Swedish citizenship, while also seeking exemption from anti-Jewish restrictions.

Those later petitions are an important part of the story, but the presently available public record does not establish whether this particular Quast panel was included in a return request or whether it was ever restored to the family. That question requires the underlying case files.

📂 What would resolve the identification

The investigation now has several concrete documentary targets. The Museum of Fine Arts, Budapest should review and make available the historic loan documentation associated with Kilényi inventory 8533, including catalogue cards, photographs, measurements and any recorded marks on the reverse. The original and annotated copies of the 26 November 1917 Kilényi auction catalogue may identify the purchaser or provide a subsequent ownership lead.

The Hungarian wartime and immediate postwar files should then be searched for P. Quast, 1636, protocol 126/1944, safe 361/I, and the names Dobay and Madarassy-Beck. Of particular importance are any intake, movement, restitution or return records generated after the June 28 seizure and the later Dobay petitions seeking return of confiscated property.

The 1997 Sotheby’s file should also be revisited, subject to applicable confidentiality rules, for provenance documentation and photographs of the panel’s reverse. A current or later holder could provide the most decisive evidence of all through high-resolution verso photographs showing old labels, numbers, seals, collection marks or changes to the panel and frame.

This is exactly the kind of inquiry contemplated by the Washington Principles on Nazi-Confiscated Art and the 2024 Best Practices: identify objects with unresolved Holocaust-era provenance, make relevant archives accessible, and allow documentary evidence to determine whether a just and fair solution is required.

🕯️ An unusually specific record, and an answerable provenance question

HARI is not presenting the RKD painting as conclusively identified with the panel removed from the Dobay safe. The documentary bridge between the 1917 Kilényi sale and the 1944 Dobay inventory has not yet been established, and that missing link matters.

What we do have is unusually compelling: a Hungarian state protocol created at the moment of dispossession records P. Quast, 1636, oil on wood, a musician, 26.2 × 19 cm. The published art-historical record contains a Pieter Quast signed and dated 1636, oil on panel, 26.7 × 19.1 cm, with a documented prewar history in Budapest and a later twentieth-century appearance at Sotheby’s in New York.

That convergence is sufficient to justify a full provenance review. The remaining questions are concrete rather than speculative: Who acquired the panel after the 1917 Kilényi sale? Did it become the Quast recorded in Margit Madarassy-Beck’s safe in June 1944? What happened to that painting after it entered state custody? Did the Dobays recover it when they sought the return of their confiscated property? And what is the complete chain associated with the panel recorded again in the art market in 1997?

The relevant archives, museum files, auction records and the physical reverse of the painting can answer those questions. Eighty-two years after protocol 126/1944 recorded the work to the millimeter, the appropriate next step is to bring those records together and determine whether the 1636 Quast known to art history is the same panel taken from the Dobay safe.

Related @ArtRecoveryInit post: The Dobay Safe Seizure: A Candidate Identified at the Museum of Fine Arts, Budapest/Szépművészeti Múzeum

text:
From Clinton's Motor Voter to Shapiro's PennDOT:

BY DARRELL PITTS

Americans have heard enough speeches about the border.

The more immediate question before November 2026 is what happens after millions of noncitizens enter or remain in the United States.

Because the trail doesn't end at immigration processing.

It can continue through:

work authorization → Social Security number → American address → driver's license → Motor Voter → voter roll → mail ballot.

Most of those steps can be perfectly legal.

None makes a noncitizen a citizen.

That distinction is where election integrity begins.

And this didn't start with Josh Shapiro.

1993: CLINTON CONNECTS THE DMV TO VOTING

On May 20, 1993, Democratic President Bill Clinton signed the National Voter Registration Act—the Motor Voter Act.

Beginning January 1, 1995, covered states had to provide voter-registration opportunities through driver's-license transactions.

The excuse was convenience for eligible citizens.

But it permanently connected two government systems:

DRIVER LICENSING AND VOTER REGISTRATION; AND, THE CONNECTION PERMANENTLY DILUTED VOTER INTEGRITY.

That connection became more consequential as states changed who could receive licenses and how automatically DMV customers entered voter registration.

2013–2019: STATES EXPAND DRIVER'S-LICENSE ACCESS

In 2013, Democratic California Gov. Jerry Brown signed AB 60, allowing qualifying undocumented residents to obtain driver's licenses beginning January 1, 2015

In June 2019, Democratic New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo signed the Green Light Law, implemented that December

In December 2019, Democratic New Jersey Gov. Phil Murphy signed similar legislation

Today, 19 states and Washington, D.C. have enacted laws allowing unauthorized immigrants to obtain driver's licenses: DILUTES VOTER INTEGRITY.

WHEN RIDICULOUS CHANGE OCCURS SLOWLY, PEOPLE DON'T NOTICE.

Those licenses do not create citizenship or federal voting rights.

But they illustrate something essential:

A GOVERNMENT-ISSUED DRIVER'S LICENSE IS NOT PROOF OF U.S. CITIZENSHIP.
2015: MOTOR VOTER BECOMES AUTOMATIC

Oregon became the first state to enact modern Automatic Voter Registration in 2015. California enacted AVR legislation that year as well.

AVR changes the traditional Motor Voter approach.

Instead of an eligible DMV customer affirmatively opting into registration, the system moves eligible customers through the registration process unless they decline.

That makes the accuracy of the government's citizenship determination more—not less—important.

2019: PENNSYLVANIA MOVES VOTING TO THE MAIL

On October 31, 2019, Democratic Pennsylvania Gov. Tom Wolf signed Act 77, establishing no-excuse mail voting.

IT REDUCED VOTER INTEGRITY.

Then came COVID.

In the 2020 presidential election, registered Democrats returned approximately 1.70 million Pennsylvania mail ballots, compared with approximately 623,000 Republicans.

Among Democratic and Republican mail-ballot returns, roughly 73 percent were Democratic.

DO NOTHING REPUBLICAN POLITICIANS DIDN'T KNOW WHAT HIT THEM.

Mail voting itself is not fraud.
BUT, IT REDUCED VOTER INTEGRITY AND SAFEGUARDS.

But the numbers establish a political reality:

DEMOCRATS HISTORICALLY USED PENNSYLVANIA'S MAIL-VOTING CHANNEL FAR MORE HEAVILY THAN REPUBLICANS UNDER SUSPICIOUS CIRCUMSTANCES.

Keep that fact in mind.

2021–2024: THE MIGRATION SURGE BECOMES A DOCUMENT PIPELINE

During Democratic President Joe Biden's administration, the United States experienced an extraordinary migration surge alongside expanded use of parole, asylum processing, CBP One and related mechanisms.

CBP One appointments expanded significantly beginning in January 2023.

That same month, the administration expanded the CHNV parole process for Cubans, Haitians, Nicaraguans and Venezuelans.

The programs didn't make participants citizens.

But qualifying noncitizens could progress from immigration paperwork to employment authorization and, where federally eligible, a Social Security number.

They could work.

Establish an address.

Rent housing.

Open accounts.

And, depending upon state law and immigration status, obtain state identification or driver's licenses.

Every document could be genuine while the person remained a noncitizen.

That makes accurate citizenship classification critical wherever driver's-license systems connect directly to voter registration.

SEPTEMBER 19, 2023: SHAPIRO FLIPS PENNDOT

Pennsylvania generally requires qualifying lawful presence for noncitizen driver's licenses, unlike California's broader system.

But PennDOT still contains records for citizens and qualifying noncitizens.

On September 19, 2023, Democratic Gov. Josh Shapiro changed PennDOT voter registration from opt-in to automatic opt-out for eligible customers.

Shapiro later said:

“I AUTHORIZED AUTOMATIC VOTER REGISTRATION.”

Within roughly two months, he reported nearly 58,000 new or updated DMV registrations—a 70 percent increase over the comparable period two years earlier.

Automatic registration isn't inherently fraudulent.
BUT, IT DOES REDUCE VOTER INTEGRITY.

But Shapiro widened the PennDOT-to-registration pipeline.

Then Pennsylvania discovered that the eligibility filter protecting that pipeline could fail.

APRIL 17, 2026: THE AUDITOR FINDS A FAILURE

Republican Auditor General Timothy DeFoor audited PennDOT Motor Voter activity covering January 1 through June 30, 2024.

PennDOT transmitted more than 200,000 unique voter-registration applications during those six months.

Among 58 applications receiving additional examination, auditors found a noncitizen who had improperly been permitted to complete a voter-registration application because a manual data-entry error omitted the person's noncitizen status.

The error was caught.

The person ultimately was not registered.

But the audit demonstrated something important:

THE AUTOMATED FIREWALL CAN FAIL WHEN THE DATA BEHIND IT ARE WRONG.

DeFoor concluded that the overall system worked but that its internal controls and security needed improvement.

That finding doesn't establish mass noncitizen voting.

It establishes the question Pennsylvania should now answer:

How often does the classification fail?
IF THE DATA WAS WRONG OR RIGHT THE MACHINES COUNTED THE DATA NOT WHO WAS LEGAL OR ILLEGAL.

AUGUST 31, 2026: ANOTHER LICENSING SYSTEM SHOWS WHAT BAD DATA CAN DO

A separate federal crackdown provides a useful warning.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced action against fraudulent or noncompliant commercial-driver training operations.

Federal officials said more than 110 training providers were being removed in connection with more than 5,000 drivers who later failed English-language-proficiency requirements.

A broader investigation found unlicensed instructors, missing training records, inadequate facilities and even a provider claiming a school bus behind a trailer was its classroom.

The schools didn't issue the CDLs.

STATE LICENSING AGENCIES DID.

The schools supplied training certifications; states accepted the underlying records and printed the licenses.

DOT says its broader enforcement campaign has resulted in states cancelling tens of thousands of improperly issued licenses involving foreign drivers.

This is not evidence of illegal voting.
BUT, IT IS CONCRETE EVIDENCE THE SYSTEM IS NOT SECURE.

It demonstrates the principle relevant to Pennsylvania:

A REAL GOVERNMENT LICENSE DOES NOT GUARANTEE THAT THE ELIGIBILITY DETERMINATION BEHIND IT WAS CORRECT.

That is exactly why voter eligibility must be independently verified rather than inferred from possession of government identification.

ONCE SOMEBODY REACHES THE VOTER ROLL

This is where Pennsylvania's ordinary election audits answer the wrong question for this particular vulnerability.

A risk-limiting audit can establish that machines accurately counted sampled paper ballots.

But a machine can accurately count a ballot cast by an ineligible person.

One question is:

Was the ballot counted correctly?

The other is:

Was the person eligible to cast it?

Pennsylvania needs both audits.

JUNE 27, 2026: WASHINGTON AND PENNSYLVANIA FIGHT OVER THE FILE

The Trump Justice Department sought Pennsylvania voter-registration information.

Pennsylvania resisted.

DOJ sued.

On June 27, 2026, Chief U.S. District Judge Cathy Bissoon dismissed the Pennsylvania case.

The ruling addressed what information Washington was legally entitled to obtain under the statutes it invoked.

It did not establish that every Pennsylvania registrant was eligible.

If unrestricted disclosure raises legitimate privacy concerns, there is an obvious alternative:

CONDUCT A CONTROLLED INDEPENDENT ELIGIBILITY AUDIT.

Securely reconcile:

authoritative citizenship/immigration records → PennDOT classification → voter registration → voter participation history.

Protect people's personal information.

Publish aggregate results.

That would settle the question with evidence rather than political assurances.

THEN COMES SHAPIRO'S SECOND SYSTEM: PUBLIC HEALTH

There is another reason Pennsylvania's 2026 election deserves unusual scrutiny.

Shapiro's administration is simultaneously seeking broader permanent public-health authority.

And medicine is familiar territory to the governor.

His father, Dr. Steven Shapiro, founded Pediatric Medical Associates.

Josh Shapiro has said he entered college intending to become a pediatrician like his father.

At Children's Hospital of Philadelphia on October 1, 2025, Shapiro said Pennsylvania vaccine manufacturing supported approximately 4,700 jobs and $4.74 billion in economic activity.

Then he said:

“IT'S ALSO BIG BUSINESS FOR US HERE IN THIS COMMONWEALTH.”

That does not establish wrongdoing.

It establishes that Shapiro understands both the medical and economic importance of vaccination policy.

Then came Chapter 27.

JUNE 4–AUGUST 8, 2026: CHAPTER 27

On June 4, Shapiro's Department of Health submitted proposed Chapter 27 Regulation 10-242.

It was published August 8.

The proposed rewrite expands Pennsylvania's disease-control framework toward the:

“PREVENTION, CONTAINMENT, OR MITIGATION”

of diseases, infections and broadly defined health conditions.

It includes provisions concerning investigations, schools, health information, susceptible individuals and vaccine reporting.

This comes five years after Pennsylvania voters restricted gubernatorial emergency authority during the COVID era.

In May 2021, voters amended Pennsylvania's Constitution.

Later that year, Pennsylvania's Supreme Court struck down the statewide school-mask order because the Department of Health exceeded its existing regulatory authority.

Now the regulatory framework itself is being rewritten.

AUGUST 25: THE MEASLES HEADLINE

Pennsylvania's 2026 measles outbreak is real.

On August 25, however, Shapiro's administration announced Pennsylvania's first two “measles-associated deaths” in 35 years.

Then came an important qualification.

Lancaster County Coroner Stephen Diamantoni said a newborn had tested positive for measles but died from a lacerated spleen, and the forensic pathologist did not believe measles caused the death.

Pennsylvania subsequently explained that “measles-associated” can include a death in which measles was present without being determined the immediate cause.

That doesn't establish a fabricated outbreak.

It demonstrates something important during an election season:

THE HEADLINE ARRIVES BEFORE THE QUALIFICATION.

Fear changes behavior.

And that brings us back to mail voting.

WHERE THE TWO SYSTEMS CONVERGE

Government doesn't have to close Pennsylvania's polling places to change voting behavior.

Imagine an October health escalation.

Cases rise.

Schools react.

Hospitals issue warnings.

Government recommends caution.

Television amplifies the threat.

Nobody has to say:

DON'T VOTE IN PERSON.

The atmosphere merely has to say:

AVOID CROWDS.

Pennsylvania already offers the alternative:

VOTE FROM HOME.

And in 2020, Democratic voters used that channel almost three-to-one over Republicans.

That doesn't prove Chapter 27 is an election scheme.

It demonstrates why extraordinary public-health powers in the hands of an incumbent government deserve safeguards when those powers could influence the conditions under which people choose how to vote.

THE ENTIRE QUESTION IN ONE CHAIN

The history now fits on a few lines:

1993 — Clinton: Motor Voter connects DMV transactions to voter registration.

2013–2019 — Democratic states: driver's-license access expands to unauthorized residents in states including California, New York and New Jersey.

2015 forward: automatic voter registration begins replacing affirmative opt-in with opt-out registration for eligible customers.

2019 — Wolf: Pennsylvania establishes no-excuse mail voting.

2021–2024 — Biden: extraordinary migration surge; qualifying noncitizens increasingly possess federal immigration documents, work authorization and SSNs.

September 19, 2023 — Shapiro: PennDOT registration becomes automatic opt-out for eligible customers.

April 17, 2026 — DeFoor: Pennsylvania audit demonstrates that erroneous noncitizen data can defeat the PennDOT registration safeguard.

June–August 2026 — Shapiro: Chapter 27 seeks broader permanent public-health authority.

August 25: the “measles-associated deaths” controversy demonstrates how quickly health messaging can influence public perception.

November 3: Pennsylvania votes.

None of that establishes that every stage was centrally designed as one election scheme.

But the systems now touch.

And when systems touch, safeguards must touch too.

WHAT PENNSYLVANIA SHOULD DO BEFORE NOVEMBER

Don't argue about whether Josh Shapiro is trustworthy.

Build a system that doesn't require trusting him.

Conduct an independent voter-eligibility audit.

Make missing or inconsistent citizenship information a hard stop for automatic voter registration.

Audit eligibility separately from ballot tabulation.

Require independent substantiation for extraordinary election-season public-health claims.

Put legislative and constitutional limits around Chapter 27.

And prevent extraordinary public-health authority from administratively changing election procedures.

If Pennsylvania's voter rolls are clean, the eligibility audit will prove it.

If they're not, Pennsylvania needs to know before the ballots are counted.

DON'T TELL PENNSYLVANIA TO TRUST THE SYSTEM.
SHOW PENNSYLVANIA THE AUDIT.

text:
Public education in the Soviet Union, Randi Weingarten’s dream

The Soviet Union’s public education system was built to serve two purposes: mass production of literate, ideologically reliable industrial labor, and the formation of a loyal administrative and technical elite (Nomenklatura).

In December 1919, Vladimir Lenin issued a decree that made literacy compulsory for everyone aged 8–50. Called the “Likbez” campaign (liquidation of illiteracy) it set up tens of thousands of literacy points in factories, villages, and army units. By the 1939 census, literacy among those aged 9–49 had reached about 87–89 percent (higher in cities, lower in the countryside). 

Most working-class youth were steered into vocational tracks: factory apprenticeship schools (FZU), tekhnikums, and evening or correspondence courses that kept them in production.

By the early 1930s 5)3 Bolshevik inspired “cultural revolution” reversed this with a massive campaign: workers and party members were pushed into higher education through rabfaks (workers’ faculties) so the regime could create its own “proletarian intelligentsia.” By the mid-1930s that experiment was scaled back due to lack of motivation.

By 1958 Khrushchev himself complained that only 30–40 percent of students at Moscow higher-education institutions came from worker or collective-farm families; the rest came from the intelligentsia and white-collar employees. 

Curriculum for ordinary schools mixed basic literacy and numeracy  - along with heavy doses of Marxism-Leninism, Soviet patriotism, atheism, and later - “scientific communism.” Several youth  organizations reinforced this as well, and it continued in the military, where men were conscripted for two years, and ran by the KGB (Putin was part of this cadre but not directly involved in admjnistering “propaganda talks” as far as I know). 

Of course, like with grocery availability and medical availability, the party elite Bolsheviks had a separate, but parallel, higher-quality channels for the children of officials, managers, and the urban intelligentsia. Specialized schools were the most visible of these. Language schools (especially English), physics-mathematics schools, and schools for music, arts, and sports offered stronger teaching staff, better facilities, exemption from factory labor, and a clear advantage in university admissions. The four boarding “phys-math” schools were attached to major universities (Moscow, Leningrad, Kiev, Novosibirsk) were the most famous of them. Selection was “on paper” by olympiads and exams, but location in the capital cities and parental connections (Bolsheviks) heavily favored those applicants . 

Ordinary working-class district schools were widely regarded as inferior.

Those four adult cadres the communist party ran on its own closed system. The Higher Party School under the Central Committee trained mid- and high-level officials in ideology, party history, propaganda, and administration. 

Again - admission was by nomination and political vetting, not open competition. Living conditions were comfortable, and the school functioned as a networking institution. A substantial fraction of regional first secretaries and Central Committee apparatus members passed through it. Earlier institutions such as Sverdlov Communist University and the Institute of Red Professors served the same function in the 1920’s.

• 2025–2026 — Trump pressured the Federal Reserve for lower rates and tried to remove Governor Lisa Cook after disputed mortgage allegations.

• 2025–2026 — The administration restricted Associated Press access over terminology while escalating lawsuits, license threats, regulatory pressure and investigations against news organizations.

• 2025–2026 — Grocery bills, energy costs, health costs, rent, insurance, and basic survival all crushing average Americans.

• 2025–2026 — Family business conflicts, crypto wealth, foreign ties, watchdog attacks, prosecutor pressure, retaliation allegations and court defeats — MORE presidential power with LESS oversight.

• November 2025 — After Trump pressured authorities against James Comey and Letitia James, a judge dismissed their prosecutions because the Trump-backed prosecutor was unlawfully appointed. Dismissals were without prejudice.

• September 2025 — A federal court found Trump unlawfully fired inspectors general without complying with the Inspector General Act.

• June 2025 — Trump deployed the National Guard to Los Angeles over California’s objections during immigration-raid protests, escalating disputes over military power, federalism and domestic enforcement.

• May 2025 — The administration accepted a Qatar-provided Boeing 747-8 for possible Air Force One use, raising ethics, security and foreign-influence concerns. Qatar denied seeking influence.

• April 2025 — Trump imposed sweeping tariffs through emergency powers, bypassing ordinary congressional processes and creating uncertainty for prices, businesses and trade.

• April 2025 — The administration terminated about $2.2 billion in Harvard research funding; a federal judge later ruled the cuts unlawful.

• March 2025 — Senior national-security officials discussed an imminent Yemen strike on Signal and accidentally included Atlantic editor Jeffrey Goldberg, exposing operational timing and strike details.

• March 2025 — Trump issued orders targeting law firms tied to critics, opponents and disfavored clients; judges blocked multiple orders as retaliatory or unconstitutional threats to legal independence.

• March 2025 — Other major firms negotiated with the White House, pledging hundreds of millions in pro bono work on administration-approved causes rather than risk similar retaliation.

• March 2025 — The government wrongfully deported Kilmar Ábrego García to El Salvador despite legal protection, then was ordered to facilitate his return.

• March 2025 — Trump used the Alien Enemies Act against alleged gang members, triggering litigation over removals without a meaningful chance to contest government accusations.

• February 2025 — DOJ ordered prosecutors to drop Mayor Eric Adams’ corruption case while citing his help with immigration enforcement. Senior prosecutors resigned; Trump denied directing the dismissal.

• January 24, 2025 — Trump abruptly fired inspectors general across major agencies. A judge later found eight removals violated federal notice and justification requirements.

• January 20, 2025 — Trump tried to end birthright citizenship by executive order, triggering repeated court blocks over whether a president can rewrite the 14th Amendment without Congress or an amendment.

THE TRUMP RECEIPTS (updated daily)
The running record of Trump 2.0 that America cannot afford to forget.

• August 31, 2026 — Treasury blocks major news organizations from G20 coverage: Treasury denied reporters from The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg credentials without publicly explaining why. The denials are established; viewpoint retaliation is not.

• August 30–31, 2026 — Iran fighting resumed as Trump posted an unsupported AI-generated attack video: U.S. forces struck Iranian launchers, Iran retaliated toward U.S. bases, and Trump posted a synthetic video claiming Kharg Island was being destroyed without corroborating evidence.

• August 30, 2026 — The administration deported dozens to the Central African Republic, including an Afghan man protected from removal to Afghanistan over Taliban threats. The removal is established; whether using a third country violated his rights remains unresolved.

• August 30, 2026 — Venezuela announced a 25-year U.S. oil deal covering 17 fields and targeting 1.5 million barrels daily. Trump claims U.S. partnerships gained majority control; Venezuela says it retains ownership. Corruption is not established.

• August 30, 2026 — Trump demanded FCC “punishment” of NBC’s Kristen Welker after she called his endorsement results mixed. The demand is documented; no FCC penalty or legal finding followed.

• August 29, 2026 — Administration escalates unsupported noncitizen-voting claims ahead of the midterms: DHS asserted without public evidence that up to 250,000 noncitizens may be on four states’ rolls. Experts say such voting is extremely rare and warn the method may produce false positives.

• August 29, 2026 — Trump imposed 50% tariffs on about $20 billion in Canadian imports under an untested Depression-era law after losing on his earlier tariff authority. Canada retaliated; the new legal theory remains unadjudicated.

• August 29, 2026 — DHS used a customs statute to obtain six months of journalist Georgia Fort’s phone records and seek data involving journalists, nonprofits and unions without prior judicial approval. The demands are documented; legality is unresolved.

• August 28, 2026 — A federal judge ruled that using immigration law to revoke visas or pursue deportation over pro-Palestinian advocacy or criticism of Israel violated the First and Fifth Amendments.

• August 28, 2026 — Regulators found White House teleprompter operator Gabriel Perez used advance access to Trump speeches for prediction-market trades; he must forfeit over $107,000, pay $65,000 and accept a three-year ban.

• August 28, 2026 — A judge rejected Trump’s effort to move his New York hush-money case to federal court, ruling the Stormy Daniels concealment was private conduct, not a presidential duty; his 34 felony convictions remain on appeal.

Legal protections for SpaceX aren’t the problem. Lack of transparency is. Before we celebrated, Louisiana should have negotiated water baselines, debris modeling, liability assignment, cumulative impact studies, and public disclosure of environmental assessments.

Instead we got sealed terms and a deal built on desperation.

We have 6,400 orphaned oil wells and a $1 billion cleanup bill from the last industrial boom. That’s the precedent. Not to mention we held all the cards. No one else has what we offered. 

So when we give SpaceX legal shields without baseline environmental documentation or liability terms, we’re not building economic strength. 

We’re setting up the next bill our grandchildren will pay.

text:
The Voice in the Basement: Lindsay Clancy, Three Dead Children, and a Jury Still Deciding

Lindsay Clancy did not walk into a Massachusetts courtroom to argue that someone else killed her children. She walked in, paralyzed and in a wheelchair, after a five-week trial in which her own lawyers conceded the physical act. On January 24, 2023, the former labor and delivery nurse strangled five-year-old Cora, three-year-old Dawson, and eight-month-old Callan with exercise bands in the basement of the family’s Duxbury home, then cut her wrists and neck and jumped from a second-story window. The jump left her paralyzed from the waist down. Callan died days later. The fight in Plymouth Superior Court has never been about whether those deaths happened at her hands. It has been about whether a mother in the grip of postpartum mental illness still possessed the legal capacity to be a murderer.
Prosecutors built their case on sequence that looks like planning. Clancy sent her husband, Patrick, out for takeout and medicine, creating a short window alone in the house. She locked a door. She chose a quiet method. She searched driving times and pharmacy details on her phone. The day before the killings, psychiatrist Jennifer Tufts saw her virtually and later testified that Clancy denied homicidal thoughts and did not appear psychotic. Treating clinicians, including Tufts and psychiatric nurse practitioner Rebecca Jollotta, said they never observed psychosis. Prosecution experts Kirk Heilbrun and Gregory Saathoff told jurors the claimed command hallucination was too tidy to be typical: a single male voice that arrived, ordered the killings, then stopped when the children were dead. Heilbrun offered another theory that still holds her responsible. He said she was suicidal and killed the children so they would not suffer after she was gone, an act some forensic psychiatrists call altruistic filicide. Under Massachusetts law, first-degree murder can rest on deliberate premeditation or on extreme atrocity and cruelty. Either path, if the jury accepts it, means life without parole.
The defense answered with a different chain of cause. After Callan’s birth in May 2022, Clancy’s sleep collapsed, her weight dropped, and she cycled through more than a dozen psychiatric medications in a few months. She called suicide hotlines, went to emergency rooms, entered a day program at Women and Infants Hospital in Rhode Island, and spent early January 2023 as an inpatient at McLean Hospital. Family members described a woman terrified she was losing her mind and terrified the state would take her children if she said too much. Forensic psychiatrist Phillip Resnick testified she was “clearly psychotic” that day, “almost like she was a puppet.” Psychologist Paul Zeizel, who spent dozens of hours with her after the deaths, said she had no appreciation of the wrongfulness of the act. A hospital chaplain later recounted Clancy describing a commanding voice that told her the children would not be safe unless she obeyed. Phone searches for schizophrenia, hallucinations, and psychosis before the killings cut both ways. Prosecutors treat them as research for a cover story. The defense treats them as a nurse documenting her own unraveling.
